question: Can guests cancel their tickets for a Wix event themselves?
answer:
Currently, guests cannot cancel their participation in a ticketed event themselves. They need to contact you so you can [remove them from the guest list](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-events-managing-ticket-orders). If your guest bought an event ticket, you'll need to [provide a refund](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-events-canceling-and-refunding-orders-for-events-with-tickets#step-3-refund-guests). 

**Tip:** Guests can, however, cancel their participation in RSVP events. They can do so through their Members Area.

question: How can I start building a website with Wix?
answer:
Prerequisites: Create a free Wix account.

To start building a website with Wix, follow these steps:

1. **Choose a Template:** Wix offers [800+ website templates](https://www.wix.com/website/templates) to help get you started on your website creation journey. Each of these templates has been carefully researched and curated by our own designers, to make sure they best fit current trends and industry needs.

2. **Customize Your Template:** All of our templates are fully customizable, meaning you can change them up as much as you want. Play with the design and layout, update and remove content, and add apps until you transform the template into a site that fits your style and business needs. Customize anything with intuitive drag and drop technology to look exactly the way you want. Make your website stand out with design features like media galleries, video backgrounds, parallax scroll, animation, and more.

3. **Start from Scratch (Optional):** If you don't want to use a template and have something very specific in mind, you can start from a [blank canvas](https://www.wix.com/website/templates/html/blank).

For agencies building sites for clients, consider using [Wix Studio](https://www.wix.com/studio) for an end-to-end solution that includes smart design capabilities and flexible dev tools.

articles.title: Getting Started with Wix
articles.html_content:
Welcome to Wix - you’ve come to the right place. Whether you're a business owner, a creative professional, or someone looking to establish an online presence, Wix offers an intuitive website builder that empowers you to bring your vision to life.
We offer so much more than just a beautiful website. Manage your entire business from your Wix account, including your contacts, products, services and sales. Promote your business using business emails, social posts and stay up-to-date with your site's analytics.
Follow the steps below to get started on your Wix journey.

Step 1 | Create a free account

Wix is 100% free to sign up. You can create a fully functioning website and manage your business without needing to pay a cent. You can also create as many sites as you want in one Wix account. Learn more about building a site for free.

After you've created your site and set up your business, you can decide if you want to upgrade to make use of Wix's Premium features, such as connecting a domain, removing Wix ads and more.
Sign up to create a free Wix account.

Step 2 | Build your site

Wix offers 800+ website templates to help get you started on your website creation journey. Each of these templates have been carefully researched and curated by our own designers, to make sure they best fit current trends and industry needs.

All of our templates are fully customizable, meaning you can change them up as much as you want. Play with the design and layout, update and remove content, and add apps until you transform the template into a site that fits your style and business needs.
Customize anything with intuitive drag and drop technology to look exactly the way you want. Make your website stand out with design features like media galleries, video backgrounds, parallax scroll, animation and more.
If you don't want to use a template and have something very specific in mind, you can start from a blank canvas.
Building sites for clients?
If you're an agency, head to Wix Studio. Wix Studio is the ultimate, end-to-end solution that includes smart design capabilities and flexible dev tools that let you deliver exceptional results for clients in any industry. It also includes a range of fully responsive and beautiful templates.

Step 3 | Set up your business

With Wix, you have the freedom to create a website that perfectly fits your needs. We offer over 250 apps and services you can add to your website. 

Sell products with an online store, provide services and take bookings, share your thoughts on a blog, showcase your work with a beautiful portfolio, and much more. Our solutions are built not only for a variety of industries, but also for businesses of all sizes, from a personal brand to an enterprise corporation.
Looking for a specific business type?
Go ahead and explore Wix's Business Solutions.

Step 4 | Choose a Premium plan

You can use Wix completely for free. However, you might want to upgrade your site with a Premium plan to access premium features including:
  • Connecting your own domain
  • Removing Wix ads
  • Accepting payments
  • Additional storage and bandwidth
  • Google Analytics
  • Premium support
Compare our Premium plans and their features
Tip:
Don't worry about committing to a plan. You can change plans or cancel a plan at any time. You can also assign a plan to another site in your Wix account. Learn more about upgrading your site.

Step 5 | (Optional) Set up payments

Accept payments for goods or services directly through your site. Wix offers different payment methods and providers depending on your location. 

Connect Wix Payments to manage your entire business, payments and payouts right from your dashboard. If Wix Payments isn’t available in your region, or you’d like to connect a different payment provider, select from 70+ payment options offered on Wix worldwide. In most countries, you can select one or more of Credit Card, PayPal and Manual payments to appear on your checkout page. This gives your customers more ways to pay. 
Depending on the availability and choice of your payment provider, you may also offer alternative options to your customers such as Apple Pay, cryptocurrency payments, recurring payments, BNPL (buy now, pay later) payments, Point of Sale, payments for CBD products, and more. 
Ready to start accepting payments on your site?
Explore the payment options for your site.

Step 6 | Manage and grow your business

Once your site is all set up, its time to grow your business. Wix has tons of solutions to help you promote and expand, and to help you reach the right audience:

  • Complete SEO solution: Optimize your site for search engines by using Wix's SEO tools. This will help increase your website's visibility online.
  • AI-driven Facebook and Instagram ads: Create a dynamic ad campaign on Facebook and Instagram with Facebook Ads with Wix. Take advantage of Wix's Smart Algorithm that continually optimizes and tests your campaign so you get the best possible results.
  • Integrate marketing tools: Use Wix's suite of marketing tools, to engage with your audience through email campaigns, social media, and more.
  • Monitor analytics: Keep track of your website's performance using Wix Analytics. Understand your audience, track site traffic, and make informed decisions to drive growth.
Manage your business like a pro:
Stay up-to-date while on the go, with the Wix app. Manage all aspects of your business and communicate with your members, right from your mobile device.

View tons of articles and helpful information in the Wix Help Center to find everything you need. You can also read our blog post and discover our 11-step guide to building a website from scratch.

Absolutely. Wix is for everyone and makes it possible to create a high-quality website without knowing how to code. question: How can I create a custom image for social media using the Wix app?
answer:
To create a custom image for social media using the Wix app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
2. Tap **Manage** ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8769cf44-f342-494c-b25f-cc98c9da3e82/2021/04/12/3fc0f98c-0997-47b3-b7bd-6ae31a67e078/ce9c0fe5-f60d-4448-8fc2-9ba4cf636f93.png) at the bottom.
3. Tap **Marketing** and select **Social Posts**.
4. Tap any template to get started.
5. Customize your post using the available options:
   
   * **Overlay:** Tap the **Overlay** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8696077d-830a-4b1e-bd86-9df98f89994a/2019/08/07/e8c5ad3f-3c07-48ea-8e43-af60a2abde35/5451621f-bd41-4808-9220-9a216a93b1cc.png) to pick a different overlay with preset text and stickers.
   * **Text:** Add your custom text to the post:
     
     1. Tap the **Text** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8696077d-830a-4b1e-bd86-9df98f89994a/2019/08/07/63c731f7-e4a3-4a80-87f0-3afe77ae963d/3219f8a1-6c70-4665-a475-70cf1fc1c314.png) from the bottom menu.
     2. Tap **Add Text**.
     3. Edit your social post text and tap **Done** at the top right.
     4. (Optional) Customize your text using the available options and tap **Done**.
   * **Stickers:** Tap the **Sticker** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8696077d-830a-4b1e-bd86-9df98f89994a/2019/08/07/f6dc429d-e149-46cc-8103-906dd7c63e79/b4396379-dbc6-4466-af21-65c84c5a079d.png) to add new stickers to your post.
   * **Images:** Tap the **Image** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8696077d-830a-4b1e-bd86-9df98f89994a/2019/08/07/0f5c039d-18cb-4dc9-b83d-02684cbf25a6/c0fb21ea-3a4a-4d77-9704-b8b0bca5760d.png) to add images from your site uploads or your phone.
6. When you're done, share your post by tapping **Share** at the top right. Select where you want to share:
   
   * **Facebook:** Share the post to your Facebook business page. Follow the on-screen instructions to connect to the relevant page.
   * **Instagram:** Share the post to your Instagram feed or story.
   * **Save Image:** Save the post as an image in your mobile device.
   * **More:** Share your post to any of the available apps in the menu.

articles.contents:
Social Media Marketing: Creating and Publishing Your Social Posts
Social posts are a great way to engage with your audience. Create images and videos that give exciting updates about your business, promoting awareness and driving traffic to your site. When you're ready, publish the content you created straight from the dashboard.In this article, learn more about:
Creating an image to share on social media Creating a video to share on social media Publishing social posts Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Creating an image to share on social mediaCreate custom images for your social media posts using Wix. Ensure your visuals are unique and aligned with your brand identity. There are helpful templates or you can start from scratch, adding text, symbols, media and more.To create an image with Wix:DashboardWix app
Go to Social Media Marketing in your site's dashboard. Click Quick Actions on the top right. Click Create image with Wix. Select an option from the settings on the left to begin customizing your post:
    
Template: Select a template to customize. Palette: Select a pre-made palette of colors that are designed to look well together.
Tip: The colors can be changed and adjusted if you need specific colors. Text: Select from the suggested fonts or add your own.  Symbols: Add your business' logo to make your social post look like your own. Or choose from a selection of pre-made icons and symbols to add to your post.  Shapes: Add shapes to your post. You can even build them on top of each other to make a truly unique design.  Images: Upload your own image or choose from the library of pre-existing ones.  Background: Select a background color for your post.    Choose what you want to do:
    
Back to Social Media Marketing: Save the image to the Your Social Posts tab in your Social Media Marketing dashboard. Publish: Share your image on social media.  
Go to your site in the Wix app.﻿ Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Marketing and select Social Posts.  Tap any template to get started.  Customize your post using the available options:
    
Overlay: Tap the Overlay icon  to pick a different overlay with preset text and stickers.  Text: Add your custom text to the post:
        
Tap the Text icon  from the bottom menu. Tap Add Text. Edit your social post text and tap Done at the top right. (Optional) Customize your text using the available options and tap Done.   Stickers: Tap the Sticker icon   to add new stickers to your post.  Images: Tap the Image icon  to add images from your site uploads or your phone.   When you're done, share your post by tapping Share at the top right. Select where you want to share:
    
Facebook: Share the post to your Facebook business page. Follow the on-screen instructions to connect to the relevant page. Instagram: Share the post to your Instagram feed or story.  Save Image: Save the post as an image in your mobile device.  More: Share your post to any of the available apps in the menu.   Creating a video to share on social mediaCreate high-quality, unique videos for your social media. Tailor your content to fit your brand identity by customizing text, style, colors, music, and more. Choose from a variety of templates or start from scratch, giving you full creative control to craft videos that stand out and engage your audience..To create a video:DashboardWix app
Go to Social Media Marketing in your site's dashboard. Click Quick Actions at the top right. Choose Create video with Vimeo. Choose how to create your video.Wix Video Maker
Add the video content and text:
    
Click the Add icon  under Add Photos and Videos.  Select the photos or videos you want to add and click Add to Video.  Enter the text for your video:
        
Opening Text: Use it to introduce the concept of the video. Second Text: Use it to explain more about the concept. Third Text: We recommend making this a call-to-action to explain what you would like the viewers to do, such as "Visit Our Store". Closing Text: We recommend entering your URL or contact details so your viewers know how to find you.     Click Next. Customize the design of your video:
    
Choose a Video Style: Select the style of your video. Hover over the styles to preview them. Choose a Layout: Choose the video layout: Horizontal, Vertical, or Square Choose Colors and Font: Click the color boxes to set the colors and use the drop-down to choose the text font.   Click Next.  Select the music track for your video. Click the tracks to listen to a preview. Tip: Alternatively, disable the Music On toggle if you do not want to play a track. Click Next.  Click the Include Business Info toggle to show or hide your business info. Note: Logos must be 48x48 pixels in order to be rendered properly. Click Apply & Preview. Choose to Save & Share or go Back to Editing.Vimeo CreateThis option will only appear after you have created several videos in the Wix video maker. 
Click Start from Scratch or select a template and click Customize.  Use the available options to create your video: 
    
New Scene: Add more scenes to your video.  Media: Select or upload images or videos. Presets: Add a pre-designed scene to your video. Text: Add text to a scene. Graphics: Add decorative elements to a scene (e.g. Shapes, Frames, Gradients).  Music: Select or upload music to your video. Palette: Switch the color theme of your video.    Click Preview or Save. Click Save to Wix.
Tip: You can also click edit to go back and make changes.  Choose to Download File or Share. 
Go to your site in the Wix app. Tap Manage  at the bottom. Tap Marketing and select Video Maker. Tap Get Started. Choose a template from the available options or tap Start from Scratch to create a video without a template. (If you selected a template) Tap Customize Video. Tap Add Media to add images or video clips to your video. Tap Next and add titles to your video:
    
Opening Text: Use it to introduce the concept of the video. Second Text: Use it to explain more about the concept. Third Text: We recommend making this a call-to-action to explain what you would like the viewers to do, such as "Visit Our Store". Closing Text: We recommend entering your URL or contact details so your viewers know how to find you. Include Business Info: Tap the toggle to show or hide your business info.
Note: Logos must be 48x48 pixels in order to be rendered properly.   Tap Next and choose from the following options: 
    
Choose a Video Style: Play the different style options and select one for your video. Choose a Layout: Choose between Square, Landscape and Portrait. Choose Colors and Font: Select the primary color, secondary colors and font.  Font: Select the font style used on your video.   Tap Next and choose a music track for your video, or select No Music. Tap Next.  Tap an option to choose what you want to do:
    
Customize: Make changes to the video. Save Video: Save the video to your Media Manager. Choose an option:
        
Share: Share your video with others. Download: Save the file to your device.     Tap Done.Avoid video copyright issues:Downloading and uploading the video manually will not protect you from copyright. The best way to avoid any copyright issues is to make sure that you share your video using the Share feature described in this article. Wix works with Magisto to ensure that any videos created with Wix Video Maker are whitelisted. This releases any copyright and monetization claims from the file. Publishing your social postsPublish your social posts to get them seen by your audience. You can edit previously saved designs before sharing, and customize each post's caption accordingly.Important:You can publish up to 10 social posts a month or you can upgrade to publish more.To publish a post: 
Go to Social Media Marketing in your site's dashboard. Click Your Social Posts at the top. Hover over the post you want to publish and click the More Actions icon . Click Preview & Publish.
Tip: Click Download to save your post to your computer. (If you haven't yet) Connect the social accounts you want to publish to. Customize how your social post will appear on each social channel:
Note: The options vary depending on which social accounts you connect.

articles.title: Social Media Marketing: Creating and Publishing Your Social Posts
articles.html_content:
Social posts are a great way to engage with your audience. Create images and videos that give exciting updates about your business, promoting awareness and driving traffic to your site. When you're ready, publish the content you created straight from the dashboard.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Creating an image to share on social media
  • Creating a video to share on social media
  • Publishing social posts
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

Creating an image to share on social media

Create custom images for your social media posts using Wix. Ensure your visuals are unique and aligned with your brand identity. There are helpful templates or you can start from scratch, adding text, symbols, media and more.

To create an image with Wix:

Dashboard
Wix app
  1. Go to Social Media Marketing in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Quick Actions on the top right.
  3. Click Create image with Wix.
  4. Select an option from the settings on the left to begin customizing your post:
    • Template: Select a template to customize.
    • Palette: Select a pre-made palette of colors that are designed to look well together.
      Tip: The colors can be changed and adjusted if you need specific colors.
    • Text: Select from the suggested fonts or add your own. 
    • Symbols: Add your business' logo to make your social post look like your own. Or choose from a selection of pre-made icons and symbols to add to your post. 
    • Shapes: Add shapes to your post. You can even build them on top of each other to make a truly unique design. 
    • Images: Upload your own image or choose from the library of pre-existing ones. 
    • Background: Select a background color for your post. 
  5. Choose what you want to do:
    • Back to Social Media Marketing: Save the image to the Your Social Posts tab in your Social Media Marketing dashboard.
    • Publish: Share your image on social media.
  1. Go to your site in the Wix app.﻿
  2. Tap Manage  at the bottom.
  3. Tap Marketing and select Social Posts. 
  4. Tap any template to get started. 
  5. Customize your post using the available options:
    • Overlay: Tap the Overlay icon to pick a different overlay with preset text and stickers. 
    • Text: Add your custom text to the post:
      1. Tap the Text icon from the bottom menu.
      2. Tap Add Text.
      3. Edit your social post text and tap Done at the top right.
      4. (Optional) Customize your text using the available options and tap Done.
    • Stickers: Tap the Sticker icon  to add new stickers to your post. 
    • Images: Tap the Image icon to add images from your site uploads or your phone.
  6. When you're done, share your post by tapping Share at the top right. Select where you want to share:
    • Facebook: Share the post to your Facebook business page. Follow the on-screen instructions to connect to the relevant page.
    • Instagram: Share the post to your Instagram feed or story. 
    • Save Image: Save the post as an image in your mobile device. 
    • More: Share your post to any of the available apps in the menu. 

Creating a video to share on social media

Create high-quality, unique videos for your social media. Tailor your content to fit your brand identity by customizing text, style, colors, music, and more. Choose from a variety of templates or start from scratch, giving you full creative control to craft videos that stand out and engage your audience..

To create a video:

Dashboard
Wix app
  1. Go to Social Media Marketing in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Quick Actions at the top right.
  3. Choose Create video with Vimeo.
  4. Choose how to create your video.

Wix Video Maker

  1. Add the video content and text:
    1. Click the Add icon  under Add Photos and Videos. 
    2. Select the photos or videos you want to add and click Add to Video. 
    3. Enter the text for your video:
      • Opening Text: Use it to introduce the concept of the video.
      • Second Text: Use it to explain more about the concept.
      • Third Text: We recommend making this a call-to-action to explain what you would like the viewers to do, such as "Visit Our Store".
      • Closing Text: We recommend entering your URL or contact details so your viewers know how to find you.
  2. Click Next.
  3. Customize the design of your video:
    • Choose a Video Style: Select the style of your video. Hover over the styles to preview them.
    • Choose a Layout: Choose the video layout: Horizontal, Vertical, or Square
    • Choose Colors and Font: Click the color boxes to set the colors and use the drop-down to choose the text font.
  4. Click Next. 
  5. Select the music track for your video. Click the tracks to listen to a preview. Tip: Alternatively, disable the Music On toggle if you do not want to play a track.
  6. Click Next. 
  7. Click the Include Business Info toggle to show or hide your business info. Note: Logos must be 48x48 pixels in order to be rendered properly.
  8. Click Apply & Preview.
  9. Choose to Save & Share or go Back to Editing.

Vimeo Create

This option will only appear after you have created several videos in the Wix video maker. 
  1. Click Start from Scratch or select a template and click Customize. 
  2. Use the available options to create your video: 
    • New Scene: Add more scenes to your video. 
    • Media: Select or upload images or videos.
    • Presets: Add a pre-designed scene to your video.
    • Text: Add text to a scene.
    • Graphics: Add decorative elements to a scene (e.g. Shapes, Frames, Gradients). 
    • Music: Select or upload music to your video.
    • Palette: Switch the color theme of your video. 
  3. Click Preview or Save.
  4. Click Save to Wix.
    Tip: You can also click edit to go back and make changes. 
  5. Choose to Download File or Share. 
  1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
  2. Tap Manage  at the bottom.
  3. Tap Marketing and select Video Maker.
  4. Tap Get Started.
  5. Choose a template from the available options or tap Start from Scratch to create a video without a template.
  6. (If you selected a template) Tap Customize Video.
  7. Tap Add Media to add images or video clips to your video.
  8. Tap Next and add titles to your video:
    • Opening Text: Use it to introduce the concept of the video.
    • Second Text: Use it to explain more about the concept.
    • Third Text: We recommend making this a call-to-action to explain what you would like the viewers to do, such as "Visit Our Store".
    • Closing Text: We recommend entering your URL or contact details so your viewers know how to find you.
    • Include Business Info: Tap the toggle to show or hide your business info.
      Note: Logos must be 48x48 pixels in order to be rendered properly.
  9. Tap Next and choose from the following options: 
    • Choose a Video Style: Play the different style options and select one for your video.
    • Choose a Layout: Choose between Square, Landscape and Portrait.
    • Choose Colors and Font: Select the primary color, secondary colors and font. 
    • Font: Select the font style used on your video.
  10. Tap Next and choose a music track for your video, or select No Music.
  11. Tap Next. 
  12. Tap an option to choose what you want to do:
    • Customize: Make changes to the video.
    • Save Video: Save the video to your Media Manager. Choose an option:
      • Share: Share your video with others.
      • Download: Save the file to your device.
  13. Tap Done.
Avoid video copyright issues:
Downloading and uploading the video manually will not protect you from copyright. The best way to avoid any copyright issues is to make sure that you share your video using the Share feature described in this article. Wix works with Magisto to ensure that any videos created with Wix Video Maker are whitelisted. This releases any copyright and monetization claims from the file.

Publishing your social posts

Publish your social posts to get them seen by your audience. You can edit previously saved designs before sharing, and customize each post's caption accordingly.
Important:
You can publish up to 10 social posts a month or you can upgrade to publish more.

To publish a post:

  1. Go to Social Media Marketing in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Your Social Posts at the top.
  3. Hover over the post you want to publish and click the More Actions icon .
  4. Click Preview & Publish.
    Tip: Click Download to save your post to your computer.
  5. (If you haven't yet) Connect the social accounts you want to publish to.
  6. Customize how your social post will appear on each social channel:
    Note: The options vary depending on which social accounts you connect. 
    • Publish as: If you're posting to Facebook and/or Instagram, choose whether you want to publish your image as a Post, Reel or Story.
    • Caption: Create a caption to add to your social post which will display to your audience.  Tip: Click Create AI Text to open the AI text creator menu. Enter a brief description of the content, select a tone of voice and click Create Text to generate a caption for your post.
    • Add Media: Add multiple media files to your post. 
    • Add Tracking Link: Include a link to your site so that when people click it, you can view the analytics of who came from your social post.
    • Hashtags: Add any hashtags you think are relevant to your post.
    • Media: Hover over the relevant media item and click the Replace media icon to swap out your image or video for another.
    • When do you want to publish?: Select Publish now or Schedule for later to choose when you want to publish.
  7. Click Publish at the bottom right.
    Note: The number next to Publish indicates how many posts you are about to publish. For example, if you have created both a Facebook and Instagram post, the number will show (2). 
Posting as a story?
  • This kind of post includes up to 5 images.
  • This option is not yet available to all Wix accounts.

FAQs

Click to learn more.

Can I add a specific caption for each platform that I publish to?

Yes, you can add a caption specific for each platform.

For example, if you've connected both your Instagram and Facebook accounts you will see two areas to add post content. You can write different captions or add different hashtags for each platform. 

Do I need a Vimeo account to create videos with Vimeo on Wix?

Yes, you will need to sign up for a Vimeo account in order to create videos using Vimeo in Wix.

Can I publish to multiple social media platforms at the same time?

Yes, make sure you have signed into all of your social accounts. You can then toggle on and off where you want the post to publish.

Note: YouTube will automatically toggle off if you are posting an image post. 

Can I edit my images and videos after saving them?

You can edit your videos from Your Social Posts in the dashboard. Hover over the relevant video and click Edit. 

Can I edit my post after publishing it?

If you need to edit your post's content after publishing you must do so from your social platforms.

Can I add an image or video that I created for a social post in my Wix site?

Yes, everything you create is saved to your site files in your editor you can add it to your page as you would add any other images or videos.

question: How can I track sales using the Thank You Page URL in Wix Stores?
answer:
To track sales using your Thank You Page URL in Wix Stores, follow these steps:

1. **Access Your Thank You Page URL**: The URL for your site's Thank You page is made of your domain name followed by: **/thank-you-page**. For example, if your site URL is **www.mystunningwebsite.com**, your Thank You page URL is **www.mystunningwebsite.com/thank-you-page**.

2. **Create a Rule in an External Tool**: Start by creating a rule to track Thank You Page visits using an external tool such as Google Analytics.

3. **Enter the URL Part**: Enter this part of the Thank You Page URL: **/thank-you-page** in the relevant tool to track visits.

### Note
If you have a conversion pixel, click [here](https://support.wix.com/en/article/connecting-your-facebook-pixel-to-your-wix-site) to learn how to add it to your site.

question: How can I fix the 'Missing field "description"' error in the Google Search Console Videos Tab?
answer: To fix the 'Missing field "description"' error in the Google Search Console Videos Tab, you need to add a description to your videos. This helps improve your site's Search Engine Optimization (SEO) by informing the search engine about the content of the video. You can learn how to add information to your videos by following this link: [add information to your videos here](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-information-to-your-videos). Addressing this issue will help improve your site's ranking on Google search results.

articles.contents:
Google Search Console: Missing Field "Description" Error in Videos Tab
Google Search Console is a handy tool for discovering errors on your website. To review the status of the videos on your site, go to the Google Search Console Videos Tab.
You may see the following error -  Missing field "description".  

To improve your site's Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Google requires you to add a description so that the Search Engine knows what the video is about. Learn how to add information to your videos here.
Following these steps will help your site's ranking on Google search results. 

Example: The Videos report shows a Search Console report for a Videos>Missing field 'description' error. If error message is red, this issue requires attention.

question: How do I connect Authorize.net Powered by Bankful as a payment provider on my Wix site?
answer:
To connect Authorize.net Powered by Bankful as a payment provider on your Wix site, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Accept Payments](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Set%20Up%20Payments&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7b%7bmetaSiteId%7d%7d/payments/) in your site's dashboard.

   **Tip:** Check your business location at the top right. If incorrect, click the drop-down menu to change it.

2. Click **See More Payment Options**.
3. Click **See Options** beside Third-Party Credit / Debit Card Providers.
4. Click **Connect** next to Authorize.net Powered by Bankful.
5. Depending on whether you are creating a new Bankful account, or have an existing account, follow the instructions:

   ### Have an account
   1. Enter your API Login ID and Transaction Key.
   2. Click **Connect**.

   ### Don't have an account
   1. Click [**Create Authorize.net Powered by Bankful account**](https://pinwheelpay.com/integration-pricing.php?page=Authorize.net&extSource=Wix-Authorize.net).
   2. Register for an Authorize.net Powered by Bankful merchant account and, once approved, retrieve your API Login ID and Transaction Key.
   3. Once your merchant account is approved, return to this window (repeat steps 1-5) and follow the steps under **Have an account** to connect your account.

Ensure that the currency used in your Wix account matches the currency in your Bankful account to avoid transaction declines. If you need to change the currency, refer to [how to change your currency](https://support.wix.com/en/article/setting-your-currency-for-accepting-payments).

How can I tell if a payment method is active?

In order to accept online payments, you must connect a payment provider. 
Once connected, your checkout will be active for your chosen payment method(s).

You need to have your account successfully verified to receive payouts.

Is my currency supported?

What is a minimum payment amount?

Do I need to upgrade my site to accept payments?

question: How can I prevent search engines from indexing a specific page on my Wix site?
answer:
To prevent search engines from indexing a specific page on your Wix site, follow these steps:

1. Click **Pages** ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/9dcc39dd-da6f-4c38-b1c3-ee79d33f39d5/2021/07/12/776143a2-f746-4083-84c1-5ed61e532ca8/9cd7bd5c-a62f-420f-a68a-1b7b1aabcdbc.png) on the left side of the Editor.
2. Click the More Actions icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/9dcc39dd-da6f-4c38-b1c3-ee79d33f39d5/2021/07/12/a364aab6-92d3-453b-953d-46566fa0f702/917c9124-75fa-4771-8e7a-8959a5d7906d.png) next to the relevant page.
3. Click **SEO Basics**.

If you want to let search engines index your page again, simply enable the **Let search engines index this page** toggle.

articles.contents:
Wix Editor: Preventing Search Engines from Indexing Your Page
By default, search engines like Google crawl and index every page on your live Wix site. If you don't want a specific page to appear in search results, you can prevent search engines from indexing it in your Editor. From your site's dashboard, you can also choose to prevent search engines from indexing your entire site or use your site's SEO Settings to prevent search engines from indexing groups of pages. Preventing search engines from indexing your entire site disables the options to prevent indexing groups of pages or individual pages. It also disables the option to prevent search engines from indexing those pages individually.Important:
Password protected pages and private member pages don't show in search results, as they are not crawled and indexed. However, you'll need to manually prevent search engines from indexing public member pages such as Followers and Profile. Pages that search engines are prevented from indexing may not appear in your sitemap.To prevent search engines from indexing a page:

articles.title: Wix Editor: Preventing Search Engines from Indexing Your Page
articles.html_content:
By default, search engines like Google crawl and index every page on your live Wix site. If you don't want a specific page to appear in search results, you can prevent search engines from indexing it in your Editor. 

From your site's dashboard, you can also choose to prevent search engines from indexing your entire site or use your site's SEO Settings to prevent search engines from indexing groups of pages. 
Preventing search engines from indexing your entire site disables the options to prevent indexing groups of pages or individual pages. It also disables the option to prevent search engines from indexing those pages individually.
Important:
  • Password protected pages and private member pages don't show in search results, as they are not crawled and indexed. However, you'll need to manually prevent search engines from indexing public member pages such as Followers and Profile.
  • Pages that search engines are prevented from indexing may not appear in your sitemap.

To prevent search engines from indexing a page:

  1. Click Pages  on the left side of the Editor.
  2. Click the More Actions icon  next to the relevant page.
  3. Click SEO Basics.
  4. Disable the Let search engines index this page toggle. 
Want to let search engines index your page again?
Enable the Let search engines index this page toggle to make the page visible to search engines again.

question: Can I have unique IDs for each widget instance when I add the same widget multiple times on a Wix site?
answer: Currently, when you install a blocks app on a site and add a widget to the canvas more than once, all instances of that widget will have the same **instanceId**. The **instanceId** is a property in the object returned by the [getDecodedAppInstance()](https://dev.wix.com/docs/velo/api-reference/wix-application/get-decoded-app-instance) in the [wix-application](https://dev.wix.com/docs/velo/api-reference/wix-application/introduction) module. This feature would allow you to distinguish between multiple widget instances on the same site.

question: How can I view the tracking codes on my website using Google Chrome?
answer:
To view the tracking codes on your website using Google Chrome, follow these steps:

1. Open the relevant page of your site in Google Chrome.
2. Open the developer tools:
   * **Windows:** Press the F12 key on your keyboard.
   * **Mac:** Press CMD + Option + I on your keyboard.
3. Click the More Actions icon at the top right.
4. Select **More tools**.
5. Select **Network conditions**.
6. Deselect **Use browser default** under **User Agent**.
7. Select **Googlebot** from the drop-down menu.
8. Close the **Network conditions** tab.
9. In the top tab, select **Network**.
10. Enter "/tags" in the filter field.
11. Refresh the page to see the active tracking codes.

question: Can I set a specific renewal date for recurring payments from my clients' pricing plans?
answer:
Currently, it is not possible for you to set a specific renewal date for recurring payments from your clients' pricing plans. Renewal dates are defined by the date clients purchase their plans or complete their free trial periods.

### Workarounds
Instead, you can [extend clients' plans](https://support.wix.com/en/article/pricing-plans-editing-an-existing-plan) (for subscriptions that already have an end date). You can also charge clients offline, or use a [Wix Invoice](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-invoices-creating-an-invoice) to cover the additional subscription time period.

question: How can I add Google AdSense ads to my blog posts in Wix Blog?
answer:
Prerequisites: Ensure you have a Google AdSense account and your site is verified. You also need to have a connected domain.

To add Google AdSense ads to your blog posts in Wix Blog, follow these steps:

### Step 1 | Create a Google AdSense account
1. Go to [Google AdSense](https://www.google.com/adsense).
2. Sign up for a new account.
3. Click **Sites** in the left sidebar.
4. Click **Add site**.
5. Enter the URL of your site.
6. Click **Save and continue**.

### Step 2 | Create an ad unit and generate an AdSense code
1. In Google AdSense, go to the **Ads** tab.
2. Click the **Ad Units** tab.
3. Select **Display ads under Create new ad unit**.
4. Enter a name for your ad in the field provided.
5. Click the Ad size drop-down at the top right and select **Fixed**.
6. Click **Create**.
7. Click **Copy code snippet** to copy the code.
8. Save the code for future use.

### Step 3 | Add the AdSense code to a blog post
1. [Go to Blog](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20My%20Blog&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D/blog) in your site's dashboard.
2. Select the blog post you want to edit, or click **Create a Post** to start writing a new post.
3. Click **Add** on the left.
4. Click **AdSense** under **From the web**.
5. Paste the AdSense code from your document under **Insert an ad from AdSense**.
6. Click **Save**.

**Notes:**
- It may take a few moments for the ad to appear in the post.
- To view the ad, make sure to disable any ad blockers you've installed on your browser.

question: How can I enable autoplay for my gallery in Wix Editor?
answer:
To enable autoplay for your gallery in Wix Editor, follow these steps:

1. Open the **Settings panel** for your gallery.
2. Look for the **Autoplays on loading** setting.
3. Enable this toggle so your gallery starts playing automatically, as soon as the page loads.
4. Control the time (in seconds) given to each image under **How long between images?**

This setting is available for the following galleries:
- Grid (Portrait)
- Slider (Arrows)
- Slider (Postcard)
- 3D Slideshow
- 3D Carousel
- Animated Slide

question: What should I do if I encounter an 'Unsupported MP4 format' error when uploading a video to Wix?
answer: If you encounter an 'Unsupported MP4 format' error when uploading your video file to Wix, it means the file format is not supported. You should check the specs of your video to ensure that it is using the H.264 codec. If it is not, you need to re-encode or convert the file using the [supported specs](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-media-supported-media-file-types-and-file-sizes).

articles.contents:
Wix Media: Troubleshooting Video File Upload Errors
If you are having trouble uploading your video files, make sure you're uploading the file in a supported file format.If you get a specific error message when uploading your video file, click the error message below to find out how to resolve it:Unsupported MP4 format. Upload this video file in a different format.The file format is not supported. Check the specs of your video, make sure that it is H.264 codec and re-encode or convert the file using the supported specs.Unsupported sample rate. Upload this video file in a different format.Check that your sample rate is 44,100, 48,000, 96,000, 88,200 or 192,000 hz. If not, re-encode or convert the file with a supported sample rate.Video bit rate ({bps}) is too high.Check the video bit rate (bps) and make sure that it's ~2600 kb\s.Video length ({videoDuration}) and audio length ({audioDuration}) don't match.Check that the video and audio duration match. Converting the file to a different or the same format can help correct this.The {codec} video codec used to make this file isn't supported.Make sure that your video is encoded with the H.264 codec and re-encode or convert file with our supported specs.Upload this file again in stereo format.Make sure that the audio of your video is in stereo format and not mono format. If it is mono format, change it and re-upload the video. Still need help?If the problem persists, contact us and we will be happy to help.
articles.title: Wix Media: Troubleshooting Video File Upload Errors
articles.html_content:
If you are having trouble uploading your video files, make sure you're uploading the file in a supported file format.
If you get a specific error message when uploading your video file, click the error message below to find out how to resolve it:

Unsupported MP4 format. Upload this video file in a different format.

The file format is not supported. Check the specs of your video, make sure that it is H.264 codec and re-encode or convert the file using the supported specs.

Unsupported sample rate. Upload this video file in a different format.

Check that your sample rate is 44,100, 48,000, 96,000, 88,200 or 192,000 hz. If not, re-encode or convert the file with a supported sample rate.

Video bit rate ({bps}) is too high.

Check the video bit rate (bps) and make sure that it's ~2600 kb\s.

Video length ({videoDuration}) and audio length ({audioDuration}) don't match.

Check that the video and audio duration match. Converting the file to a different or the same format can help correct this.

The {codec} video codec used to make this file isn't supported.

Make sure that your video is encoded with the H.264 codec and re-encode or convert file with our supported specs.

Upload this file again in stereo format.

Make sure that the audio of your video is in stereo format and not mono format. If it is mono format, change it and re-upload the video. 

Still need help?

If the problem persists, contact us and we will be happy to help.

question: What responsibilities do I have as a site owner regarding content published by site members and visitors?
answer: As a site owner, you are responsible for the content and comments available on your site. When using applications that allow visitors to add content such as Wix Forum, Wix Blog, Wix Video, or third-party applications, you allow your site visitors to post and publish content on your site. Therefore, all of the information posted by your visitors and members also becomes your site content. It's important that you're aware of the content published on your site, and that the content is compliant both with Wix’s Terms of Use, and also with the laws and regulations of your country. In the event Wix receives a valid court order, or law enforcement notice justifying a site's removal, we reserve our right to act upon it. This may mean immediately removing such a website, with or without notice prior to the removal. To learn more about user content and prohibited uses, please see Section 2 of our [Terms of Use](http://www.wix.com/about/terms-of-use).

question: Can I send confirmation emails from my own email address when someone RSVPs to my event on Wix?
answer:
Currently, confirmation emails sent to guests who RSVP your event are sent from notifications@wixevents.com. Sending a confirmation email from your own email address is not supported.

### Workaround
You can [create an automated email that is sent whenever a visitor RSVPs for an event](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-events-about-automated-emails-for-events). You can set this automated email to be sent from your own email address. Note that for RSVP events, you can [deactivate the regular confirmation email](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-events-managing-emails-you-send-and-receive) so guests won't get 2 messages.

question: How can I create and send a pay link using Wix Pay Links?
answer:
To create and send a pay link using Wix Pay Links, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Pay Links](https://manage.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?siteType=HtmlWeb&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/payment-links?&title=Select%20a%20site&buttonText=Create+Pay+Link) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **Create Link**.
3. Click **One-time payment** to create a link that accepts one payment, or click **Multi payment** to create a link that accepts multiple payments.
4. Click **Next**.
5. Set up your pay link:
   
   1. **Link name:** Enter a name for your pay link.
   2. **Price:** Enter the amount of money your pay link will charge your customer.
   3. (Optional) **Description:** Enter a description for your pay link. This should clearly summarize the reason for payment.
   4. (Optional) **Set an expiration date:** Click **Open settings** and enable the **Set an expiration date** toggle. Set a date when the link will expire and cannot be used.
   5. (Optional) **Customize link:** Click **Open settings** and set a **Button color**, edit **Button text** and upload a **Link image**. On the left you'll see a preview of how your pay link will be displayed.
   6. (Optional, multi-payment only) **Limit the number of payments:** Click **Open settings** and enable the **Limit the number of payments** toggle to set the number of times the link can be used before it expires.
6. Click **Create Link**.
7. Your link has been created. Choose what you want to do:
   
   * **Copy Link:** Copy the link to your clipboard.
   * **Send via email:** Select a contact using the **Select a customer** drop-down and click **Send Link** to send your pay link to this contact. 
     
     **Note:** Click **+ Add Contact** in the drop-down to create a new contact to send your pay link to.
   * **HTML embed:** Add pay link widget to your site by using HTML code.
   * **QR Code:** Click to generate a QR code. Customers can scan this code to access your pay link.
   * **Facebook:** Click **Share** to share your link via Facebook.
   * **LinkedIn:** Click **Share** to share your link via LinkedIn.
   * **Twitter:** Click **Share** to share your link via Twitter.

articles.contents:
Wix Pay Links: Creating and Managing Pay Links
Instantly request payments from contacts by sharing unique pay link URLs that allow them to make secure online payments. Share pay links via email, social media, SMS, or any other channel. You can also create a QR code for a pay link. Payments made via your pay links appear in your Wix account like all other transactions through your site.Send pay links to single or multiple recipients. Quickly and easily request one-time payments for products/services, or easily co-ordinate group activities, social event collections, and more. Pay links are not linked to any products or services listed on your site, so they can be used for many different purposes.Before you begin:
You need to upgrade your site so you can accept online payments to use Pay Links. If your plan expires, your active pay links will be on hold. In order to accept payments, you must also set up a payment method. If you've already set up a payment method for Wix Stores, Wix Bookings or Wix Events, you do not need to set one up again.In this article, learn more about:
Creating and sending a pay link Managing your pay links Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Creating and sending a pay linkChoose to create a one-time pay link or multi-payment link. A one-time pay link expires after your chosen contact makes one payment. A multi-payment link can be shared with multiple contacts and used for multiple payments. It can also be used for recurring payments from a single contact.To create and send a pay link:
Go to Pay Links in your site's dashboard. Click Create Link. Click One-time payment to create a link that accepts one payment, or click Multi payment to create a link that accepts multiple payments. Click Next. Set up your pay link:
    
Link name: Enter a name for your pay link. Price: Enter the amount of money your pay link will charge your customer. (Optional) Description: Enter a description for your pay link. This should clearly summarize the reason for payment. (Optional) Set an expiration date: Click Open settings and enable the Set an expiration date toggle. Set a date when the link will expire and cannot be used. (Optional) Customize link: Click Open settings and set a Button color, edit Button text and upload a Link image. On the left you'll see a preview of how your pay link will be displayed. (Optional, multi-payment only) Limit the number of payments: Click Open settings and enable the Limit the number of payments toggle to set the number of times the link can be used before it expires.   Click Create Link. Your link has been created. Choose what you want to do:
    
Copy Link: Copy the link to your clipboard. Send via email: Select a contact using the Select a customer drop-down and click Send Link to send your pay link to this contact.
Note: Click + Add Contact in the drop-down to create a new contact to send your pay link to. HTML embed: Add pay link widget to your site by using HTML code. QR Code: Click to generate a QR code. Customers can scan this code to access your pay link. Facebook: Click Share to share your link via Facebook. LinkedIn: Click Share to share your link via LinkedIn. Twitter: Click Share to share your link via Twitter.  Managing your pay linksAll of the pay links you create will be listed on the Pay Links page in your site's dashboard. The actions you can take for each link will depend on the link's type (one-time payment or multi-payment) and status.On your Pay Links page, you'll see a status attached to each pay link:
Active: Your link is accepting payments. Inactive: Your link is not accepting payments.
Note: If your inactive link hasn't expired, you can change its status to active. Paid: Payment has been made via this link. Expired: The expiration date you selected has passed and the link is no longer active.Hover over your pay link's status to view further information.To manage your pay links:
Go to Pay Links in your site's dashboard. Click a pay link to view further information in a panel on the right. Choose what you want to do:
    
Copy Link: Copy this pay link URL to your clipboard. Share: Send via email, QR code, Facebook, LinkedIn or Twitter. Activate: Make an inactive link active. Open link: Click the More Actions icon  and select Open link to view an active pay link. Deactivate: Click the More Actions icon  and select Deactivate to make an active link inactive.
Note: If no payments have been made, you'll also be able to select Delete to permanently delete a pay link. View Payments: View details of each payment.  FAQsHere are some common questions about pay links:Why is my contact unable to make a payment?If your contact reports that they are unable to make a payment, it could be because:
Your pay link is not accepting payments. Check its status - to accept payments, it needs to be Active rather than Inactive, Expired or reached its payment limit. If a pay link has a payment limit, it will not accept further payments if it has reached its limit or has pending transactions that will reach its limit (e.g. pay link with a limit of 3, with 2 payments received and 1 transaction in progress). Your pay link is temporarily offline. Refreshing the page should fix this.How do I change the currency of my pay links?You can change the currency of all invoices, price quotes and pay links. You do this from Settings in your site's dashboard.How do I embed a Pay Link on my site using an HTML code?You can embed HTML code to your site directly from the Add Elements panel.To add a HTML embed to your site:
Click Add Elements  in your Editor. Click Embed Code. Click Popular Embeds. Choose the type of embed you want to add to your site:Embed HTML: Embed a code snippet to display a widget on your site pages and set it up.
Embed a site: Display an external site in a window on your page. Click your chosen embed to add it to your site.
Learn more about embedding HTML code, external sites or widgets on your site.

Creating and sending a pay link

Choose to create a one-time pay link or multi-payment link. A one-time pay link expires after your chosen contact makes one payment. A multi-payment link can be shared with multiple contacts and used for multiple payments. It can also be used for recurring payments from a single contact.

  2. Click Create Link.

    4. (Optional) Set an expiration date: Click Open settings and enable the Set an expiration date toggle. Set a date when the link will expire and cannot be used.
    5. (Optional) Customize link: Click Open settings and set a Button color, edit Button text and upload a Link image. On the left you'll see a preview of how your pay link will be displayed.
    6. (Optional, multi-payment only) Limit the number of payments: Click Open settings and enable the Limit the number of payments toggle to set the number of times the link can be used before it expires.
  6. Click Create Link.
  7. Your link has been created. Choose what you want to do:
    • Copy Link: Copy the link to your clipboard.
    • Send via email: Select a contact using the Select a customer drop-down and click Send Link to send your pay link to this contact.
      Note: Click + Add Contact in the drop-down to create a new contact to send your pay link to.
    • HTML embed: Add pay link widget to your site by using HTML code.
    • QR Code: Click to generate a QR code. Customers can scan this code to access your pay link.
    • Facebook: Click Share to share your link via Facebook.
    • LinkedIn: Click Share to share your link via LinkedIn.
    • Twitter: Click Share to share your link via Twitter.

Managing your pay links

All of the pay links you create will be listed on the Pay Links page in your site's dashboard. The actions you can take for each link will depend on the link's type (one-time payment or multi-payment) and status.

On your Pay Links page, you'll see a status attached to each pay link:
  • Active: Your link is accepting payments.
  • Inactive: Your link is not accepting payments.
    Note: If your inactive link hasn't expired, you can change its status to active.
  • Paid: Payment has been made via this link.
  • Expired: The expiration date you selected has passed and the link is no longer active.

Hover over your pay link's status to view further information.

To manage your pay links:

  1. Go to Pay Links in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click a pay link to view further information in a panel on the right.
  3. Choose what you want to do:
    • Copy Link: Copy this pay link URL to your clipboard.
    • Share: Send via email, QR code, Facebook, LinkedIn or Twitter.
    • Activate: Make an inactive link active.
    • Open link: Click the More Actions icon and select Open link to view an active pay link.
    • Deactivate: Click the More Actions icon and select Deactivate to make an active link inactive.
      Note: If no payments have been made, you'll also be able to select Delete to permanently delete a pay link.
    • View Payments: View details of each payment.

FAQs

Here are some common questions about pay links:

Why is my contact unable to make a payment?

If your contact reports that they are unable to make a payment, it could be because:
  • Your pay link is not accepting payments. Check its status - to accept payments, it needs to be Active rather than Inactive, Expired or reached its payment limit. If a pay link has a payment limit, it will not accept further payments if it has reached its limit or has pending transactions that will reach its limit (e.g. pay link with a limit of 3, with 2 payments received and 1 transaction in progress).
  • Your pay link is temporarily offline. Refreshing the page should fix this.

How do I change the currency of my pay links?

You can change the currency of all invoices, price quotes and pay links. You do this from Settings in your site's dashboard.

How do I embed a Pay Link on my site using an HTML code?

You can embed HTML code to your site directly from the Add Elements panel.

To add a HTML embed to your site:

  1. Click Add Elements  in your Editor.
  2. Click Embed Code.
  3. Click Popular Embeds.
  4. Choose the type of embed you want to add to your site:Embed HTML: Embed a code snippet to display a widget on your site pages and set it up.
    Embed a site: Display an external site in a window on your page.
  5. Click your chosen embed to add it to your site.
Learn more about embedding HTML code, external sites or widgets on your site.

question: Why might there be discrepancies between Wix Analytics and Google Analytics data?
answer:
Discrepancies between Wix Analytics and Google Analytics data can occur due to several reasons:

1. **Differences in Traffic Data**: Both Wix Analytics and Google Analytics filter out traffic from bots, but they use different algorithms, which can lead to different results.

2. **Differences in Sales and People Reports**: Wix Analytics has access to production data on your Wix site, such as your contact list and transaction database, and will not show cancelled orders but will show zero sum (free) orders. Google Analytics, on the other hand, relies on client events, which might be lost due to network issues or not collected if cookies are not enabled, and it will show cancelled orders but not zero sum (free) orders.

3. **Differences in Metric Names**: The metric names between the two platforms aren't always an exact match. For example, 'Users' in Google Analytics is equivalent to 'Visitors' in Wix Analytics.

4. **Differences in Time Frames**: When Google shows stats for the last 7 days, the end date is yesterday, whereas in Wix Analytics, the last 7 days time period includes today.

For more detailed information, you can refer to the [Google Analytics data discrepancies](https://support.wix.com/en/article/discrepancies-between-wix-analytics-data-in-other-tracking-tools#google-analytics-data-discrepancies) section.

articles.title: Wix Analytics: Discrepancies Between Wix Analytics & Data in Other Tracking Tools
articles.html_content:
If you are using Wix Analytics and other tracking tools, such as Google Ads, Google Analytics, or Facebook Ads, you may find there are differences in your data.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Google Analytics data discrepancies
  • Google Ads data discrepancies
  • Facebook Ads data discrepancies
  • Other reasons for data discrepancies
Note:
The most common reason for seeing discrepancies in analytics data is cookie consent.

Google Analytics data discrepancies

Click a title below to learn more about the differences between Wix Analytics and Google Analytics data:

Differences in Traffic Data

Wix Analytics and Google Analytics filter out traffic from bots such as computer scripts, search engines, and QA checks by default. As Google and Wix use different algorithms to filter bot traffic, your analytics data may show different results.

Differences in Sales and People Reports

The differences in sales and people reports between Wix Analytics and Google Analytics are due to the different ways in which data is collected and processed:
  • Wix Analytics has access to production data in your Wix site, such as your contact list and transaction database. Wix Analytics will not show you cancelled orders, and it will show you zero sum (free) orders. 
  • Google Analytics data source is client events. Client events might be lost due to network issues, or not collected if cookies are not enabled, or if javascript does not run. Google Analytics will show you cancelled orders, and won't show you zero sum (free) orders.

Differences in Metric Names

Metric names between Wix Analytics and Google Analytics aren't always an exact match. When comparing data, note:

  • Users in Google Analytics = Visitors in Wix Analytics.
  • Traffic Channel in Google Analytics = Referring Category in Wix Analytics.
  • Referral in Google Analytics = Referring URL in Wix Analytics. 
  • Page in Google Analytics = Page Path in Wix Analytics.
  • Transactions in Google Analytics = Orders in Wix Analytics.
  • Revenues in Google Analytics = Total Sales in Wix Analytics.

Differences in Time Frames

When Google show stats for the last 7 days, the end date they refer to is yesterday. In Wix Analytics, the last 7 days time period includes today. This applies to all "Last X" time periods (last 30 days, last month, last year, etc.)

Google Ads data discrepancies

Click a title below to learn more about the differences between Wix Analytics and Google Ads data:

Discrepancies caused by disabled URL auto-tagging

If there are discrepancies between your site's Wix Analytics data and Google Ads data, check if URL auto-tagging is enabled. If auto-tagging is disabled, most of your traffic will be tagged as organic.

Tagging your Google Ads URLs

Metrics that are similar, but not the same

In Wix Analytics, a Site Session is all of the actions performed by a visitor, and ends after 30 minutes of inactivity.

If you compare Google Ad Clicks to Wix Analytics Site Sessions, it's possible you'll see a difference in your data. This is because the same visitor can click your ad more than once during a session.

Facebook Ads data discrepancies

Click a title below to learn more about the differences between Wix Analytics and Facebook Ads data:

Differences in metric names

In Wix Analytics, a Site Session is all of the actions performed by a visitor, and ends after 30 minutes of inactivity.

If you use Facebook Pixel, you'll see Landing Page Views metrics in your Facebook metrics. Landing Page Views can be compared to Site Sessions in Wix Analytics. Facebook's Link Clicks metrics should not be compared to Site Sessions in Wix Analytics. 

Learn more:
  • Facebook Visits Metric Information
  • Facebook Metrics for Website Visitors Ads

Differences in Traffic Source attribution models

Attribution models are customer touchpoints, showing which marketing campaigns and social media platforms are used to find and then revisit your site in a 30 day period. Due to the differences in traffic source attribution models, you might see more visits (landing page views) in Facebook metrics than in Wix Analytics.

Traffic Source in Wix Analytics:
The traffic source is where the visitor was referred from. If a visitor clicks a Facebook Ad, the traffic source is Facebook.

Traffic Source in Facebook metrics:
Wix gathers traffic data from sources that Facebook is not aware of, which can lead to data discrepancies. 

Example: A visitor clicked a Facebook ad, then received a marketing email sent through your Wix site, and they clicked a link in the email. Wix will attribute the visit to email marketing, and Facebook will attribute it to Facebook ads.

If you’re using the Wix Facebook Ads tool, you can count visits like these the same way Facebook does. Meaning, if a visitor clicked a Facebook ad in the last 7 days, and then came via email marketing, you can still attribute the visit to Facebook Ads by selecting the Wix FB Ads Last Click attribution model.

Learn more about Facebook attribution models

Differences in data due to visitors changing devices or browsers

Wix Analytics data: 
The data collected is based on site sessions, and each sessions limited to the browser in use at that time. If someone clicks a Facebook Ad, but completes the purchase later on a different device or browser, the order will not be attributed to the Facebook Ad.

Facebook Ads data:  
Facebook can track data from the same person over different devices and browsers. This means that if someone clicks a Facebook Ad and completes a purchase later on using a different device, the order is attributed to the Facebook Ad.

Other reasons for data discrepancies

Click a title below to find more reasons for data discrepancies in Wix Analytics:

Discrepancies when using multiple marketing channels

Wix Analytics collects traffic data from multiple marketing channel sources such as Facebook Ads, and Google Ads. The data in Facebook and Google may not be exact match to Wix Analytics data, as their data is based on one source.

Cookie Consent data discrepancies

If your site has a cookie consent banner, Wix Analytics data can only be collected from visitors who have clicked "Accept". Our analysis shows approximately 50% of visitors accept cookies, so if you have a Cookie Consent banner, it's fair to assume your traffic data should be doubled. 

Learn more about displaying cookie banners

Discrepancies caused by Analytics Blockers

Your site visitors can set their browser preferences to prevent the collection of data on specific websites, which can result in data discrepancies.

Discrepancies caused by timezone differences

There may be discrepancies between Wix Analytics and other analytics tools data due to different reporting timezones. 

For example: If your Wix account's time zone is set to Dublin GMT 00:00, and your Google Analytics account time zone is set to Kiev GMT +02:00, there will be a two hour difference in data collected.

To change the time zone in your Wix account:
  1. Go to Settings in your site's dashboard.
  2. Scroll to the General section and click Languages & Region. 
  3. Scroll to Time zone and update your time zone as required.
 

Discrepancies due to data latency

Wix Analytics and other analytics tools have different latency periods. There is a 1 hour latency in Wix Analytics. For the most accurate overview, compare long date ranges instead of hour by hour data.

Discrepancies due to different bot algorithms

Wix Analytics and other tracking tools filter out traffic from bots such as computer scripts, search engines, and QA checks by default. As each tool uses different algorithms to filter bot traffic, your analytics data may show different results.

Discrepancies resulting from HTTPS redirects in promotion tool ads

If your site is uses HTTPS, the referral data will be stripped out as direct data if you use http:’your site address’ in Google Ads or Facebook Ads.

Missing clicks in promotion ad tools

Not all clicks on your ads will result in your site page loading.
Need help?
If you need further assistance with Wix Analytics data discrepancies, contact us for support.

question: How can I mark a room as 'Not Available' in Wix Hotels?
answer:
To mark a room as 'Not Available' in Wix Hotels, follow these steps:

1. [Go to your dashboard.](https://support.wix.com/en/article/accessing-your-sites-dashboard)
2. Click the **Hotels** tab.
3. Click the **Reservations** tab.
4. Click the start date on the calendar for the relevant room.
5. Drag your mouse across and click the end date.
6. Click **Set as not available**.
7. (Optional) Add a note for yourself.
8. Click **Save**.

**Note**: Alternatively, you can mark a room as 'Not Available' by clicking **Create New** on the reservation calendar, filling out the requested information, and clicking **Save**.

* Your unavailable room is grayed out on your reservation calendar.
* To unblock a room, hover over the grayed out area on your reservation calendar and click **Unblock**.

question: What happens if I issue a chargeback for a Wix Premium plan payment, and how can I restore the features?
answer:
If you perform a chargeback for a payment made for your Premium plan, your plan is canceled. When a Premium plan is canceled:

* Your domain is disconnected from your site
* Your site displays Wix ads
* Your site's storage and bandwidth is limited
* Any other Premium features that come with your plan (e.g. Wix Stores) are removed

### Want to restore these features?
You must [purchase a new Premium plan](https://support.wix.com/en/article/choosing-a-premium-plan) with a **different** payment card.

Your service is canceled immediately. You may be liable for fees incurred as a result of the chargeback. Learn more in our Terms of Use. articles.title: Chargebacks in Your Wix Account
articles.html_content:
A chargeback is a debit or credit card transaction that's reversed by the customer's bank after they dispute a charge on their payment card. This article relates to chargebacks between Wix and its customers. 
If you issue a chargeback for a Wix service:
  • Your service is canceled immediately.
  • You may be liable for fees incurred as a result of the chargeback. Learn more in our Terms of Use.
  • Any data that relies on purchased features could be lost.
Important:
Before filing a dispute with your bank or credit card company, always contact Wix Customer Care with any questions concerning a charge from Wix.

Chargebacks for Premium plan payments

If you perform a chargeback for a payment made for your Premium plan, your plan is canceled.  
When a Premium plan is canceled: 
  • Your domain is disconnected from your site
  • Your site displays Wix ads
  • Your site's storage and bandwidth is limited
  • Any other Premium features that come with your plan (e.g. Wix Stores) are removed
Want to restore these features?
You must purchase a new Premium plan with a different payment card.

Chargebacks for Wix domain payments

Upon receiving a chargeback for a Wix domain payment:
  • The domain is suspended or removed from Wix for the remainder of its registration period
  • You will no longer be able to connect the domain to any website
  • You receive an email notification from Wix to inform you of the cancelation of your subscription

Chargebacks for business email subscriptions

If you issue a chargeback for a Google Workspace business email:
  • Your business email is canceled immediately
  • You are no longer be able to send or receive emails from your business email
  • Wix sends a cancelation notification to the email address of your Wix account
  • Your Wix account may become blocked from further use

Chargebacks for apps from the Wix App Market

If you issue a chargeback for an app from the Wix App Market:
  • Your service is canceled immediately.
  • Any Premium app features are removed from your site.
  • Any data that relies on these Premium features could be lost.
To restore your app features, you must upgrade it again using a different payment card. Learn how to upgrade an app from the Wix App Market.

question: How can I set viewing permissions for screens in the Wix mobile app for my members?
answer:
To set viewing permissions for screens in the Wix mobile app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
2. Tap **Manage** ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8769cf44-f342-494c-b25f-cc98c9da3e82/2021/04/12/3fc0f98c-0997-47b3-b7bd-6ae31a67e078/ce9c0fe5-f60d-4448-8fc2-9ba4cf636f93.png) at the bottom.
3. Tap **Mobile App**.
4. Tap **Edit**.
5. Tap **Screens**.
6. Tap the **More Actions** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/23b907b0-432d-4b7f-aaf8-02eba0ddf782/2021/08/26/2d4448a7-4b77-4dee-b7a7-0b75594eb843/d48de655-417d-4667-8ce0-b9c323144275.png) next to the relevant screen.
7. Tap **Set screen permissions**.
8. Select who can view this screen:
   
   * **All Members:** All members that visit your site have screen access.
   * **Members with Badges:** Choose which badge holders can access the screen, or tap **Create New Badge** to [create a new badge](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-owner-app-creating-and-managing-member-badges).
   * **Members with Pricing Plans:** Choose which Pricing Plan holders can access the screen, or tap **Create New Plan** to [create a new plan](https://support.wix.com/en/article/pricing-plans-creating-plans-in-the-wix-owner-app).

Members who do not have permission to view a screen will receive a message informing them that they don't have access and can request permission from you, the site owner.

articles.title: Wix Mobile Apps: Setting Viewing Permissions for Your Members
articles.html_content:
Your site on the member apps includes various screens that keep your content organized (e.g. Home, Events, Classes, etc.). Members use the navigation menu at the top to browse through your screens.
You can set permissions for each screen, so that only those members with specific badges or pricing plans can access them.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Setting viewing permissions for your screens
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

Setting viewing permissions for your screens

Decide who can view each screen on the Wix member apps. Give exclusive access to certain members with specific badges or pricing plans. For example, you can restrict a screen that features a special event or a private sale.

To set viewing permissions:

  1. Go to your site in the Wix app.  
  2. Tap Manage at the bottom.
  3. Tap Mobile App.
  4. Tap Edit.  
  5. Tap Screens. 
  6. Tap the More Actions icon next to the relevant screen.
  7. Tap Set screen permissions.
  8. Select who can view this screen:
    • All Members: All members that visit your site have screen access.
    • Members with Badges: ﻿Choose which badge holders can access the screen, or tap Create New Badge to create a new badge.
    • Members with Pricing Plans: ﻿Choose which Pricing Plan holders can access the screen, or tap Create New Plan to create a new plan.

FAQs

Click a question below to learn more about managing permissions for each screen.

What do members see when they don't have permission to view a screen?

Members receive a message informing them that they don't have permission to access the screen and to request permission from you (the site owner).

What happens after a member requests permissions to view a screen?

A chat message notifies you that a member is seeking permission to view a screen that you set permissions for. 

You can grant the member permissions by assigning them the relevant badge or advising them to purchase the specific pricing plan. If needed, you can also add a member manually to a pricing plan. 

Is there a difference between my site pages and the screens in the app?

Yes. Screens on the Wix member apps are structured differently than the pages on your site. 

If you restrict access to one of your site's pages, you also need to restrict the screen that shows this information on the Wix member apps (via the Wix mobile app).

question: How can I send a 30-second music track preview to my fans using Wix Email Marketing?
answer:
To send a 30-second music track preview to your fans using Wix Email Marketing, follow these steps:

1. Go to your [Music Library](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Open%20My%20Music&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/music/).
2. Select the song you want to promote.
3. Click **Edit Track Info**.
4. Scroll down and select **Fans can listen to a 30 sec preview** from the **Track Streaming Options** drop-down menu.
5. Click **Save** on the top right.
6. Go to your [Email Marketing Dashboard](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Go%20to%20Email%20Marketing&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https:%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Fdashboard%2F%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D%2Fshoutout%2F).
7. Hover over the **Promote Your Music** template.
8. Click **Use Template**.
9. Click on the music player in your email.
10. Select the preview song from the **Set Player Music** drop-down menu.
11. Choose to display a light or dark theme music player.
12. Design the rest of your email. [Learn More](https://support.wix.com/en/article/email-marketing-customizing-your-email-campaign)
13. Click **Next**.
14. Add your recipients.
15. Click **Publish.**

Fans will be redirected to your site from the email they receive to listen to the preview.

question: Can I add a hyperlink to a container in the Studio Editor?
answer:
While you can hyperlink text, images, and buttons in the Studio Editor, it is not possible to add a link to a container. As an alternative, you can add and set up a linked image inside the container, and set it to be transparent.
