articles.title: Adding Business Owners to Your Wix Payments Account
articles.html_content:
If you're accepting payments as a business entity (Corporation, General Partnership, Limited Liability Company), you must add the details of the relevant business owners to make sure your Wix Payments account complies with all legal requirements. 

Who is a Business Owner?

  • People holding 25% or more of the company's ownership. 
  • People who are significantly responsible for managing the company. This includes (but is not limited to) roles like the CEO, CFO, COO, President, Vice President, General Partner, Treasurer, Chairperson, etc.
Important:
  • Wix Payments may require additional information and/or documents to verify your Business Owners' identity. 
  • You may, but are not required to add another manager if you've already added yourself. 

Learn how to add a Business Owner:

  • In the Wix Payments setup process
  • In your Wix Payments Account Settings tab

Adding Business Owners in the Wix Payments Setup Process

  1. Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Complete Set-up under the relevant Wix Payments payment method. 
  3. Click Complete Account Set-up.
  4. Select your business type: Corporation, General Partnership, Limited Liability Company.
  5. Enter the Business Owner details:
    1. Full name
    2. Date of birth
    3. Country of citizenship
    4. Personal address
    5. ID number or Social Security Number (SSN)
  6. Select the checkboxes:
    1. Does this person own 25% or more of the business:
      • Yes: Select this option if this person is a shareholder owning 25% or more of the business.
      • No: Select this option if this person owns less than 25% or doesn't own the business at all.  
    2. Does this person have significant responsibility over company management:
      • Yes: Select this option if this person holds a position with significant responsibility over company management (e.g. CEO, CFO, Treasurer, Chairperson, etc.)
      • No: Select this option if this person's position doesn't involve significant responsibility over company management. 
  7. Enter the person's Role in the Business using the text box. 
  8. Click Save. 

Adding Business Owners in Wix Payments Account Settings

  1. Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Wix Payments Dashboard below the relevant payment method.
  3. Click Account Settings on the left. 
  4. Scroll down to Business Owners and click + Add Business Owner.
  5. Enter the Business Owner details:
    1. Full name
    2. Date of birth
    3. Country of citizenship
    4. Personal address
    5. ID number or Social Security Number (SSN)
  6. Select the checkboxes:
    1. Does this person own 25% or more of the business:
      • Yes: Select this option if this person is a shareholder owning 25% or more of the company.
      • No: Select this option if this person owns less than 25% or doesn't own the business at all.  
    2. Does this person have control over company management:
      • Yes: Select this option if this person holds a position with control over company management (e.g. CEO, CFO, Treasurer, Chairperson, etc.)
      • No: Select this option if this person's position doesn't involve company management. 
  7. Enter the person's Role in the Business using the text box. 
  8. Click Save. 
Tip:
Manage your Business Owners at any time through the Account Settings tab. Learn More

question: How can I sync my sandbox collection to my live collection in the CMS?
answer:
To sync your sandbox collection to your live collection, follow these steps:

1. Access your sandbox collections through your editor.
2. Make sure you have the content you want in your sandbox collection.
3. When you're ready, transfer the content from your sandbox collection to your live collection.
4. If your live collection already has content, you have the option to replace it with the content from your sandbox collection.

For detailed instructions, you can learn more about [syncing your sandbox collection to your live collection](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-accessing-and-syncing-your-sandbox-and-live-collections#accessing-and-syncing-sandbox-and-live-collections).

articles.contents:
CMS: About Sandbox and Live Collections
Important:When you create a new site, you'll notice that the sandbox is set to 'disabled' by default. If you're working on an existing site and want to disable the sandbox, you can. Learn how to enable sandbox collections. With the CMS (Content Management System), your site gets collections that hold various types of content, such as text, images, and files. Each collection can have a live version and, if you choose, a sandbox version. By default, the sandbox version is 'disabled'.The sandbox collection, accessible through your editor, serves as a test collection. The live version is what your visitors see on your live site. While these two versions can contain different content, you can sync the sandbox collection to the live collection whenever you want.Sandbox collectionsA sandbox collection gives you a test environment where you can arrange and store your site content while you're building your site. You can only see this content in the editor. It won't impact your live site unless you choose to sync it to a live collection.Learn how to access your sandbox collections. Live collectionsA live collection is where you store content such as text, images, and files that your visitors see and interact with on your live site. The content in a live collection may differ from that in your sandbox collection. You're able to change the content in a live collection, making it different from what's in the sandbox collection. However, the structure of both collections remains the same. If you want to see your live collections in your site's dashboard, you need to sync your sandbox collection with your live collection.Syncing a Sandbox collection to a Live collectionWorking on your sandbox collections won't change the appearance or functionality of your live site. When you're ready, you can transfer the content from your sandbox collection to your live collection. If your live collection already has content, you have the option to replace it with the content from your sandbox collection.Learn how to sync your sandbox collection to your live collection.
articles.title: CMS: About Sandbox and Live Collections
articles.html_content:
Important:
When you create a new site, you'll notice that the sandbox is set to 'disabled' by default. If you're working on an existing site and want to disable the sandbox, you can. Learn how to enable sandbox collections. 
With the CMS (Content Management System), your site gets collections that hold various types of content, such as text, images, and files. Each collection can have a live version and, if you choose, a sandbox version. By default, the sandbox version is 'disabled'.

The sandbox collection, accessible through your editor, serves as a test collection. The live version is what your visitors see on your live site. While these two versions can contain different content, you can sync the sandbox collection to the live collection whenever you want.

Sandbox collections

A sandbox collection gives you a test environment where you can arrange and store your site content while you're building your site. You can only see this content in the editor. It won't impact your live site unless you choose to sync it to a live collection.
Learn how to access your sandbox collections. 

Live collections

A live collection is where you store content such as text, images, and files that your visitors see and interact with on your live site. The content in a live collection may differ from that in your sandbox collection. 

You're able to change the content in a live collection, making it different from what's in the sandbox collection. However, the structure of both collections remains the same. If you want to see your live collections in your site's dashboard, you need to sync your sandbox collection with your live collection.

Syncing a Sandbox collection to a Live collection

Working on your sandbox collections won't change the appearance or functionality of your live site. When you're ready, you can transfer the content from your sandbox collection to your live collection. If your live collection already has content, you have the option to replace it with the content from your sandbox collection.
Learn how to sync your sandbox collection to your live collection.

question: How can I create an automation in Wix to send an email to someone who submits a CMS form?
answer:
To create an automation that sends an email to the form submitter, follow these steps:

1. After selecting **CMS** as your trigger, select the **Create a contact** action.
2. Click **Match Data**.
3. Select **\+ Add Field** and choose the **Email** field.
4. Click the drop-down under **Automation data** and select the **Email** field that collects the form submitter's email address.
5. Repeat these steps for each field you want the automation to update with data submitted by your custom form.
6. Click **OK**.
7. Select an option under **If a similar contact already exists** to choose what happens if you already have a contact with the same email or phone number:
   * **Update the existing contact:** Override the existing contact's contact info.
   * **Create a duplicate contact:** Create a new duplicate contact with the matched custom form data.
   * **Do nothing:** Do not override existing contact info or create a new contact from the matched custom form data.
8. Click **\+ Add an Action** at the bottom, then select the **Send an email** action.
9. Customize the email that will be sent in the **Create an email** drop-down.
10. Click the **Set email type** drop-down to choose the type of email that is sent.
11. Click **Set recipients** and make sure **Include trigger contact** is checked. This ensures that the recipient who triggered the automation receives the email. You can click **Change** to select an alternative email address where this automated email will be sent.
12. Click **Activate** when you are done setting up the automation.

articles.contents:
Wix Automations: Creating Automations for CMS Form Submissions
Use Wix Automations to ensure that all submissions you receive from custom CMS (Content Management System) forms are handled appropriately. This automation works with any CMS forms created with input elements. Choose from a variety of actions such as running Velo code, sending data via webhooks, or connecting third-party apps such as Google Sheets and Zapier. You can also automate more basic actions like sending or receiving emails, creating or updating contacts, and more. Before you begin: 
Make sure to add the CMS to your site, if you haven't already.  Make sure to create a custom form with input elements that submit to a CMS collection. In this article, learn more about:
Creating an automation for CMS custom form submissions Frequently asked questions (FAQs)Creating a CMS custom form automationWhen setting up your automation, choose the CMS trigger and whichever action you want to occur when you receive a submission from your custom form. To create an automation for CMS custom form submissions:
Go to Automations in your site's dashboard. Click + New Automation. Click + Start from Scratch. Click the title to give your automation a name. In the Trigger section, click CMS. Select an option under Select which CMS form triggers this automation:

articles.title: Wix Automations: Creating Automations for CMS Form Submissions
articles.html_content:
Use Wix Automations to ensure that all submissions you receive from custom CMS (Content Management System) forms are handled appropriately. This automation works with any CMS forms created with input elements. Choose from a variety of actions such as running Velo code, sending data via webhooks, or connecting third-party apps such as Google Sheets and Zapier. You can also automate more basic actions like sending or receiving emails, creating or updating contacts, and more. 
Before you begin:
  • Make sure to add the CMS to your site, if you haven't already. 
  • Make sure to create a custom form with input elements that submit to a CMS collection. 

In this article, learn more about:
  • Creating an automation for CMS custom form submissions
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

Creating a CMS custom form automation

When setting up your automation, choose the CMS trigger and whichever action you want to occur when you receive a submission from your custom form. 

To create an automation for CMS custom form submissions:

  1. Go to Automations in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click + New Automation.
  3. Click + Start from Scratch.
  4. Click the title to give your automation a name.
  5. In the Trigger section, click CMS.
  6. Select an option under Select which CMS form triggers this automation:
    • Any: Any form that uses input elements and the CMS triggers the automation.
    • Specific: Specific forms that use input elements and the CMS trigger the automation. Click Select, then select the custom form(s) you want to use and click OK.
      Note: Your custom forms are listed with the name of the page they appear on first, followed by the collection that stores the submissions.
  7. Click the Limit frequency to drop-down to set the trigger frequency:
    • Don't limit (trigger every time): Your action will take place every time it is triggered by a visitor.
    • Once per contact: Your action will take place only once per contact.
    • Once per contact every 24hrs: Your action will take place only once per contact in any 24hr period.
  1. (Optional) Click + Add Delay to add a delay between the trigger and when the action occurs. Then choose how many days, hours or minutes to delay the timing by. 
  2. (Optional) Add a condition that must happen in order for the automation to continue:
    1. Click + Add Condition.
    2. Click the Select criteria drop-down and choose the collection field to use in the condition.
    3. Click the next drop-down and choose an operator (e.g. equals, contains, is true).  
    4. Click the drop-down or text box that appears next to your operator drop-down to complete your condition. The logical statement you've created will determine whether the automation continues.
    5. (Optional) Click + Add Criteria to add any further criteria.
  1. Select the action that will take place after the trigger (e.g. send an email, get an email, create a contact). Learn more about the actions you can choose.
    Note: If you want to use the automation to send an email to the person who submitted a form, update an existing contact, or create a new contact, select the Create a contact action. See the FAQ section below for more information.
  2. Set up the action using the available options, which vary depending on the action type. 
  3. (Optional) Click + Add an Action to add a follow-up action.
    Note: It is not possible to add a follow-up action that creates or updates one of your contacts. Use the Create a contact as your automation's 1st action if you want to create or update contacts. 
  4. Click Activate to save and activate the automation.

FAQs

Click below for answers to common questions about using automations with custom CMS forms. 

How do I use the automation to send an email to the person who submitted the form?

To send an email to the person who triggered the automation by submitting your form, you must first use the Create a contact action. This allows you to match the email address collected from your form with the email address you have stored in your Contacts list. Then you can create an additional action and choose the Send an email action to have the automation send an email to the person who submitted your form. 

To create an automation that sends an email to the form submitter: 
  1. After selecting CMS as your trigger, select the Create a contact action. 
  2. Click Match Data.
  3. Select + Add Field and choose the Email field.
  4. Click the drop-down under Automation data and select the Email field that collects the form submitter's email address.
  5. Repeat these steps for each field you want the automation to update with data submitted by your custom form. 
  6. Click OK.
  7. Select an option under If a similar contact already exists to choose what happens if you already have a contact with the same email or phone number: 
    • Update the existing contact: Override the existing contact's contact info. 
    • Create a duplicate contact: Create a new duplicate contact with the matched custom form data. 
    • Do nothing: Do not override existing contact info or create a new contact from the matched custom form data. 
  8. Click + Add an Action at the bottom, then select the Send an email action. 
  9. Customize the email that will be sent in the Create an email drop-down. 
  10. Click the Set email type drop-down to choose the type of email that is sent. 
  11. Click Set recipients and make sure Include trigger contact is checked. This ensures that the recipient who triggered the automation receives the email. You can click Change to select an alternative email address where this automated email will be sent.
  12. Click Activate when you are done setting up the automation. 

How do I use the automation to update a contact or create a new contact?

The Create a contact action allows you to use the submissions from your custom form to update contact details for an existing or new contact. You can map any of the fields from your CMS collection to the following Contacts fields: First name, Last name, Email, or Phone number.

You can also decide what happens if a contact with the same email address or phone number already exists in your Contacts list. Choose to either update the existing contact, create a new one, or do nothing. 

To use the 'Create a contact' action: 
  1. After selecting CMS as your trigger, select the Create a contact action. 
  2. Click Match Data and choose which fields from your collection to save to your new or existing contact: 
    1. Click + Add Field and select the Contacts field you would like to map to a CMS collection field that your custom form submits to. Choose from First name, Last name, Email, or Phone number.
    2. Click the drop-down under Automation data and choose the CMS collection field you would like to map to your selected Contacts field. 
    3. Repeat these steps for each Contacts field you want the automation to update using data submitted by your custom form. 
    4. Click OK.
  3. Select an option under If a similar contact already exists to choose what happens if you already have a contact with the same email or phone number: 
    • Update the existing contact: Override the existing contact's contact info. 
    • Create a duplicate contact: Create a new duplicate contact with the matched custom form data. 
    • Do nothing: Do not override existing contact info or create a new contact from the matched custom form data. 
  4. Click Activate when you are done setting up the automation. 

How do I understand which automations are available to me?

The automations you can create depend on which apps (e.g. Wix Blog, Wix Restaurants) you have added to your site.

Automation trigger options are specific to the app you've selected, and automation action options are specific to the trigger you've selected. Select an app to view your trigger options, then select your trigger to view your action options.

Popular automations include:
  • Sending a "thank you", "welcome" or "next steps" email when a visitor submits a form. Learn more about sending automated emails to contacts after form submissions
  • Sending a discount coupon or reminder email when a customer has abandoned their shopping cart. Learn more about automatically sending discount coupons
  • Sending an email when an invoice is overdue. Learn more about Wix Invoices automations
  • Awarding loyalty points when a restaurant order is received. Learn more about Wix Restaurants automations
  • Sending a chat message when a form is submitted, or automatically replying to incoming chat messages. Learn more about Wix Chat automations

Can I connect my automations to apps that I use outside of my Wix site?

Yes, you can use Zapier to connect your Wix automations to external apps such as Slack, Trello and Google Docs.

question: Can I customize the automated emails sent to clients for services that require approval in Wix Bookings?
answer:
Currently, none of the automated emails sent to clients for services that [require your approval](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-bookings-requiring-approval-for-appointment-bookings) can be customized. These emails are sent to notify clients when:

* Their request was received
* Their request was approved

* The service is being rescheduled

You can add a personal note to emails notifying that you declined the request or rescheduled the session.

question: How do I connect my Google Workspace business email for a domain that is pointing to Wix?
answer:
To connect your Google Workspace business email for a domain that is pointing to Wix, follow these steps:

1. Log in to your domain host account where your DNS records are managed.
2. Add the following MX records to your DNS settings:

   | Name/Host/Alias | Time to Live (TTL*) | Record Type | Priority | Value/Answer/Destination |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Blank or @ | 3600 | MX | 1 | ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM. |
   | Blank or @ | 3600 | MX | 5 | ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM. |
   | Blank or @ | 3600 | MX | 5 | ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM. |
   | Blank or @ | 3600 | MX | 10 | ALT3.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM. |
   | Blank or @ | 3600 | MX | 10 | ALT4.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM. |

### Tip
View Google's list of [host-specific directions for adding Google Workspace MX records](https://support.google.com/a/topic/1611273).

### Note about TTL
Once the MX records are set up correctly, Google recommends changing the TTL value to 86400.

question: How can I manage my online programs using the Wix app?
answer:
To manage your online programs using the Wix app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
2. Tap **Manage** ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8769cf44-f342-494c-b25f-cc98c9da3e82/2021/04/12/3fc0f98c-0997-47b3-b7bd-6ae31a67e078/ce9c0fe5-f60d-4448-8fc2-9ba4cf636f93.png) at the bottom.
3. Tap **Online Programs**.
4. Tap the relevant tab according to the status of your program: **Published**, **Drafts** or **Archived**.
5. Tap the **Show More** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8696077d-830a-4b1e-bd86-9df98f89994a/2019/12/12/1835d4f5-b2dd-4e7a-89a5-827300193b95/4cb18247-c7c8-4de8-b91f-8d4f4f30ccbc.png) next to the program you want to manage and do one of the following:

   * **Edit:** Edit your program's details.
   * **Duplicate:** Make a copy of your program. This creates a copy of your program in the **Draft** tab.
   * **End:** Discontinue your program at any time.
   * **Publish:** If your program is still a draft, you can publish it from here.
   * **Archive:** Send your program to the archive. You can find it in the **Archived** tab.
   * **Delete:** Delete your program and its information permanently.

question: How can I update multiple orders at once in Wix Stores?
answer:
To update multiple orders at once in Wix Stores, follow these steps:

1. [Go to the Orders tab](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20Orders&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/store/orders) in your site's dashboard.
2. Select checkboxes next to the orders you want to update.
3. Click the action from the top bar:
   
   * **Assign Tags:** Add or remove tags you created. [Learn more](https://support.wix.com/en/article/assigning-tags-to-orders)
   * **Export:** Click to download a .CSV file. [Learn more](https://support.wix.com/en/article/exporting-orders-3126323)
   * **Print Orders:** Send orders to your printer.
   * **Print Shipping Label:** Create and print multiple labels through Wix Shipping. [Learn more](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-printing-shipping-labels-with-wix-shipping#purchasing-and-printing-multiple-labels-at-once) 
     
     **Note:** This option is not available in all regions.
4. Click **More Actions** and select an action:
   
   * **Mark as paid:** Mark the selected orders as "Paid".
   * **Mark as fulfilled:** Mark the selected orders as "Fulfilled" (Relevant only for store orders).
   * **Create Invoice:** An invoice is created and appears in the Invoices tab.
   * **Archive:** Adds the selected orders to the archive.

### Notes
* You can create an invoice for up to 100 invoices at once.
* You cannot add tracking numbers to multiple store orders at once.

question: How can I connect page elements to my CMS collections in Wix?

articles.title: CMS (Content Management System): An Overview
articles.html_content:
The Wix CMS (Content Management System) allows to you manage your site's content in collections that are separate from your editor. You then connect this content to elements on your site, such as repeaters, galleries, and tables. As a result, the connected elements dynamically display the content from your CMS collection.

Display your content in an unlimited number of dynamic pages that share the same consistent layout. Create custom forms for visitors to submit information directly to your collections. Utilize Wix's full suite of SEO options to get the best search engine rankings possible. See how it all works by adding presets in your editor and let AI help you get started creating your first collection. 
Click to watch a video overview of using the CMS in Wix Studio. 

Store vast amounts of content in CMS collections

CMS collections are databases where you store content such as text, images, and videos for use on dynamic pages and elements. 

Within each collection, you have the flexibility to select your preferred layout—choose from Table, List, or Gallery—and effortlessly manage different field types. Organize, sort, and filter your data, and save customized views for smooth collaboration with your team. Import and export your collections as CSV files with ease.

Fine-tune access controls with permissions and privacy settings, determining who can view, add, edit, or delete content. Optimize performance with advanced indexes to speed up queries and prevent duplicates.

Stay organized by neatly organizing your collections into folders for quick and easy access. For added security and peace of mind, use Backups to restore previous collection versions.

Integrate seamlessly with Wix App Collections to access data from other Wix apps like Wix Stores or Wix Bookings. And for a worry-free experience, leverage the Sandbox as a safe testing environment to ensure everything is perfect before launching live.
Learn how to create a CMS collection for your site's content. 

Use dynamic content in your page elements

In the CMS, datasets are your tool for linking elements within your editor to the content stored in your collections. Select any supported element in your editor and click the Connect to CMS icon to map out which collection fields correspond to each part of your elements. 

Within your dataset settings, you have full control. Customize the dataset mode to suit your needs, set the maximum number of items to load at once, and fine-tune filters and sorting conditions to exclude specific items and determine their display order on your site. With these settings, you can ensure your content is presented exactly how you envision it.
Learn more about connecting page elements to datasets.

Create dynamic pages that share the same structure

With dynamic pages, you can revolutionize the way you build and manage your website, streamlining the creation and upkeep process with ease. Dynamic pages maintain a consistent layout and design across your site while dynamically updating their content based on the connected collection items.

Unlike static pages, which are limited to 100 per Wix site, dynamic pages offer limitless potential. You can create as many dynamic pages as needed to meet your clients' requirements without any restrictions.

There are two types of dynamic pages:
  • Dynamic List Pages: These pages serve as showcases for multiple items sourced from a collection, presenting them in galleries or repeaters. Visitors can interact with these pages, clicking on specific items to navigate to their respective dynamic item pages for details.
  • Dynamic Item Pages: Automatically generated for each item within your connected collection, these pages provide comprehensive information about individual collection items. Various page elements are dynamically populated with details from your collection fields, offering a seamless browsing experience for your site visitors.
Learn more about:
  • How dynamic pages work
  • Dynamic list pages
  • Dynamic item pages

Collect site visitor submissions in CMS collections

Empower site visitors to engage with your site through personalized input and navigation features. Take full control by setting permissions for each collection, managing who can access and modify collection content.

Enhance user interaction by seamlessly integrating input elements like text fields, signature boxes, and upload buttons with datasets, enabling visitors to submit data directly to CMS collections. Implement interactive filtering options with dropdowns, selection tags, and radio buttons, allowing visitors to refine their browsing experience within repeaters or galleries.

Tailor unique interactive and navigational elements by linking buttons or images to datasets and defining their click actions. For example, you can design buttons that load additional items within a repeater or gallery, navigate to the next dynamic item page, reset input values, and more. With these customized features, you can enhance user experience and encourage meaningful engagement on your site.
Learn how to create a custom form using input elements that submits to your collection. 

Optimize dynamic page SEO settings

Manage SEO settings for dynamic pages within your editor. Customize the URL slug structure by adding variables, ensuring that each CMS collection item receives its own distinctive web address. These variables are automatically substituted with the actual field values from the collection items so that every page has a unique URL. This practice not only aids search engines in comprehending the content of each page but also assists visitors in understanding the relevance of the content.
Learn more about working with SEO settings for dynamic pages. 

Jumpstart your CMS with presets and AI

Begin by exploring presets or AI (Artificial Intelligence) to expedite your workflow.

Presets serve as templates for dynamic page creation within the CMS. Each preset includes:
  • A sample collection pre-filled with content linked to new dynamic pages.
  • A dynamic list page showcasing collection items in a repeater or gallery.
  • A dynamic item page providing detailed information about individual collection items.

Choose from a range of customizable presets. Upon adding a preset, the dynamic pages and their associated collection are seamlessly integrated into your editor, ready for customization according to your preferences.

Additionally, harness the power of AI with the AI Collection Creator to streamline the creation of new CMS collections. Simply provide a name and prompt for the collection you wish to create, and let AI handle the rest. Once generated, manage the collection fields and content just like any other collection.
Get started today by adding the CMS to your site.

question: How can I manually add guests to a ticketed event with a seating map using the Wix dashboard?
answer:
To manually add guests to a ticketed event with a seating map using the Wix dashboard, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Events](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20Events&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D/events/) in your site's dashboard.
2. Hover over the relevant event and click **Manage**.
3. Click the **Guests** tab at the top.
4. Click **Add Guests**. If your event doesn't have guests yet, click **Or add guests manually**.
5. Add **Ticket details**:
   - Click **Select tickets**.
   - Choose a seat(s) from the seating map.
   - Click **Select Tickets**.
   - (Optional) Click **\+ Add ticket** to add another ticket type.
6. Enter the **Buyer details** (first name, last name, email). You can click **\+ Add from Contacts** to choose a guest from your contact list.
7. Add the **Guest details** (If your registration form settings is "registration form for each ticket in an order"):
   - If the guest is also the buyer, select the **Same as buyer details** checkbox.
   - Enter the first name, last name, and email.
   - Click **\+ Add from Contacts** to select and add guests from your contact list.
8. Select an **Order status** (not paid, paid, or free).
9. Select or deselect the **Send tickets via email** checkbox.
10. Click **Save** at the top right.

articles.html_content:
You can manually add guests to your event without them having to RSVP or purchase a ticket through your site. This can come in handy in various situations, such as:
  • Adding multiple tickets / guests to one order.
  • Purchasing tickets for a group.
  • Handling guests who RSVP'd in person.
  • Offering free tickets to your ticketed event.
  • Assigning specific seats to guests in your seating map.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Manually adding guests
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

Manually adding guests

When adding guests manually, you can choose whether to add just 1 or multiple people at once. This lets you assign tickets or seats to an entire group in a single transaction. 
Depending on your registration form settings, guest information can either be collected once for the entire order or separately for each ticket.
Note:
Currently, adding multiple guests is only available on desktop.

To manually add guests:

Dashboard
Wix app

  2. Hover over the relevant event and click Manage. 
  3. Click the Guests tab at the top.
  4. Click Add Guests. 
    Note:     If your event doesn't have guests yet, click Or add guests manually. 
  5. Click a type of event below to complete the Add Guests form:

Event without tickets

  1. Enter the Guest details (first name, last name, email).  
    Note: You can click Add from Contacts to choose a guest from your contact list. 
  2. (Optional) Click +Add New Guest to add more people. 
  3. Select an RSVP status (going, not going or waitlist).
  4. Click Save at the top right.


Events with tickets

  1. Add Ticket details:
    1. Click the Ticket Type drop-down and select a ticket type (e.g. VIP, Early Bird). 
    2. Click the Quantity drop-down and select the number of tickets.
    3. (Optional) Click + Add ticket to add another ticket type. 
  2. Enter the Buyer details (first name, last name, email).
    Note: You can click + Add from Contacts to choose a guest from your contact list. 
  3. Add the Guest details (If your registration form settings is "registration form for each ticket in an order"):
    • If the guest is also the buyer, select the Same as buyer details checkbox.
    • Enter the first name, last name and email.
    • Click + Add from Contacts to select and add guests from your contact list.
  4. Select an Order status (not paid, paid, or free).
  5. Select or deselect the Send tickets via email checkbox.
  6. Click Save at the top right.

Ticketed event with a seating map

  1. Add Ticket details:
    1. Click Select tickets.
    2. Choose a seat(s) from the seating map.
    3. Click Select Tickets.
    4. (Optional) Click + Add ticket to add another ticket type. 
  2. Enter the Buyer details (first name, last name, email).
    Note: You can click + Add from Contacts to choose a guest from your contact list. 
  3. Add the Guest details (If your registration form settings is "registration form for each ticket in an order"):
    • If the guest is also the buyer, select the Same as buyer details checkbox.
    • Enter the first name, last name and email.
    • Click + Add from Contacts to select and add guests from your contact list.
  4. Select an Order status (not paid, paid, or free).
  5. Select or deselect the Send tickets via email checkbox.
  6. Click Save at the top right.

Adding multiple guests?
Gather guest details by collecting registration information for the entire order or for each guest individually.

FAQs

Click a question below to learn more about manually adding guests to events.

Can I add a guest to a past event?

Yes, but only if the event already has at least one guest. If your past events have no guests, then it's not possible. 

What email notifications do manually-added guests receive?

Guests that you've added manually receive reminder emails if they were added before the reminder is sent out. This also applies to cancellation emails. However, they do not receive a confirmation email.

How can I check details about an order?

When viewing an order, you can access the buyer's info, such as the order number and order date. Additionally, you can review the order summary, which includes all purchased tickets for the event along with their payment status.
  1. Go to Events in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Manage next to the relevant event. 
  3. Click the Guests tab at the top.
  4. Hover over the relevant guest and click View. 
  5. Click View Order under Buyers info.

How many tickets can I add to a single order?

You can add up to 50 tickets at once.

question: How can I cancel my Branded App plan and request a refund within the first 30 days?
answer:
To cancel your Branded App plan and request a refund within the first 30 days, follow these steps:

1. Go to [Subscriptions](https://premium.wix.com/wix/api/mpContainerStaticController?originWidgetName=billings) in your Wix account.
2. Scroll down to the site with the branded app and click the More Actions icon next to **Branded App**.
3. Click **Cancel Branded App**.
4. Click **Cancel Now** in the pop-up to confirm.

You are eligible to receive a refund within the first 30 days from the initial purchase. If you canceled within 72 hours of a purchase (during the trial period), it is likely that the transaction was canceled before the funds settled. In this case, instead of receiving a refund, the original charge(s) will be removed from your account within 20 business days. Please allow up to 20 business days for your refund to appear on your credit card statement.

articles.html_content:
Before you can get your Branded App live and connected to Apple's App Store or Google Play, first purchase a Branded App plan. After you've purchased, you are eligible to receive a refund within the refund timeframe.

Branded app refund policy details

question: How can I connect an additional domain to my Wix site?
answer:
To connect an additional domain to your Wix site, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Domains](https://manage.wix.com/wix/api/mpContainerStaticController#/domains) in your Wix account.
2. Assign your domain to your site:

### If you want to assign a domain that is currently assigned to a different site:
1. Click the **Domain Actions** icon next to the relevant domain.
2. Click **Assign to a Different Site**.
3. Select a site and click **Next**.
4. Click **Assign**.

### If you want to assign a domain that is not currently assigned to a site:
1. Scroll to the relevant domain and click the **Assign** button next to the text **Not Assigned to a Site**.
2. Select a site and click **Next**.
3. Click **Assign**.

### Allow 24 hours for the redirection to propagate
For the first 24 hours, the site is available under two domain names (both the primary and redirected domain). After 24 hours, the URL in your browser's address bar changes to your primary domain when you enter your redirecting domain's URL.

### Tip
When using Google Analytics, you only need to add a tracking ID to your primary domain. Learn more about [using Google Analytics with your Wix site](https://support.wix.com/en/article/tracking-events-on-your-wix-site-with-a-google-analytics-property).

question: How can I add a new item or service to my Wix invoices or price quotes?
answer:
To add an item or service to your Wix invoices or price quotes, follow these steps:

1. Go to [Invoices](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Go%20to%20Invoices&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/invoices/invoices/list?referralInfo=KB-Article) or [Price Quotes](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20Price%20Quotes&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/price-quotes) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **More Actions** at the top right.
3. Select **Create items & services**.
4. Click **+ New Item** and enter the details:
   
   * **Item / Service:** Enter the name of the item or service.
   * **Description:** Add a short description.
   * **Price:** Enter the price of the item or service.
5. Click **Save**.

### Tip
You can also add a new item or service while creating an invoice or price quote. Start typing in the **Item or Service** field and click **New Item**.

question: How can I add a filter to my dataset in the CMS to control which items appear on my live site?
answer:
To add a filter to your dataset in the CMS, follow these steps:

1. **Select the field:** After adding the filter in the dataset settings, choose which collection field you want to filter by. Think of it as setting the criteria for your search.

2. **Define the condition:** Next, specify the condition that your filter should apply. Depending on the type of field, you can use conditions like "is," "Starts with," "Greater than," or "Equals." The options are tailored to suit the field type.

3. **Set the Value:** Finally, decide on the value that your filter should match. This could be a specific category, a numerical threshold, or even the logged-in user.

Learn how to [add filters to your dataset to include or exclude items](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-formerly-content-manager-adding-filters-and-sorts-to-datasets-to-control-live-site-content#adding-filters-to-your-dataset-to-exclude-items-from-your-page).

articles.contents:
CMS: About Filtering and Sorting Live Site Content with Datasets
When you're managing CMS (Content Mangement System) content, it's important to keep things organized and make sure only the right items show up on your live site. You can do this by adding sorts and filters to your datasets. Keep in mind that filters and sorts you add to the dataset have no effect on how items appear in your CMS collection views. If you enable the "Mirror on Site" feature to use the collection's order on your live site, sorts you add to the dataset override the order from your mirrored collection.In this guide, explore how you can use these tools to ensure your collection items are presented exactly as you intend.Filter datasets for clarityFiltering your dataset gives you precise control over which collection items appear on the connected site elements. It's like using a magnifying glass to focus on specific details within a collection that contains vast amounts of content. If you ever need to change or remove a filter, you can do it easily from the dataset settings. Here's how adding a filter to your dataset works:Select the field: After adding the filter in the dataset settings, choose which collection field you want to filter by. Think of it as setting the criteria for your search.Define the condition: Next, specify the condition that your filter should apply. Depending on the type of field, you can use conditions like "is," "Starts with," "Greater than," or "Equals." The options are tailored to suit the field type.Set the Value: Finally, decide on the value that your filter should match. This could be a specific category, a numerical threshold, or even the logged-in user.Learn how to add filters to your dataset to include or exclude items.Combine filters for precisionYou may need more than one filter to get really specific. Imagine you're curating a list of recipes, and you want to showcase French recipes that are not too difficult to complete. You could add a filter that includes only French recipes, and another that excludes advanced recipes. Only items that match the criteria of both filters will display in the dataset's connected repeater, gallery, or other elements. Learn more about using datasets to control your live site content. Sorting to reorder itemsSorting helps you put your collection items in a specific, logical order. It's like arranging your books on a shelf in alphabetical or date order. Here's how sorting in your dataset settings works:Choose which field to sort: Start by picking which collection field you want to sort your items by. This field determines the basis for arranging your items. It could be something like the name of a recipe or the date it was created.Decide the order: Decide on the order in which you want your items to appear. The field type you sort by determines the available sorting options. You can sort alphabetically, numerically, oldest to newest, true fields first, and vice versa for each option.Notes:
Sorts also determine the order in which items load for navigational buttons connected to the dataset. Learn about the dataset click actions you can assign to buttons and images.  Dataset sorts override the order in any collections in which you've enabled the "Mirror on Site" feature. However, dataset sorts do not affect the order in which items appear in your collection views.Learn how to add sort conditions to datasets to control the order in which items display.Sorting by multiple conditionsYou can add multiple sort conditions for more advanced organization. With multiple sorts, the first condition is sorted first, followed by the second condition, and so on. This helps when you have multiple items that match your first sort condition and you want to further customize their order. For example, you may want to sort recipes by cuisine, then add another sort to keep them listed alphabetically by name within each cuisine group. To do so, add a sort for the cuisine field and a second sort for the recipe name. You can also add a collection field exclusively for sorting to create a custom order. Learn how to add fields to your CMS collection. FAQsClick below for answers to common questions about filtering and sorting live site content. Can I hide fields in my collection to prevent them from appearing on the page?Yes. In your collection settings, you can toggle on Control item visibility. This adds a new field in your collection where you can set individual items as "Hidden". These items do not get read by the dataset, so they cannot appear on your live site. With this feature, you can also set schedules that automatically show or hide collection items at specific dates and times.Learn more about controlling item visibility from your collection itself.  Keep in mind that hiding, showing, or reordering fields in your collection view, does not affect whether they can be connected to your page elements. Does filtering or sorting datasets affect my collection?No. Adding filters or sorts to datasets affects item visibility and order on your connected page elements. It does not change anything in your collection itself. Learn how to manage your collection content. Does the dataset mode matter when filtering or sorting?Yes. The dataset mode determines whether the dataset can read your collection content, write to your collection, or both. Your dataset needs to be in "Read" or "Read & Write" mode to read your collection items and apply filters or sort conditions. If your dataset is set to "Write" mode, it is meant to be used to connect user input elements to your collection for capturing visitor submissions. "Write" mode datasets cannot read your collection content, so they cannot display the content or apply filters or sorts. Learn more about dataset modes. Can I filter by a reference field or another dataset?In a regular dataset, you can filter by a reference field, only if the referenced collection is connected to another dataset on the same page. With dynamic page datasets, you cannot filter by a reference field. You can also filter by a field used in another collection. To do so, choose Another dataset under Value source. Then choose another dataset that connects to the collection that has the field you want to filter and select the relevant field. Can I control the order in which the items display on my live site from my collection?Yes. You can enable the "Mirror on Site" feature to apply the order of your collection view to connected site elements. Keep in mind that any sorts added to datasets override the order set in the mirrored collection view. How can I sort my items in a more logical way when using a mixture of letters and numbers in a Text field type?When you're using a Text field type that contains both letters and numbers, the system applies an alphabetic sorting order. This means that Text field values are sorted in an alphabetic sequence. For example: 
P101 P120 P1200 P123While this is an expected behavior for an alphabetic sorting logic, you might prefer to sort these values in a numerical sequence.To achieve this, you can use a Number field type without any letters. By using a Text field type, the system will sort the same set of numbers as follows: 
101 120 123 1200This order aligns with a numerical sequence, offering a more intuitive understanding of your sorted data.Learn how to: 
Add sorts to a dataset to control the order of items on your live site.  Add sorts to your collection view to control the order of items in your collection. What happens if no collection items match my dataset filter criteria?If you add a filter to the dataset that returns no matching results from your collection, then the connected elements will not appear on the live site. After applying a dataset filter, the total number of items that can appear on the page displays next to Filter in the dataset settings. A zero appears if no items match the filter criteria.
articles.title: CMS: About Filtering and Sorting Live Site Content with Datasets
articles.html_content:
When you're managing CMS (Content Mangement System) content, it's important to keep things organized and make sure only the right items show up on your live site. You can do this by adding sorts and filters to your datasets. 

Keep in mind that filters and sorts you add to the dataset have no effect on how items appear in your CMS collection views. If you enable the "Mirror on Site" feature to use the collection's order on your live site, sorts you add to the dataset override the order from your mirrored collection.

In this guide, explore how you can use these tools to ensure your collection items are presented exactly as you intend.

Filter datasets for clarity

Filtering your dataset gives you precise control over which collection items appear on the connected site elements. It's like using a magnifying glass to focus on specific details within a collection that contains vast amounts of content. If you ever need to change or remove a filter, you can do it easily from the dataset settings. Here's how adding a filter to your dataset works:

Select the field: After adding the filter in the dataset settings, choose which collection field you want to filter by. Think of it as setting the criteria for your search.

Define the condition: Next, specify the condition that your filter should apply. Depending on the type of field, you can use conditions like "is," "Starts with," "Greater than," or "Equals." The options are tailored to suit the field type.

Set the Value: Finally, decide on the value that your filter should match. This could be a specific category, a numerical threshold, or even the logged-in user.
Learn how to add filters to your dataset to include or exclude items.

Combine filters for precision

You may need more than one filter to get really specific. Imagine you're curating a list of recipes, and you want to showcase French recipes that are not too difficult to complete. You could add a filter that includes only French recipes, and another that excludes advanced recipes. Only items that match the criteria of both filters will display in the dataset's connected repeater, gallery, or other elements. 
Learn more about using datasets to control your live site content. 

Sorting to reorder items

Sorting helps you put your collection items in a specific, logical order. It's like arranging your books on a shelf in alphabetical or date order. Here's how sorting in your dataset settings works:

Choose which field to sort: Start by picking which collection field you want to sort your items by. This field determines the basis for arranging your items. It could be something like the name of a recipe or the date it was created.

Decide the order: Decide on the order in which you want your items to appear. The field type you sort by determines the available sorting options. You can sort alphabetically, numerically, oldest to newest, true fields first, and vice versa for each option.
Notes:
  • Sorts also determine the order in which items load for navigational buttons connected to the dataset. Learn about the dataset click actions you can assign to buttons and images. 
  • Dataset sorts override the order in any collections in which you've enabled the "Mirror on Site" feature. However, dataset sorts do not affect the order in which items appear in your collection views.
Learn how to add sort conditions to datasets to control the order in which items display.

Sorting by multiple conditions

You can add multiple sort conditions for more advanced organization. With multiple sorts, the first condition is sorted first, followed by the second condition, and so on. This helps when you have multiple items that match your first sort condition and you want to further customize their order. 

For example, you may want to sort recipes by cuisine, then add another sort to keep them listed alphabetically by name within each cuisine group. To do so, add a sort for the cuisine field and a second sort for the recipe name. You can also add a collection field exclusively for sorting to create a custom order. 
Learn how to add fields to your CMS collection. 

FAQs

Click below for answers to common questions about filtering and sorting live site content. 

Can I hide fields in my collection to prevent them from appearing on the page?


Yes. In your collection settings, you can toggle on Control item visibility. This adds a new field in your collection where you can set individual items as "Hidden". These items do not get read by the dataset, so they cannot appear on your live site. With this feature, you can also set schedules that automatically show or hide collection items at specific dates and times.

Learn more about controlling item visibility from your collection itself.  

Keep in mind that hiding, showing, or reordering fields in your collection view, does not affect whether they can be connected to your page elements. 

Does filtering or sorting datasets affect my collection?


No. Adding filters or sorts to datasets affects item visibility and order on your connected page elements. It does not change anything in your collection itself. Learn how to manage your collection content. 

Does the dataset mode matter when filtering or sorting?


Yes. The dataset mode determines whether the dataset can read your collection content, write to your collection, or both. Your dataset needs to be in "Read" or "Read & Write" mode to read your collection items and apply filters or sort conditions. 

If your dataset is set to "Write" mode, it is meant to be used to connect user input elements to your collection for capturing visitor submissions. "Write" mode datasets cannot read your collection content, so they cannot display the content or apply filters or sorts. 

Learn more about dataset modes. 

Can I filter by a reference field or another dataset?


In a regular dataset, you can filter by a reference field, only if the referenced collection is connected to another dataset on the same page. With dynamic page datasets, you cannot filter by a reference field. 

You can also filter by a field used in another collection. To do so, choose Another dataset under Value source. Then choose another dataset that connects to the collection that has the field you want to filter and select the relevant field. 

Can I control the order in which the items display on my live site from my collection?


Yes. You can enable the "Mirror on Site" feature to apply the order of your collection view to connected site elements. Keep in mind that any sorts added to datasets override the order set in the mirrored collection view. 

How can I sort my items in a more logical way when using a mixture of letters and numbers in a Text field type?


When you're using a Text field type that contains both letters and numbers, the system applies an alphabetic sorting order. This means that Text field values are sorted in an alphabetic sequence. For example: 
  • P101
  • P120
  • P1200
  • P123

While this is an expected behavior for an alphabetic sorting logic, you might prefer to sort these values in a numerical sequence.

To achieve this, you can use a Number field type without any letters. By using a Text field type, the system will sort the same set of numbers as follows: 
  • 101
  • 120
  • 123
  • 1200

This order aligns with a numerical sequence, offering a more intuitive understanding of your sorted data.

Learn how to: 
  • Add sorts to a dataset to control the order of items on your live site. 
  • Add sorts to your collection view to control the order of items in your collection. 

What happens if no collection items match my dataset filter criteria?

If you add a filter to the dataset that returns no matching results from your collection, then the connected elements will not appear on the live site. 

After applying a dataset filter, the total number of items that can appear on the page displays next to Filter in the dataset settings. A zero appears if no items match the filter criteria.

question: How can I view my blog's analytics using the Wix app?
answer:
To access Blog Analytics in the Wix app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the [Wix app](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-owner-app-an-overview).
2. Tap **Manage** at the bottom right.
3. Tap **Blog**.
4. Tap **Analytics**.
5. See an overview of your blog's statistics for the selected time period (7 days, 4 weeks, or 3 months):
   
   * **Posts Views:** Shows the overall number of views for all posts.
   * **Unique Posts Views:** Shows the number of different people who visited your blog. Each visitor is counted once, even if they've seen your blog multiple times during the selected timeframe.
   * **Shares:** Shows the number of times your posts were shared in the selected time period.
   * **Site Visits:** Shows the total amount of visits made to your site. The same visitor can be counted multiple times if they visit your site more than once.
6. Check how your most recent post is doing:
   
   * **Views:** Shows the total number of post views, including multiple views by the same reader.
   * **Unique views:** Shows how many people have viewed your post. A reader who views your post multiple times in the defined time period is counted once.
   * **Likes:** The number of times a reader clicked "like" on the post
   * **Shares:** The number of times the post was shared.
7. See your three most popular posts and tap **Post Analytics** for in-depth information about each one.

### Tip
Tap the drop-down at the top to change the selected time frame.

question: How can I add a tax rate to my bookings in Wix Hotels?
answer:
To add a tax rate to your prices in Wix Hotels, follow these steps:

1. Go to your [Hotels Dashboard](https://support.wix.com/en/article/accessing-your-wix-hotels-dashboard).
2. Click the **Payments** tab.
3. Scroll down to **Price Settings**.
4. Enter the tax rate you want to add to your prices in the **Tax** field.
5. Click **Save** at the bottom.

Note that Wix Hotels displays prices without the tax added until a customer selects a room and dates of stay, then the tax is included in the final price breakdown of the reservation. If you want tax included in the initial room prices, build the tax in when you set up your rates instead of using the tax field in Price Settings.

question: How can I add additional meta tags to a page on my Wix site to use Pinterest Rich Pins?
answer:
To add additional meta tags to a page on your Wix site for Pinterest Rich Pins, follow these steps:

### Using Wix Editor:
1. [Go to your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26).
2. Click **Pages & Menu** on the left side of the editor.
3. Click the **More Actions** icon next to the relevant page.
4. Click **SEO basics**.
5. Click the **Advanced SEO** tab.
6. Click **+ Add New Tag** under **Meta Tags**.
7. Add your meta tag code in the **HTML Code** field.
8. Click **Apply**.

### Using Studio Editor:
1. [Go to your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26).
2. Click **Pages** on the left side of the editor.
3. Click the **More Actions** icon next to the relevant page.
4. Click **SEO Basics**.
5. Click the **Advanced SEO** tab.
6. Click **+ Add New Tag** under **Meta Tags**.
7. Add your meta tag code in the **HTML Code** field.
8. Click **Apply**.

### Tip
Make sure to check [Pinterest's guidelines](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/web-features/rich-pins-overview/) on how this metadata should be written.

answer:
To restrict access to your store pages using the Wix Editor, follow these steps:

1. [Go to your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26).
2. Click **Pages & Menu** on the left side of the editor.
3. Choose the page you want to restrict:
   - **Category Page or Shop Page:**
     1. Click **Store Pages**.
     2. Click **Category Page** or **Shop**.
   - **A site page with a Product Gallery:**
     1. Click **Site Menu**.
     2. Click the page with the Product Gallery you want to restrict.
4. Click the **Settings** or **More Actions** icon on the page.
5. (For Gallery Pages only) Click **Settings**.
6. Click the **Permissions** tab.
7. Set a permission level:
   - **Password holders:** Only visitors with the password can access the page.
     1. Enter the password.
   - **Members only:**
     1. Select Members only.
     2. Select which of your members can access the page:
        - All members: Anyone who signs up to become a site member can access the page.
        - Only selected members or paying customers:
          - **Select from your Member Roles:** Click the **Edit** icon to select a member role. [Learn more about roles and permissions](https://support.wix.com/en/article/roles-permissions-overview)

question: How can I connect Clearpay as a payment provider on my Wix site?
answer:
To connect Clearpay as a payment provider on your Wix site, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Accept Payments](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Set%20Up%20Payments&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/payments/) in your site's dashboard.

   **Tip:** Check your business location at the top right. If incorrect, click the drop-down menu to change it.

2. Click **See More Payment Options**.
3. Click **Connect** next to Clearpay.
4. Depending on whether you have an account with Clearpay, or need to create a new one, follow the steps:

   **Have an account**
   1. Enter your Merchant ID and Secret Key.
   2. Click **Connect**.

   **Don't have a Clearpay account**
   1. Click [**Create Clearpay account**](https://get.clearpay.co.uk/).
   2. Register for a Clearpay merchant account.
   3. Once your merchant account is approved, you will be provided with your unique Merchant ID and Secret Key.
   4. Return to the [Accept Payments tab](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Set%20Up%20Payments&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/payments/) (repeat steps 1-4) and follow the steps under Have an account to connect your account.

Once connected, you need to have your account successfully verified to receive payouts.

In order to accept online payments, you must connect a payment provider. For Clearpay, follow the steps above to accept online payments.

Once connected, you need to have your account successfully verified to receive payouts.

Is my currency supported?

Be aware that payments will fail If you are using an unsupported currency. 
The currency used in your payment provider account must match the currency that you set in your Wix account. If you need to change the currency set in your provider account, please contact your payment provider.

If your current payment provider does not support your desired currency, Wix hosts a wide range of alternative payment providers. Learn how to change your payment provider.

What is a minimum payment amount?

Some payment providers have a minimum payment threshold (e.g. $1.01). Payments below this amount will not be processed.

Make sure that all of your products or services are priced over the minimum threshold. This includes discounted items or Pricing Plans. 

Please contact your payment provider to get the most up-to-date information about their minimum payment threshold. 

Can I offer recurring payments?

To offer recurring payments, you must connect a payment provider that supports recurring payments.

How do I get my payouts?

Payouts are managed by your payment provider. If your provider is a third-party provider, contact them directly. If your provider is Wix Payments, learn about receiving payouts from Wix Payments.

My customers' payments are being declined. What can I do?

If your customers are experiencing payment failures, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting issues for accepting payments.

Why can’t I connect my desired payment provider?

If you’re having trouble connecting your payment provider, you may be able to fix the issue by troubleshooting common connection issues.

Do I need to upgrade my site to accept payments?

Yes. You need to upgrade your site to a plan that supports payments in order to accept payments.

question: How can I add an app to my Wix site using the Wix app?
answer:
To add an app to your site using the Wix app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
2. Tap the **Manage** icon ![](https://d2x3xhvgiqkx42.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/8769cf44-f342-494c-b25f-cc98c9da3e82/2021/04/12/3fc0f98c-0997-47b3-b7bd-6ae31a67e078/ce9c0fe5-f60d-4448-8fc2-9ba4cf636f93.png).

   * [**Online Programs**](https://support.wix.com/en/article/online-programs-managing-your-program-in-the-wix-owner-app): Create step-by-step training programs for your clients.
   * [**Shared Gallery**](https://support.wix.com/en/article/the-shared-gallery-app-an-overview): Let your members upload photos and videos to albums in a shared place.
