question: How can I fix elements that appear in the wrong location on my Wix mobile site?
answer:
If elements you have added to your page in the desktop editor are placed differently on the mobile version of your site, you can manually rearrange these elements by dragging them to your chosen location. If an element appears on the menu, header, or footer of a mobile site, it is not possible to click and drag it around the page. However, you can use the right-click menu to [move these elements](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-moving-elements-between-the-mobile-menu-header-and-footer) between the menu, header, and footer.

### Tip
When placing an item in the gap between elements, you may need to adjust the spacing. Use the [Auto Space on Drag tool](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-using-the-mobile-editor-tools#using-the-auto-space-on-drag-tool) to automatically create even spaces between the elements.

articles.title: Wix Editor: Troubleshooting Layout Issues on Your Mobile Site
articles.html_content:
Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly site for you using the content and elements from your desktop site. They are not different sites, just different views of the same site.
As your mobile site gets automatically optimized to fit smaller screens, you may notice alignment or structural issues. This guide will help you resolve such problems.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Elements appearing in the wrong place
  • Gaps on your mobile site
  • Elements hidden from the mobile site

Elements appearing in the wrong location

Elements you have added to your page in the desktop editor may be placed differently on the mobile version of your site. You can manually rearrange these elements by dragging them to your chosen location.
If an element appears on the menu, header, or footer of a mobile site, it is not possible to click and drag it around the page. However, you can use the right-click menu to move these elements between the menu, header and footer.
Tip:
When placing an item in the gap between elements, you may need to adjust the spacing. Use the Auto Space on Drag tool to automatically create even spaces between the elements. 

Gaps on the mobile site

You may notice gaps on your mobile site. Our mobile algorithm "translates" desktop content for mobile but it's not always perfect, and can sometimes lead to gaps on your mobile site. 
Depending on where the gaps are, you may be able to remove them by make the element smaller, or by shortening the page length.
Tip:
The Spacing Guide tool shows you the existing gaps on your section (in pixels). It also shows an indication when these gaps are equal to one another. 

Elements hidden from the mobile site

When editing your mobile site, you may notice that you can't find some elements that appear on desktop. This is because some elements are automatically hidden from your mobile site in order to make it more suitable for mobile devices. 
Check which elements have been hidden from your mobile site, and unhide if needed, from the Hidden on Mobile panel.
Did you know?
You can hide desktop elements from your mobile site, and replace them with mobile-only elements. Create a personalized experience that accurately reflects your brand or business on mobile.

question: What are the limitations of the Wix Music Player and how can I set it up on my site?

- **Single:** Up to 5 tracks per single.
- **Playlist:** Up to 500 tracks per playlist.

question: How can I show or hide the number of participants in my online program using the Wix Editor?
answer:
To show or hide the number of participants in your online program using the Wix Editor, follow these steps:

1. [Go to your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26).
2. Click **Pages & Menu** on the left side of the editor.
3. Click **Program Pages**.
4. Select the relevant program page.

   **Note:** The Program List page and Visitor Page automatically sync the setting that shows or hides the number of participants. Showing or hiding the number of participants in one of these pages also applies the change to the other page.

5. Click the relevant program element on your page.
6. Click **Settings**.
7. Click the **Display** tab.
8. Click the **Participants** toggle to change the visibility of the number of participants in your program:
   
   * **Enabled:** The number of program participants is displayed on your live site.
   * **Disabled:** The number of program participants is not displayed on your live site.
9. Publish your site when you're ready to make the change go live.

### Tip

articles.title: Wix Bookings: Viewing Booking Form Responses
articles.html_content:
When clients book a service on desktop, they fill out their details in your booking form, like the one below. For your convenience, there are a few different ways to view client responses to your form.
Note:
Clients who book services through a member app on mobile do not fill out the booking form. 
In this article, learn more about viewing form responses:
  • In emails
  • In the Booking Calendar
  • In a client's contact info page
  • In the Wix app
Tip:
You can export a report showing clients who booked during a specific time period (e.g. a list of all clients who attended classes during a particular week).

Viewing responses in emails

When a client books a service, Wix sends an email to the address you set in the General Info tab in Wix Bookings. This email contains the information your client filled out in the booking form, including responses to custom fields (e.g. dog's name).

Viewing responses in the Booking Calendar

A quick and easy way to see your responses is on your Bookings Calendar. This lets you view all your clients' bookings and choose the one you want to view in more detail.

To view clients responses in the Booking Calendar:

  1. Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard.
  2. Choose what you want to do:

View appointment responses

  1. Click the relevant appointment in your calendar.
  2. View the response details next to the Booking Form icon .

View class or course responses

  1. Click the relevant class or course in your calendar.
  2. Click Manage next to the participants.
  3. Click the Booking Form icon  next to the relevant client. 

Viewing responses in your contacts' info

Your site's Contact List displays all the site visitors who interacted with your site in any way (e.g. booked a service, contacted you on chat, subscribed to your newsletter, etc.). You can find your contacts' responses from your booking form in each client's contact info.

To view responses on a client's contact info page:

  1. Go to Contact List in your site's dashboard.
  2. Hover over the relevant contact and click View.
  1. Click the Bookings tab.
  2. Click the Booking Form icon next to the relevant booking. 

Viewing responses from the Wix app

Clients who book a service using one of the Wix member apps do not fill out a booking form. You can, however, use the Wix app to view responses from clients who booked on desktop. 

To view client responses from the Wix app:

  1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
  2. Tap Manage  at the bottom.
  3. Tap Bookings under Business.
  4. Choose what you want to do:

View appointment responses

  1. Tap the relevant appointment.
  2. Scroll down and view the responses in the More Information section. 

View class or course responses

  1. Tap the relevant session.
  2. Tap the Manage Participants button.
  3. Tap a participant's name.
  4. Tap View Form Responses.
Tip:
You can also view form responses by tapping the participants name, then tapping View Booking Details.

question: What are the recommended guidelines for choosing accessible fonts on a Wix site?
answer:
When adding text and fonts to your Wix site, it is important to follow these accessibility guidelines:

- **Choose a font** that has a balance between character ambiguity and character complexity. Characters should be easily distinguished from each other, but also have simple patterns and shapes.
- **Use a limited number of fonts** on your site, and avoid having multiple typefaces in the same block of text.
- **Avoid small font sizes** where possible. We recommend keeping your text at 14 pixels and above.
- **Ensure sufficient spacing** between characters, words, and lines to prevent text from being compacted and difficult to read.
- **Be cautious with formatted text** such as italics, all caps, and strikethrough, as they can be more difficult to read for visitors with visual and reading impairments.
- **Consider color contrast** between your text and background, especially when using lightweight fonts. [Learn more about color contrast](https://support.wix.com/en/article/accessibility-preparing-your-text-and-graphics)
- **Align text to the left**, as justified text contains spacing variations that can impact readability.
- **Include empty space** between and around text blocks and paragraphs to ensure they can be easily read and distinguished.
- **Maintain line length** between 50 and 120 characters where possible to enhance readability.

For further steps, you can refer to the [Accessibility Checklist](https://support.wix.com/en/article/accessibility-checklist-for-improving-your-sites-accessibility) to continue improving your site's accessibility.

Keep in mind that formatted text such as italics, all caps, and strikethrough can be more difficult to read for visitors with visual and reading impairments.

Text blocks and paragraphs should contain empty space between and around them to ensure they can be easily read and distinguished.
Having too many or too few characters in a line can impact readability. We recommend keeping your line length between 50 and 120 characters where possible. Next step:Go back to the Accessibility Checklist to continue improving your site for accessibility.

question: How does the iOS 15 update affect the opened email statistics in email marketing campaigns?
answer:
With iOS 15, Apple device owners who have set up the Apple Mail app receive a prompt to choose "Protect Mail activity" or "Don't protect Mail activity". When Apple device owners choose “Protect Mail activity”, the Apple Mail app downloads emails received when the app is opened. For a marketing email, this automatic download is counted in campaign statistics as an email being opened. These false positive results increase the following statistics: 
* Opened email
* Open rate
* Recipients who opened your campaign
* Recipients that did not open your email statistics.

articles.contents:
Email Marketing: iOS 15 Update and Your Campaign Statistics
In 2021, Apple released iOS 15, which includes Mail Privacy Protection for the Apple Mail app. This feature has significant impact on email marketing campaign statistics. Read more about the iOS 15 release from Apple. In this article, learn more about: 
Changes to opened email statistics Tracking the success of email campaignsChanges to opened email statisticsGlobally, around 40% of emails are viewed using Apple Mail on Apple mobile and desktop devices. With iOS 15, Apple device owners who have set up the Apple Mail app receive a prompt to choose "Protect Mail activity" or "Don't protect Mail activity". When Apple device owners choose “Protect Mail activity”, the Apple Mail app downloads emails received when the app is opened. For a marketing email, this automatic download is counted in campaign statistics as an email being opened. These false positive results increase the following statistics:
Opened email  Open rate Recipients who opened your campaign Recipients that did not open your email statisticsTracking the success of email campaignsOpened statistics won't offer a true representation of the success of an email marketing campaign after the iOS 15 update.To track the success of your campaigns, review your Clicked statistics. Your Click rate shows how many recipients showed interest by engaging with your email. You can encourage your contacts to engage with your emails by adding a button with a clear Call To Action (CTA), such as “Shop Now” or “Order Online”.
articles.title: Email Marketing: iOS 15 Update and Your Campaign Statistics
articles.html_content:
In 2021, Apple released iOS 15, which includes Mail Privacy Protection for the Apple Mail app. This feature has significant impact on email marketing campaign statistics. Read more about the iOS 15 release from Apple. 
In this article, learn more about: 
  • Changes to opened email statistics
  • Tracking the success of email campaigns

Changes to opened email statistics

Globally, around 40% of emails are viewed using Apple Mail on Apple mobile and desktop devices. With iOS 15, Apple device owners who have set up the Apple Mail app receive a prompt to choose "Protect Mail activity" or "Don't protect Mail activity". 
When Apple device owners choose “Protect Mail activity”, the Apple Mail app downloads emails received when the app is opened. For a marketing email, this automatic download is counted in campaign statistics as an email being opened. These false positive results increase the following statistics:
  • Opened email 
  • Open rate
  • Recipients who opened your campaign
  • Recipients that did not open your email statistics

Tracking the success of email campaigns

Opened statistics won't offer a true representation of the success of an email marketing campaign after the iOS 15 update.
To track the success of your campaigns, review your Clicked statistics. Your Click rate shows how many recipients showed interest by engaging with your email. You can encourage your contacts to engage with your emails by adding a button with a clear Call To Action (CTA), such as “Shop Now” or “Order Online”.

question: How can I replace an image in my email marketing campaign template using Wix?
answer:
To replace an image in your email marketing campaign template using Wix, follow these steps:

1. Go to [Email Marketing](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Email%20Marketing%20Dashboard&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D/shoutout/) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **Edit** next to an existing campaign or [create a new one](https://support.wix.com/en/article/email-marketing-creating-a-new-campaign).
3. Select the relevant image in your campaign.
4. Click **Change Image**.
5. Select an image from:
   * **Site Files:** Images that you've uploaded to your site. Click **Upload Media** to upload a new image.
   * **Media from Wix:** Free images available for you to use. Browse through the available images using the categories on the left or the search bar on the right.
   * **Shutterstock Images:** Images available for purchase. Select an image and click **Buy Image** to purchase it.
6. Click **Add to Page**.
7. (Optional) Choose from the following options, then click **Apply**:
   * **Edit:** Use the [Wix Photo Studio tools](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-media-using-the-wix-photo-studio-tools) to enhance and improve the image.
   * **Add a link:** Enable the toggle and enter the URL you want to link the image to.
   * **Design:** Use the sliders to adjust the padding around the image.

### Note
Email campaign images have a width of 700 pixels. If you replace the template image with a wider image, it resizes to 700 pixel width. Smaller images retain their original size.

### Tip
Learn more about [modifying your email campaign template](https://support.wix.com/en/article/adding-elements-to-your-email-campaign).

question: How can I set up a webhook in Wix Automations to send data to a specific URL?
answer:
To connect automations with a webhook in Wix, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Automations](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Open%20Wix%20Automations&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D/triggers/) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **+ New Automation** in the top right corner.
3. Click **+ Start from Scratch** or choose a suggested automation.
4. Click the title to give your automation a name.
5. Select a trigger for your automation.
6. Choose **Send via webhook** as your automation's action.
   1. Enter the URL the webhook should send a notification to under **Target URL**. Every time your automation is triggered (e.g., a customer fills out a form on your site), the webhook sends data to the URL you've specified.
   2. Choose whether the webhook should send all available data to the URL or only certain data:
      * **All keys and values:** All data from the trigger is sent to the target URL. For example, if the trigger is Wix Forms, the webhook sends data from every form field.
         
         **Tip:** Click **View Structure** to see all the data that the webhook will send. When you're done, click **Got It**.
      * **Customize structure:** Only specific data is sent to the target URL. For example, if your trigger is Wix Forms, you might only want to send the Name and Email fields.
         
         1. Click **Customize structure** next to **Add your own keys and values**.
         2. Enter a key name in the **Key** field. This helps you distinguish what data is sent.
         3. Click **Insert Variable** next to **Value** to choose the data that should match the key.
         4. (Optional) Click **+ Add Key-Value** to add another row and match key names to data.
         
         **Note:** If you choose not to map a specific key to a value, the webhook will notify the URL without any additional information from the trigger.
         5. When you're done, click **Save**.
7. Click the **Timing** drop-down to select a timing for your automation.
8. Click **Activate** or **Save**.

Send automation data to a third-party app or to your own web server using a webhook. Webhooks are a way for apps that aren't connected to send messages and information to one another in real-time. Every time your automation is triggered (e.g. a customer fills out a form on your site) the webhook sends data to the URL you've specified. All keys and values: All data from the trigger is sent to the target URL. For example, if the trigger is Wix Forms, the webhook sends data from every form field.
Tip: Click View Structure to see all the data that the webhook will send. When you're done, click Got It. Customize structure: Only specific data is sent to the target URL. For example, if your trigger is Wix Forms you might only want to send the Name and Email fields.
        
Click Customize structure next to Add your own keys and values. Enter a key name in the Key field. This helps you distinguish what data is sent. Click Insert Variable next to Value to choose the data that should match the key. (Optional) Click + Add Key-Value to add another row and match key names to data.
Note: If you choose not to map a specific key to a value, the webhook will notify the URL without any additional information from the trigger. When you're done, click Save.     Click the Timing drop-down to select a timing for your automation. Click Activate or Save.

question: How can I resolve the 'Default mail client is not properly installed' error message when clicking an email link on my website?
answer:
If you receive the error message: **"Default mail client is not properly installed,"** you need to set a default mail client in your browser's settings. This issue occurs when you click an email link from your live site if you do not have a defined default mail client for your device. 

To avoid this issue, it is recommended to display your email address on your site and [use a contact form](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-forms-adding-and-setting-up-a-form-on-your-site). This issue is localized to your computer and should not affect your visitors unless they have also not set up a default mail client.

articles.contents:
Troubleshooting Error Message: Default Mail Client Is Not Properly Installed
If you receive the error message: "Default mail client is not properly installed," you are experiencing a local issue related to the email configuration of your browser or computer. This issue occurs when you click an email link from your live site if you do not have a defined default mail client for your device.  To resolve this issue, make sure you've set a default mail client in your browser's settings.Important:This issue is localized to your computer and should not affect your visitors unless they have also not set up a default mail client. If you haven't set up a mail client on your device, you will experience this issue when clicking "mailto:" links on any websites (not just Wix sites). To avoid this issue, we recommend displaying your email address on your site and using a contact form.
articles.title: Troubleshooting Error Message: Default Mail Client Is Not Properly Installed
articles.html_content:
If you receive the error message: "Default mail client is not properly installed," you are experiencing a local issue related to the email configuration of your browser or computer. 

This issue occurs when you click an email link from your live site if you do not have a defined default mail client for your device.  
To resolve this issue, make sure you've set a default mail client in your browser's settings.
Important:
This issue is localized to your computer and should not affect your visitors unless they have also not set up a default mail client. If you haven't set up a mail client on your device, you will experience this issue when clicking "mailto:" links on any websites (not just Wix sites). 

To avoid this issue, we recommend displaying your email address on your site and using a contact form.

question: How can I delete my Wix account using the Wix app?
answer:
To delete your account using the Wix app, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
2. Tap your profile icon at the top.
3. Tap **Manage Account Settings**.
4. Tap **Delete Your Account**.
5. Tap **Continue** to follow the steps on how to delete your account.

Once you delete your account, you can no longer use any of your Wix services. Your account and all its data will be removed permanently. **Important:** Wix will not be able to restore your account or retrieve your data in the future.

articles.title: Wix App: Deleting Your Account
articles.html_content:
From the Wix app, you can delete your entire account and any sites that belong to your account.
In this article, learn more about: 
  • Deleting your account
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs) 

Deleting your account

Once you delete your account, you can no longer use any of your Wix services. Your account and all its data will be removed permanently. 
Important:
Wix will not be able to restore your account or retrieve your data in the future.

To delete your account:

  1. Go to your site in the Wix app.
  2. Tap your profile icon at the top.
  3. Tap Manage Account Settings.
  4. Tap Delete Your Account. 
  5. Tap Continue to follow the steps on how to delete your account. 

FAQs

Click the questions below to learn more.

Why might I want to delete my account?

Sites can contain a lot of personal data, identity details, credit card numbers, and more. In some cases, you may not use these accounts any longer. With privacy in mind, it is a good idea to remove private data from services that are no longer used.

How long will it take for my account to be removed after I send a request to delete it?

Your account will be deleted by Wix Customer Care experts up to 7 days from the request.

What if I dont have any sites in my account?

If you don't have a website and choose to remove your account, your Wix account will be removed. You will not be able to log in to the Wix apps with that account any longer.

How do my members delete their account?

Members can request that their account is deleted. This fully removes them from the member apps and means they can no longer visit sites from the different apps. 

Can I delete a specific site only?

Yes, you can move a site to the trash from the Wix app if you no longer want it. Learn how to delete a site.

question: How can I import blog posts from one Wix site to another?
answer:
To import blog posts from one Wix site to another, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Blog](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20My%20Blog&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D/blog) in the dashboard of the site you want to transfer posts to.
2. Click the **More Actions** drop-down at the top right.
3. Click **Import posts**.
4. Select **Wix** and click **Next**.
5. Click **Get Started**.
6. Select the site you want to import the content from. 

   **Note:** You only see the sites that have Wix Blog installed.
7. Click **Next**.
8. Select the checkbox to confirm that you own or are licensed to use this content.
9. Click **Import Posts**. 

   **Note:** Once you start the import process, there is no way to cancel it.
10. Wait for the import to finish.

articles.contents:
Wix Blog: Importing Blog Posts from Another Wix Site
You can import blog posts from one Wix site to another. This is a great way to merge content from multiple blogs into one blog. This is particularly beneficial if you have an old Wix site filled with valuable posts that you'd hate to lose. Instead of leaving those posts unused on an inactive site, you can import them to your active blog. This way, you ensure that all your hard work continues to engage readers and drive traffic.Important:
In this article we refer to two different sites, your source site and your destination site. Your source site is the site you want to transfer content from, and your destination site is the site you want to transfer content to. Your destination site must be in the same Wix account as your source site. Your destination site must have Wix Blog already installed.In this article, learn more about:
Importing blog posts FAQ'sImporting blog posts from another Wix siteFrom your destination site's dashboard, you can import posts from your source site. To import blog posts:
Go to Blog in the dashboard of the site you want to transfer posts to. Click the More Actions drop-down at the top right. Click Import posts.                                             
Select Wix and click Next.  Click Get Started. Select the site you want to import the content from.  
Note: You only see the sites that have Wix Blog installed.  Click Next.  Select the checkbox to confirm that you own or are licensed to use this content. Click Import Posts.  
Note: Once you start the import process, there is no way to cancel it. Wait for the import to finish. FAQ'sWe've compiled a list of some of the main FAQ's about the import process.Who can move the blog posts between sites? To import posts, you need to be an Owner/Admin on the source site and at least a Blog Editor on the destination site.What is imported?The following features are imported:
All published posts: Only published posts are imported. Once they are imported they are automatically published in your destination site. Each published post includes the original formatting, settings, images, and videos.  Categories, tags and authors: These are all taken from your source site and copied to your destination site.  Likes and view count: Likes and views are copied with your posts. Multilingual settings: All translated content transfers if you have the same languages on both sites.  What is not imported?Draft posts, scheduled posts, and deleted posts are not imported.The following features are also not imported:
Analytics: Only likes and view counts are imported from the source site.  Comments: Comments on blog posts are not imported from the source site. Members: Members are not imported from the source site. Subscription plans: Connected plans are not imported from the source site.Will my existing posts be deleted?No, your existing posts won’t be deleted from your source site. Is there a risk of duplicating posts with the transfer?No, there will be no duplication of posts. We check if the post has already been imported, if it has, we will not import again. Is there a limit to the amount of posts I can transfer?Currently, the maximum amount of posts that can transfer is 5,000. How many video hours can I import?If you want more than 30 minutes of video on the destination site, then you need to upgrade to Premium. Learn how many video hours you can upload with different Premium plans. How long does the process take?It might take several minutes to import all your posts. The time it takes depends on how much data (posts, image, videos) need to be imported. My blog has more than one author. Do I need to do something special?If you have more than one author in your source blog, then they are also added in the destination blog, but they won't have any permissions. You can manage the permissions your writers have in the Blog section of the dashboard. Learn more about blog writer roles.What about my SEO?After you import posts, you can set up 301 redirects from the old posts to the new ones. 301 redirects tell search engines that the URL of a page in your site has changed and where they can find the new page.Wix does not automatically create a 301 redirect for each post during the import. Instead, we suggest you set up 301 redirects for each post when you’re ready.If you change the URL for a blog post in the destination site, the new URL is treated as a brand-new page by search engines and your old URL will no longer work. Any links to the old URL will stop working and the SEO rankings for that page will be lost. My source site has Wix Multilingual, what can I do?If your source site had Wix Multilingual, then your destination site should also have Wix Multilingual installed in order to migrate all your localized content.
articles.title: Wix Blog: Importing Blog Posts from Another Wix Site
articles.html_content:
You can import blog posts from one Wix site to another. This is a great way to merge content from multiple blogs into one blog. 
This is particularly beneficial if you have an old Wix site filled with valuable posts that you'd hate to lose. Instead of leaving those posts unused on an inactive site, you can import them to your active blog. This way, you ensure that all your hard work continues to engage readers and drive traffic.
Important:
  • In this article we refer to two different sites, your source site and your destination site. Your source site is the site you want to transfer content from, and your destination site is the site you want to transfer content to.
  • Your destination site must be in the same Wix account as your source site.
  • Your destination site must have Wix Blog already installed.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Importing blog posts
  • FAQ's

Importing blog posts from another Wix site

From your destination site's dashboard, you can import posts from your source site. 

To import blog posts:

  1. Go to Blog in the dashboard of the site you want to transfer posts to.
  2. Click the More Actions drop-down at the top right.
  3. Click Import posts.                                             
  1. Select Wix and click Next. 
  2. Click Get Started.
  3. Select the site you want to import the content from. 
    Note: You only see the sites that have Wix Blog installed. 
  4. Click Next. 
  5. Select the checkbox to confirm that you own or are licensed to use this content.
  6. Click Import Posts. 
    Note: Once you start the import process, there is no way to cancel it.
  7. Wait for the import to finish. 

FAQ's

We've compiled a list of some of the main FAQ's about the import process.

Who can move the blog posts between sites?

To import posts, you need to be an Owner/Admin on the source site and at least a Blog Editor on the destination site.

What is imported?

The following features are imported:
  • All published posts: Only published posts are imported. Once they are imported they are automatically published in your destination site. Each published post includes the original formatting, settings, images, and videos. 
  • Categories, tags and authors: These are all taken from your source site and copied to your destination site. 
  • Likes and view count: Likes and views are copied with your posts.
  • Multilingual settings: All translated content transfers if you have the same languages on both sites.  

What is not imported?

Draft posts, scheduled posts, and deleted posts are not imported.

The following features are also not imported:
  • Analytics: Only likes and view counts are imported from the source site. 
  • Comments: Comments on blog posts are not imported from the source site.
  • Members: Members are not imported from the source site.
  • Subscription plans: Connected plans are not imported from the source site.

Will my existing posts be deleted?

No, your existing posts won’t be deleted from your source site. 

Is there a risk of duplicating posts with the transfer?

No, there will be no duplication of posts. We check if the post has already been imported, if it has, we will not import again. 

Is there a limit to the amount of posts I can transfer?

Currently, the maximum amount of posts that can transfer is 5,000. 

How many video hours can I import?

If you want more than 30 minutes of video on the destination site, then you need to upgrade to Premium. Learn how many video hours you can upload with different Premium plans. 

How long does the process take?

It might take several minutes to import all your posts. The time it takes depends on how much data (posts, image, videos) need to be imported. 

My blog has more than one author. Do I need to do something special?

If you have more than one author in your source blog, then they are also added in the destination blog, but they won't have any permissions. You can manage the permissions your writers have in the Blog section of the dashboard. Learn more about blog writer roles.

What about my SEO?

After you import posts, you can set up 301 redirects from the old posts to the new ones. 301 redirects tell search engines that the URL of a page in your site has changed and where they can find the new page.

Wix does not automatically create a 301 redirect for each post during the import. Instead, we suggest you set up 301 redirects for each post when you’re ready.

If you change the URL for a blog post in the destination site, the new URL is treated as a brand-new page by search engines and your old URL will no longer work. Any links to the old URL will stop working and the SEO rankings for that page will be lost. 

My source site has Wix Multilingual, what can I do?

If your source site had Wix Multilingual, then your destination site should also have Wix Multilingual installed in order to migrate all your localized content.

question: How can I unsubscribe from an email campaign mailing list?
answer:
To unsubscribe from an email campaign mailing list, follow these steps:

1. Go to the email campaign in your inbox and scroll to the bottom.
2. Click **click here** in the sentence: "If you feel you received it by mistake or wish to unsubscribe, please click here."
3. Click the **Unsubscribe** button that opens in a new tab to confirm you want to unsubscribe.

After confirming, the recipient's status changes to "Unsubscribed" in your Contacts list, ensuring the contact does not receive future emails from your campaigns.

articles.contents:
Email Marketing: About the Unsubscribe Link in Your Email Campaign
Every email campaign must include an opt-out option that is clearly visible to subscribers. For this reason, an "unsubscribe" link at the bottom of the email is automatically included and cannot be removed or edited. Recipients who no longer want to receive emails from you can click the unsubscribe link to be removed from your mailing list. In your dashboard, you can view contacts by their subscription status to see who has unsubscribed. Important:Do not add your own unsubscribe link to your email campaign as this can cause it to get declined. Unsubscribing from an email campaign mailing listWhen recipients open your email in their mailbox, they can click a link at the bottom to unsubscribe. A new tab opens where the recipient can click "Unsubscribe" to confirm that they want to be removed from your mailing list. After confirming, the recipient's status changes to "Unsubscribed" in your Contacts list. This ensures the contact does not receive future emails from your campaigns. To unsubscribe from an email campaign mailing list: 
Go to the email campaign in your inbox and scroll to the bottom. Click click here in the sentence: "If you feel you received it by mistake or wish to unsubscribe, please click here."
Click the Unsubscribe button that opens in a new tab to confirm you want to unsubscribe.Viewing contacts who unsubscribedView which recipients have unsubscribed from your mailing list in the Contacts section of your site's dashboard. You can filter your contacts by subscription status: Subscribed or Unsubscribed.To view your unsubscribed contacts: 
Go to Contacts in your site's dashboard. Click the Filter by: drop-down at the top of the list. Scroll down and click Unsubscribed under Subscribed Status.Note:If you are previewing or testing emails, the unsubscribe link will lead to this article rather than the unsubscribe flow. Once you publish and send to recipients, however, the unsubscribe link works as normal.Troubleshooting issues with your unsubscribe linkIf you are experiencing issues with the unsubscribe link (the link doesn't appear or doesn't work) try the following troubleshooting steps:Step 1 | Check if the link was in a test emailIf you send a test campaign, the unsubscribe link leads to this article rather than to a real unsubscribe link. If you send a real campaign the link should work.Step 2 | Make sure you're clicking both unsubscribe links When you click the unsubscribe link from your inbox a new tab opens, which includes an unsubscribe button. You must click this unsubscribe button to complete the process of unsubscribing from the campaign.  Follow the steps in the 1st section of this article above to click both unsubscribe links and complete the process. Step 3 | Test the link in a mail client other than Microsoft OutlookSometimes Microsoft Outlook blocks the unsubscribe links. To test if Microsoft Outlook is causing the issue:
Open the email campaign in a different mail client such as Gmail.  Follow the steps in the 1st section of this article above to unsubscribe. Note:The unsubscribe text at the bottom of your email campaigns is written in the language of the associated Wix account. To change the language, change your account language. If you change the language, the unsubscribe text changes for future campaigns only. All past campaigns still show the original language.
articles.title: Email Marketing: About the Unsubscribe Link in Your Email Campaign
articles.html_content:
Every email campaign must include an opt-out option that is clearly visible to subscribers. For this reason, an "unsubscribe" link at the bottom of the email is automatically included and cannot be removed or edited. 

Recipients who no longer want to receive emails from you can click the unsubscribe link to be removed from your mailing list. In your dashboard, you can view contacts by their subscription status to see who has unsubscribed. 
Important:
Do not add your own unsubscribe link to your email campaign as this can cause it to get declined. 

Unsubscribing from an email campaign mailing list

When recipients open your email in their mailbox, they can click a link at the bottom to unsubscribe. A new tab opens where the recipient can click "Unsubscribe" to confirm that they want to be removed from your mailing list. After confirming, the recipient's status changes to "Unsubscribed" in your Contacts list. This ensures the contact does not receive future emails from your campaigns. 

To unsubscribe from an email campaign mailing list:

  1. Go to the email campaign in your inbox and scroll to the bottom.
  2. Click click here in the sentence: "If you feel you received it by mistake or wish to unsubscribe, please click here."
  1. Click the Unsubscribe button that opens in a new tab to confirm you want to unsubscribe.

Viewing contacts who unsubscribed

View which recipients have unsubscribed from your mailing list in the Contacts section of your site's dashboard. You can filter your contacts by subscription status: Subscribed or Unsubscribed.

To view your unsubscribed contacts:

  1. Go to Contacts in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click the Filter by: drop-down at the top of the list.
  3. Scroll down and click Unsubscribed under Subscribed Status.
Note:
If you are previewing or testing emails, the unsubscribe link will lead to this article rather than the unsubscribe flow. Once you publish and send to recipients, however, the unsubscribe link works as normal.

Troubleshooting issues with your unsubscribe link

If you are experiencing issues with the unsubscribe link (the link doesn't appear or doesn't work) try the following troubleshooting steps:

Step 1 | Check if the link was in a test email

If you send a test campaign, the unsubscribe link leads to this article rather than to a real unsubscribe link. If you send a real campaign the link should work.

Step 2 | Make sure you're clicking both unsubscribe links

When you click the unsubscribe link from your inbox a new tab opens, which includes an unsubscribe button. You must click this unsubscribe button to complete the process of unsubscribing from the campaign.  

Follow the steps in the 1st section of this article above to click both unsubscribe links and complete the process. 

Step 3 | Test the link in a mail client other than Microsoft Outlook

Sometimes Microsoft Outlook blocks the unsubscribe links. 

To test if Microsoft Outlook is causing the issue:
  1. Open the email campaign in a different mail client such as Gmail. 
  2. Follow the steps in the 1st section of this article above to unsubscribe. 
Note:
The unsubscribe text at the bottom of your email campaigns is written in the language of the associated Wix account. To change the language, change your account language. If you change the language, the unsubscribe text changes for future campaigns only. All past campaigns still show the original language.

question: How can I create a new group on my Wix site using the dashboard?
answer:
To create a new group on your Wix site using the dashboard, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Groups](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Go%20to%20Groups&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https:%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Fdashboard%2F%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D%2Fsocial-groups-dashboard/?referralInfo=KB_Article) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **+ Create Group**.
3. Choose the type of group you want to create:
   - **Start from scratch or choose a template**
     1. Click **+Start from scratch**.
     2. Choose from the available options:
        - **Template:** Select a group template from the available list (e.g. Health and Wellness).
        - **Start from scratch:** If none of the templates suit your needs, you can start fresh and create your own. Click **Create New Group** to get started from scratch.
4. Enter your group's **Info**:
   1. Give your group a name.
   2. Click the **Add Image** icon to add a cover image.
   3. Choose who can see and join this group under **Privacy**:
      - **Public:** Anyone can view this group.
      - **Private:** Only members can view the group's content. Click the **Visibility** drop-down and select the settings of the group (e.g. Visible or Hidden).
      - **Only paying members:** Members pay to view this group's content. Click **+ Connect a Pricing Plan** to [choose an existing plan or create a new one](https://support.wix.com/en/article/pricing-plans-an-overview).
5. Click **Create Group**.
6. [Manage and customize](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-groups-managing-your-group) every aspect of your group.
7. Click **Save**.

articles.title: Wix Groups: Creating a New Group

Make sure you have added Wix Groups to your site. 
In this article, learn more about:
  • Creating a new group
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

Creating a new group

Create a new group from your site's dashboard or the Wix app. You can choose from a set of templates or create a custom design for your group. You can also use AI to name the group, write a description, create a cover image, and set privacy preferences. 
Dashboard
Wix app

  3. Enter your group's Info:
    1. Give your group a name. 
    2. Click the Add Image icon  to add a cover image.
    3. Choose who can see and join this group under Privacy:
      • Public: Anyone can view this group.
      • Private: Only members can view the group's content. Click the Visibility drop-down and select the settings of the group (e.g. Visible or Hidden).

  2. Answer the questions in the Wix AI Assistant chat.

FAQs

How can site members join my groups?

Existing site members can join any group regardless of whether they have a public or private profile. When new people join your site, you can set up an automation to join your group automatically.

You can manage your group's info such as create new posts, monetize your exclusive content, and use various admin tools.

Is there a limit to how many groups I can create?

Yes. The maximum number of groups you can create is 1,000.

question: What should I do if I encounter an error message saying 'The upload failed because you uploaded too many videos in a short time' when uploading from Wix Video to YouTube?
answer: If you encounter the error message 'The upload failed because you uploaded too many videos in a short time,' you should come back and upload the rest of your videos later.

question: Can I reply to Wix Forms submissions directly from my email inbox?
answer:
Currently, using [new Wix Forms](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-forms-the-difference-between-the-new-and-old-wix-forms), it is not possible to reply to form submissions through your email inbox. You need to click the button in the email, or head over to your dashboard, in order to respond to the submission.

### Workaround
You can click the email address that appears in the email notification to start a direct conversation. However, the correspondence won’t appear in your Wix account.

question: Can I limit a shipping method to customers who purchase more than a minimum amount in Wix Stores?
answer: Currently, it's not possible to restrict a shipping method to customers who purchase more than a minimum amount. For example, you cannot limit a $10 flat-rate shipping rule to purchases over $100. You can, however, [limit purchases to a minimum order amount](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-setting-a-minimum-order-amount).

question: How can I set multiple contacts as members from the member list on my Wix site?
answer:
To set multiple contacts as members from the member list on your Wix site, follow these steps:

1. Go to [Site Members](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20Members&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/member-permissions/members) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click the **More Actions** drop-down at the top right.
3. Click **Set Contacts as Members**.
4. Select the relevant contacts (you can select up to 50 contacts at a time).
5. Click **Set as Members**.

Once you complete these steps, the selected contacts will receive an email to help them create an account on your site.

articles.title: Site Members: Setting Contacts as Members
articles.html_content:
You can select a person in your contact list and instantly make them a member of your site. Adding members from your contacts list is a quick and easy way for you to grow your site's community.
In this article, learn about setting contacts as members:
  • From the member list
  • From the person's Contact Panel
  • Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Important:
This feature is only available after adding the Members Area to your site and publishing it.

Setting contacts as members from the member list

You can set multiple contacts as members from your member list. Choose which contacts you want to make members and they'll all get an email to help them create an account on your site. 
Note:
You can select up to 50 contacts at a time. 

To set contacts as members from the member list:

  1. Go to Site Members in your site's dashboard. 
  2. Click the More Actions drop-down at the top right.
  3. Click Set Contacts as Members.
  4. Select the relevant contacts.
  5. Click Set as Members.

Setting a contact as a member from their Contact Panel

Set a contact as a member directly from the Contact List. Once you select the relevant person and their Contact Panel opens on the right, you can add them to your Member's Area in one click. They automatically get an email asking them to create a password for their new account.

To set a contact as a member from their Contact Panel:

  1. Go to Contacts in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click the relevant member to open their Contact Panel.
  3. (In the Contact Panel) Click Set Contact as Member under Member Info.

FAQs

What happens once I set a contact as a member?

Your contact receives an email asking them to create a password for their new account on your site. 

I got an error message while trying to set a contact as a member. Why?

You'll receive an error message if the contact is already a site member or if there are duplicate contacts.

Can I import contacts and make them members?

Yes. If you don't have any contacts in your dashboard, you can import external contacts via a CSV file or Google accounts. Then, set the relevant people as your site members.

question: How can I create a landing page from scratch using the Wix Editor?
answer:
To create a landing page from scratch using the Wix Editor, follow these steps:

1. [Go to your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26).
2. Click **Pages & Menu** on the left side of the editor.
3. Click **Add Page** at the top of the panel.
4. Choose the page template from the options.
5. Enter the new landing page name.
6. Click **Done**.
7. Remove the header and footer from this page:
   
   1. Click the **More Actions** icon on the page in the list.
   2. Click **Settings**.
   3. Click the **Layouts** tab.
   4. Select **No Header & Footer**.
8. (Optional) Make the landing page your site's homepage:
   
   1. Click the **Page Info** tab.
   2. Click **Set** next to **Make this your homepage?**.

articles.contents:
Wix Editor: Creating a Landing Page (E.g. 'Coming Soon' Page)
A landing page enables you to create an intent-focused experience for your site visitors, such as an 'Under Construction' or 'Coming Soon' page. Landing pages can capture your visitors' attention, and encourage them to interact by performing actions such as subscribing to your site, or signing up for your services.Your landing page should not display a header or a footer. This encourages visitors to focus on the message of your page, and is also helpful if your site is not yet ready. You can create a landing page from scratch, or choose a template available from Wix.In this article, learn more about:
Creating a landing page from scratch Creating a landing page with a template Useful information about landing pagesCreating a landing page from scratchBegin creating a landing page from scratch by adding a blank page to your site. You can then customize and build the site by adding elements such as images, text, and forms.To create a landing page from scratch:
Go to your editor. Click Pages & Menu    on the left side of the editor. Click Add Page at the top of the panel. Choose the page template from the options. Enter the new landing page name. Click Done. Remove the header and footer from this page:
    
Click the More Actions icon  on the page in the list. Click Settings. Click the Layouts tab. Select No Header & Footer.   (Optional) Make the landing page your site's homepage:
    
Click the Page Info tab. Click Set next to Make this your homepage?.  Creating a landing page using a templateAdd an optimized template from Wix to build your landing page much quicker.There are a variety of options to choose from, and the templates include elements such as forms and headings to help you build an eye-catching and engaging landing page. To add a landing page template:
Go to your editor. Click Pages & Menu    on the left side of the editor. Click +Add Menu Item at the bottom of the panel. Click New Page. Click Landing Page from the menu on the left. Hover over your chosen page and click Add Page. Type the name for the page in the field. Click Done. Remove the header and footer from this page:
    
Click the More Actions icon  on the page in the list. Click Settings. Click the Layouts tab. Select No Header & Footer.   (Optional) Make the landing page your site's homepage:
    
Click the Page Info tab. b.  Click Set next to Make this your homepage?.  Tip:You can also build a striking and informative and landing page site with our free landing page builder.Useful information about landing pagesWhen designing your landing page, it is important to keep the below points in mind:
If you want the landing page to be the first page that people see when they access your site URL, you need to set it as your homepage. If you are not ready for visitors to view your whole site, you can also prevent search engines from finding your site.  You can build awareness and excitement for your site or brand by linking the landing page in an email marketing campaign. If you have set your landing page to not display the header or footer, you should also keep these points in mind:
It does not have a menu. If you want your visitors to be able to navigate to the rest of your site, make sure to link a button to your site's main page. It does not display elements set to "show on all pages". articles.title: Wix Editor: Creating a Landing Page (E.g. 'Coming Soon' Page)
articles.html_content:
A landing page enables you to create an intent-focused experience for your site visitors, such as an 'Under Construction' or 'Coming Soon' page. Landing pages can capture your visitors' attention, and encourage them to interact by performing actions such as subscribing to your site, or signing up for your services.
Your landing page should not display a header or a footer. This encourages visitors to focus on the message of your page, and is also helpful if your site is not yet ready. 
You can create a landing page from scratch, or choose a template available from Wix.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Creating a landing page from scratch
  • Creating a landing page with a template
  • Useful information about landing pages

Creating a landing page from scratch

Begin creating a landing page from scratch by adding a blank page to your site. You can then customize and build the site by adding elements such as images, text, and forms.

To create a landing page from scratch:

  1. Go to your editor.
  2. Click Pages & Menu    on the left side of the editor.
  3. Click Add Page at the top of the panel.
  4. Choose the page template from the options.
  5. Enter the new landing page name.
  6. Click Done.
  7. Remove the header and footer from this page:
    1. Click the More Actions icon  on the page in the list.
    2. Click Settings.
    3. Click the Layouts tab.
    4. Select No Header & Footer.
  8. (Optional) Make the landing page your site's homepage:
    1. Click the Page Info tab.
    2. Click Set next to Make this your homepage?.

Creating a landing page using a template

Add an optimized template from Wix to build your landing page much quicker.
There are a variety of options to choose from, and the templates include elements such as forms and headings to help you build an eye-catching and engaging landing page. 

To add a landing page template:

  1. Go to your editor.
  2. Click Pages & Menu    on the left side of the editor.
  3. Click +Add Menu Item at the bottom of the panel.
  4. Click New Page.
  5. Click Landing Page from the menu on the left.
  6. Hover over your chosen page and click Add Page.
  7. Type the name for the page in the field.
  8. Click Done.
  9. Remove the header and footer from this page:
    1. Click the More Actions icon  on the page in the list.
    2. Click Settings.
    3. Click the Layouts tab.
    4. Select No Header & Footer.
  10. (Optional) Make the landing page your site's homepage:
    1. Click the Page Info tab.
    2. b.  Click Set next to Make this your homepage?.
Tip:
You can also build a striking and informative and landing page site with our free landing page builder.

Useful information about landing pages

When designing your landing page, it is important to keep the below points in mind:
  • If you want the landing page to be the first page that people see when they access your site URL, you need to set it as your homepage.
  • If you are not ready for visitors to view your whole site, you can also prevent search engines from finding your site. 
  • You can build awareness and excitement for your site or brand by linking the landing page in an email marketing campaign. 
If you have set your landing page to not display the header or footer, you should also keep these points in mind:
  • It does not have a menu. If you want your visitors to be able to navigate to the rest of your site, make sure to link a button to your site's main page.
  • It does not display elements set to "show on all pages".
  • Certain apps might not appear on your page. 
Want to learn more about landing pages?
The Wix blog has information on how landing pages can help you achieve your goals.

question: What should I do if I receive a 'Couldn't Fetch' error for my sitemap in Google Search Console?
answer: If you receive a "Couldn't Fetch" error in the Status field for your sitemap, first check to see that the URL path in the sitemap field on the left says "/sitemap.xml" and not the page URL (e.g., "/homepage"). If it was submitted incorrectly, go ahead and submit it again. If the sitemap URL is correct, note that this error is known to occur for sites hosted with any company and is not related to Wix. In most cases, it resolves itself within a couple of days or weeks. However, you can submit the URL using the Inspection Tool to speed up the process.

question: How can I schedule a course session in Wix Bookings?
answer:
To schedule a course session in Wix Bookings, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Booking Calendar](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Open%20Booking%20Calendar&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D/bookings/scheduler/owner/calendar?referralInfo=sidebar) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click the time slot in which the course takes place for the first time.
3. Select **Course session**.
4. Add the course session details: 
   
   * **Course/Service:** Select the course you want to schedule.
   * **Staff:** Select the staff member who is leading the course.
   * **Start Time:** Edit the date and start time of the session.
   * **Duration:** Select the duration of the course. 
     
     **Note:** Select **Custom** to enter a custom duration.
   * **Repeat:** Choose how often the course session is offered: 
     
     1. Select an option from the drop-down. 
        
        **Note:** Select **Doesn't Repeat** to only offer the course once.
     2. Select the day(s) of the week the course takes places.
     3. (Optional) Click the field next to **Until** and choose the date of the last class.
5. Choose a saving option:
   
   * **Save & Add New:** Save the session and start scheduling another one.
   * **Save:** Save the session and return to your calendar.

### Tip
Go to the [Bookings Services](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Booking%20Services&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/bookings/scheduler/owner/offerings?referralInfo=sidebar) tab and click **Show Schedule** next to the relevant course to view a summary of its schedule. You can also [select the Schedule view in your calendar](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-bookings-filtering-your-bookings-calendar) to check the list of upcoming sessions on the certain date.

question: How can I add a custom element to my Wix site using the Wix Editor?
answer:
To add a custom element to your Wix site using the Wix Editor, follow these steps:

1. Click **Add Elements** ![](https://d2eyqiy4n03ve6.cloudfront.net/12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab/2015/08/13/ff6d0998-bff3-41b9-bc06-595fd926d806.png) on the left side of the Editor.
2. Click **Embed Code**.
3. Click the Custom Element to add it to your page.
4. Click **Choose Source**.
5. Select **Server URL** and enter the URL, including the file name. 

   **Note:** If [you are using Velo](https://support.wix.com/en/article/velo-about-custom-elements), you can click **Velo File**.
6. Enter the **Tag Name**.

**Note:** All elements must be defined in the custom elements registry for the page. The tag name is the name used when registering the element. You can find the tag name in the customElements.define() line in the JavaScript file.

articles.contents:
Wix Editor: Adding a Custom Element to Your Site Use the custom element to add visible content to your site, and to design elements with additional CSS capabilities. In this article, read more about: How custom elements work Adding a custom element Adding attributes Guidelines and limitations An example of a custom elementImportant:We cannot provide support for external codes that were not created or tested by Wix. If you are experiencing an issue with your code snippet, please contact the provider directly.What are custom elements?Custom elements allow you to create custom HTML tags that you can use on your Wix site. The custom elements work across all Wix-supported browsers, and can be used with any JavaScript ES6 library or framework that works with HTML 5.You might want to use a custom element to:Design your own elements that are not yet available in the Wix Editor's Add panel or via apps.Design elements with additional CSS capabilities, such as CSS animation, countdown animation, breadcrumbs, tooltips, tags, charts, quotes, cursor changes and scroll interactions.Change the height of your element on your published site, such as to avoid layout collisions on the page.Improve performance (compared to iframe-based components). This largely depends on the implementation of the custom element.Note:You can use custom elements from third-party sources, just make sure to update the Tag Name in Properties when adding the custom element to your page.Adding the custom element Click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor. Click Embed Code. Click the Custom Element to add it to your page. Click Choose Source. Select Server URL and enter the URL, including the file name. Note: If you are using Velo, you can click Velo File.  Enter the Tag Name. Note:All elements must be defined in the custom elements registry for the page. The tag name is the name used when registering the element. You can find the tag name in the customElements.define() line in the JavaScript file.Setting the custom element's attributesImportant:Attributes are not open to all users yet.Define the HTML attributes on the custom element's DOM node. Make sure to add code to acknowledge and handle these defined attributes in the code of the custom element.  Click Set Attributes on the custom element. Click New Attribute.  Name the attribute, for example, "rotation" or "width".  Assign the value for the attribute, for example, 45.Note:You can also edit and remove a custom element's HTML attributes.Guidelines and limitations For security reasons, to use the custom element, you must upgrade your site with a Premium Plan, connect a domain and have no ads on it. Make sure that your code contains HTTPS, not HTTP, or it will not be displayed on your live site. JavaScript code contains the core elements of the page, but the design settings and other complex functionalities might be stored separately. Therefore, some elements may not function or look the same if the relevant elements aren’t included within the main JS code, for example the CSS and other JS files.  Always make sure the code is up to date and HTML5 compatible. Most browsers don't display pages and scripts properly if they were written using older versions of JS or HTML.  SEO can be defined separately using Velo API.  The performance depends on the implementation of the custom element itself. The custom element code must be hosted by you if you are not using Velo.Important:For security reasons, the custom element is rendered inside an iFrame inside the Editor and in preview mode. This might affect the layout of the component. Go to your published site to see how it actually looks on your live site. You can also use test sites as a live site preview. Custom element exampleBelow is an example of adding a basic custom element to your site. The instructions explain how to add "Hello World" text to your site.First you need to create and code the element and its behavior in a JavaScript file. Note:Upgrade your site with a Premium Plan, connect a domain and make sure the Wix ads are removed.To create and add your custom element: Set up, or get access to, a server for your custom element. If you host externally on your own server, you will need to connect the custom element to the server URL when adding the custom element in the Wix Editor. If you are hosting locally, you can use HTTP.   If you are hosting on an external server, you must use HTTPS. Learn how to get started hosting an external server Note: If you are using Velo and want to host with Wix click here. Use any IDE to create a custom element in a Javascript file using the standard ECMAScript 2015 class syntax. For full instructions and examples, see the MDN documentation. Define the custom element class: The HelloWorld class is the class of the custom element, which we'll use when registering the custom element. connectedCallback() is a lifecycle callback function that is triggered automatically when the element is attached to DOM. 3. Define the custom element class: + The `HelloWorld` class is the class of the custom element, which we'll use when registering the custom element. + [`connectedCallback()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Web_Components/Using_custom_elements#Using_the_lifecycle_callbacks) is a lifecycle callback function that is triggered automatically when the element is attached to DOM. class HelloWorld extends HTMLElement { connectedCallback() { this.innerHTML = '


Hello World!'; } } customElements.define('hello-world', HelloWorld); Register the custom element class with the customElements.define(name, class) method. articles.title: Wix Editor: Adding a Custom Element to Your Site
articles.html_content:
Use the custom element to add visible content to your site, and to design elements with additional CSS capabilities. 
In this article, read more about:
  • How custom elements work
  • Adding a custom element
  • Adding attributes
  • Guidelines and limitations
  • An example of a custom element
Important:
We cannot provide support for external codes that were not created or tested by Wix. If you are experiencing an issue with your code snippet, please contact the provider directly.

What are custom elements?

Custom elements allow you to create custom HTML tags that you can use on your Wix site. The custom elements work across all Wix-supported browsers, and can be used with any JavaScript ES6 library or framework that works with HTML 5.
You might want to use a custom element to:
  • Design your own elements that are not yet available in the Wix Editor's Add panel or via apps.
  • Design elements with additional CSS capabilities, such as CSS animation, countdown animation, breadcrumbs, tooltips, tags, charts, quotes, cursor changes and scroll interactions.
  • Change the height of your element on your published site, such as to avoid layout collisions on the page.
  • Improve performance (compared to iframe-based components). This largely depends on the implementation of the custom element.
Note:
You can use custom elements from third-party sources, just make sure to update the Tag Name in Properties when adding the custom element to your page.

Adding the custom element

  1. Click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor.
  2. Click Embed Code.
  3. Click the Custom Element to add it to your page.
  4. Click Choose Source.
  5. Select Server URL and enter the URL, including the file name.
    Note: If you are using Velo, you can click Velo File. 
  6. Enter the Tag Name. 
Note:
All elements must be defined in the custom elements registry for the page. The tag name is the name used when registering the element. You can find the tag name in the customElements.define() line in the JavaScript file.

Setting the custom element's attributes

Important:
Attributes are not open to all users yet.
Define the HTML attributes on the custom element's DOM node. Make sure to add code to acknowledge and handle these defined attributes in the code of the custom element. 
  1. Click Set Attributes on the custom element.
  2. Click New Attribute. 
  3. Name the attribute, for example, "rotation" or "width". 
  4. Assign the value for the attribute, for example, 45.
Note:
You can also edit and remove a custom element's HTML attributes.

Guidelines and limitations

  • For security reasons, to use the custom element, you must upgrade your site with a Premium Plan, connect a domain and have no ads on it.
  • Make sure that your code contains HTTPS, not HTTP, or it will not be displayed on your live site.
  • JavaScript code contains the core elements of the page, but the design settings and other complex functionalities might be stored separately. Therefore, some elements may not function or look the same if the relevant elements aren’t included within the main JS code, for example the CSS and other JS files. 
  • Always make sure the code is up to date and HTML5 compatible. Most browsers don't display pages and scripts properly if they were written using older versions of JS or HTML. 
  • SEO can be defined separately using Velo API. 
  • The performance depends on the implementation of the custom element itself.
  • The custom element code must be hosted by you if you are not using Velo.
Important:
For security reasons, the custom element is rendered inside an iFrame inside the Editor and in preview mode. This might affect the layout of the component. Go to your published site to see how it actually looks on your live site. You can also use test sites as a live site preview. 

Custom element example

Below is an example of adding a basic custom element to your site. The instructions explain how to add "Hello World" text to your site.
First you need to create and code the element and its behavior in a JavaScript file. 
Note:
Upgrade your site with a Premium Plan, connect a domain and make sure the Wix ads are removed.

To create and add your custom element:

  1. Set up, or get access to, a server for your custom element. If you host externally on your own server, you will need to connect the custom element to the server URL when adding the custom element in the Wix Editor.
    • If you are hosting locally, you can use HTTP.  
    • If you are hosting on an external server, you must use HTTPS. Learn how to get started hosting an external server
      Note: If you are using Velo and want to host with Wix click here.
  2. Use any IDE to create a custom element in a Javascript file using the standard ECMAScript 2015 class syntax. For full instructions and examples, see the MDN documentation.
  1. Define the custom element class:
    • The HelloWorld class is the class of the custom element, which we'll use when registering the custom element.
    • connectedCallback() is a lifecycle callback function that is triggered automatically when the element is attached to DOM.
3. Define the custom element class: + The `HelloWorld` class is the class of the custom element, which we'll use when registering the custom element. + [`connectedCallback()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Web_Components/Using_custom_elements#Using_the_lifecycle_callbacks) is a lifecycle callback function that is triggered automatically when the element is attached to DOM. 
class HelloWorld extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    this.innerHTML = '<br/><br/><br/>Hello World!';
  }
}
customElements.define('hello-world', HelloWorld);

  1. Register the custom element class with the customElements.define(name, class) method. In the Editor, enter the registered name as the tag name when adding the custom element to the site. Once registered, the custom element can be used on your site.

    • The first parameter, hello-world, maps to the tag name, which will be defined in the Editor (step 8).
    • The second parameter, HelloWorld, is the class name of the custom element.
4. Register the custom element class with the `customElements.define(name, class)` method. In the Editor, enter the registered name as the tag name when adding the custom element to the site. Once registered, the custom element can be used on your site. + The first parameter, `hello-world`, maps to the tag name, which will be defined in the Editor (step 8). + The second parameter, `HelloWorld`, is the class name of the custom element.
CustomElementRegistry.define('hello-world', HelloWorld);
  1. Add the custom element in your Editor (see above).
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Choose Server URL and enter the server URL for your custom element script file.
  4. Enter the tag name. The tag name corresponds to the element name we registered using the define() function in the previous step. The tag name in this example is hello-world.
  5. Save and publish your site.
5. Add the custom element in your Editor (see above). 6. Click **Settings**. 7. Choose **Server URL** and enter the server URL for your custom element script file. 8. Enter the tag name. The tag name corresponds to the element name we registered using the `define()` function in the previous step. The tag name in this example is `hello-world`. 9. Save and publish your site.
Looking for more advanced information?
Learn how to use this element with Velo by Wix
Tips:
  • Show your custom element on all pages. 
  • Display your custom element even on scroll with Pin to Screen. Or, alternatively, use the CSS fixed positioned element in the custom element code.

question: How can I reactivate a canceled Premium or Studio site plan on Wix before the subscription ends?
answer:
To reactivate your Premium or Studio plan before the subscription ends, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Premium Subscriptions](https://premium.wix.com/wix/api/mpContainerStaticController?originWidgetName=billings) in your Wix account.
2. Click **Turn Auto Renew On** under the relevant subscription.

**Note:** Site plans canceled during the [14-day money back period](https://support.wix.com/en/article/requesting-a-refund-for-a-premium-plan) are canceled immediately and cannot be reactivated by turning the auto renew back on. In such cases, you can upgrade the site again to purchase a new plan.

question: Can customers set their own prices for products in Wix Stores?
answer:
Currently, it is not possible to give customers the ability to choose a price for a product they are purchasing. This would mean that you could sell products on a sliding scale, or collect donations.

If you want to set variable prices yourself, you can: 
* Sell store products through Wix Invoices. [Learn how](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-stores-creating-a-manual-order-using-wix-invoices)
* Negotiate prices with customers using Price Quotes, and then turn quotes into invoices. [Learn how](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-price-quotes-creating-and-sending-price-quotes-to-clients)
