articles.contents:
Studio Editor: Troubleshooting Gaps and Horizontal Scroll Bars
While building a site in the Studio Editor, you may notice unwanted gaps and horizontal scroll bars. Use the steps in this article to learn what you should check, and ensure that they don't appear to visitors on any screen size.Step 1 | Find and re-position elements in the Layers panelIf an element is outside its section boundaries, a blank gap is automatically created to make the element fully visible. Use the Layers panel to see a list of your page elements, and click each one to check and re-position them as needed.To find and re-position elements in the Layers panel:
Click Layers  on the left of the Studio Editor. Select an element to find it on the page.  Re-position the element using the following tools:
    
Drag and drop it to the right place. Use the handles to decrease the size of the element. Adjust the margins or resize the element from the Inspector panel .  Step 2 | Check the page edgesWhile an element may be positioned inside a section, its edges could still cross the page's boundaries and create a white gap and / or a horizontal scroll bar. This often happens with text elements. Click each section and hover over all of the elements close to the edges of the page. If any of them are overflowing, you can move or resize them as needed.Step 3 | Change the Overflow Content setting of the pageYou can hide a page's overflow content to prevent white gaps and horizontal scroll bars from automatically being displayed on the page. This setting "clips" the edges of the page, so any overflowing elements (or parts of elements) are cropped. To change the overflow content setting:
Select your page:
    
Go to the relevant page. Click Layers  on the left of the Studio Editor. Click Page.   Click the Open Inspector arrow  at the top right of the Studio Editor. Click the Design tab . Select Hide from the Overflow content drop-down.Step 4 | Check the section's heightThe height and / or minimum height you set for a section or CSS Grid may create a gap. If you're using the Fit to screen behavior, or the vh measurement (which is relative to the viewport height), the gap may appear bigger on larger screens. You can use the Inspector panel to check the CSS Grid and section's sizing, and change their height and / or minimum height as needed. To check the section's height:
Select the relevant section. Click the Open Inspector arrow  at the top right of the Studio Editor Click the Design tab . Check and adjust Height and Min H settings under Size. TroubleshootingIf you’re still seeing unwanted gaps on your client's live site, check out this video tutorial to troubleshoot the issue.
articles.title: Studio Editor: Troubleshooting Gaps and Horizontal Scroll Bars
articles.html_content:
While building a site in the Studio Editor, you may notice unwanted gaps and horizontal scroll bars. Use the steps in this article to learn what you should check, and ensure that they don't appear to visitors on any screen size.

Step 1 | Find and re-position elements in the Layers panel

If an element is outside its section boundaries, a blank gap is automatically created to make the element fully visible. Use the Layers panel to see a list of your page elements, and click each one to check and re-position them as needed.

To find and re-position elements in the Layers panel:

  1. Click Layers  on the left of the Studio Editor.
  2. Select an element to find it on the page. 
  3. Re-position the element using the following tools:
    • Drag and drop it to the right place.
    • Use the handles to decrease the size of the element.
    • Adjust the margins or resize the element from the Inspector panel .

Step 2 | Check the page edges

While an element may be positioned inside a section, its edges could still cross the page's boundaries and create a white gap and / or a horizontal scroll bar. This often happens with text elements. 
Click each section and hover over all of the elements close to the edges of the page. If any of them are overflowing, you can move or resize them as needed.

Step 3 | Change the Overflow Content setting of the page

You can hide a page's overflow content to prevent white gaps and horizontal scroll bars from automatically being displayed on the page. This setting "clips" the edges of the page, so any overflowing elements (or parts of elements) are cropped. 

To change the overflow content setting:

  1. Select your page:
    1. Go to the relevant page.
    2. Click Layers  on the left of the Studio Editor.
    3. Click Page.
  2. Click the Open Inspector arrow  at the top right of the Studio Editor.
  3. Click the Design tab .
  4. Select Hide from the Overflow content drop-down.

Step 4 | Check the section's height

The height and / or minimum height you set for a section or CSS Grid may create a gap. If you're using the Fit to screen behavior, or the vh measurement (which is relative to the viewport height), the gap may appear bigger on larger screens. 
You can use the Inspector panel to check the CSS Grid and section's sizing, and change their height and / or minimum height as needed. 

To check the section's height:

  1. Select the relevant section.
  2. Click the Open Inspector arrow  at the top right of the Studio Editor
  3. Click the Design tab .
  4. Check and adjust Height and Min H settings under Size. 

Troubleshooting

If you’re still seeing unwanted gaps on your client's live site, check out this video tutorial to troubleshoot the issue.

articles.title: Business Phone Number: Getting Started
articles.html_content:
Separate work and personal life by getting a dedicated phone number for your business. Call and text your contacts from the Wix mobile app, decide when your line should be available for incoming business calls, and customize your voicemail to make sure you never miss a lead.
Important:
Business Phone Number is only available to Wix users from the U.S. and Canada.

Purchase a business phone number

You can purchase a business number directly from your site's dashboard. Select from a wide range of local numbers in the U.S. and Canada. Then, choose a monthly or yearly subscription plan that meets your needs in terms of calls and texts.

Create a personalized voicemail

Your business phone number comes with a voicemail inbox so callers can leave a message when you're not available. By default, you get a built-in greeting that you can customize to make it speak your brand's tone and voice.
Upload a recording of your own, write a message read by a computer-generated voice or record a voicemail greeting on the spot with the Wix app. Learn how to create a personalized voicemail.
Tip:
  • Let your callers know they've reached the right place by mentioning your business name and info in the voicemail greeting.
  • Enable email notifications so voicemail transcripts are sent directly to your email address.

Set your availability with call hours & 'Do Not Disturb' mode

With Business Phone Number, you have full control of your line's call hours. Set the specific days and times when your number is available to take calls, or set it to be available 24/7. You can also switch to the Do Not Disturb mode and make your number temporarily unavailable.

Receive incoming calls & SMS messages

Incoming calls reach the phone number that you connect to when you purchase your business number. You can choose whether to have your phone display your caller's number or your business number.
Tip:
If you choose to display your business number, you can save it on your phone under a recognizable name (e.g. "Business Line") so you instantly recognize incoming business calls.
When your business number receives a call, your phone will also display a Wix app notification showing the phone number of the incoming call.
Incoming text messages reach Wix Inbox, so you can easily manage the correspondence and follow up. You can see and respond to texts from both the Wix app and your site's dashboard.

Make outbound business calls & send SMS messages

Using the Wix app, you can make business calls to contacts in the U.S. and Canada. Access the conversation with the relevant contact and tap the Call icon  to call them. Your contact will then receive a call from your business number.
In order for Wix to verify the call is coming from your phone:
Enable the Caller ID feature on your personal device. If you cannot enable the Caller ID from your device, you will need to contact your wireless provider for assistance.
You can also send SMS text messages to communicate with your contacts. Incoming text messages are displayed in Wix Inbox (available on dashboard and mobile), and you can reply on the go with the Wix app.
Notes:
  • Using SMS messages to communicate with your contacts means that you must comply with certain rules and regulations. Ensure you are familiar with them and comply with the requirements of the applicable laws.
  • If you're in the U.S., you may be prompted to submit information about your business before you send an SMS message. Mobile carriers require this information to help prevent spam.

Manage your communications in one place

Conveniently manage communication with your contacts using Wix Inbox, from your desktop or on the go with the Wix app. Access your contacts, check your call logs, send messages, and manage your voicemail, all from a centralized location.

articles.title: Branded App: FAQs
articles.html_content:
Here are some commonly asked questions about Branded App by Wix:

General FAQs

What's the process of creating my own branded app with Wix?

First you'll design your app (including its name, logo, look and feel) from the Branded App dashboard in your Wix account. Once your app is designed you can preview it for free on your mobile device. If you like the way it works, purchase a Branded App plan and follow the steps to publish your app on the Google Play and App Store.

Is this app a native app or a web app?

Branded App by Wix is a native app, which means it's built with the native language of the device it's installed on. This allows for a smoother user experience.

Does a branded app replace the existing mobile version of my site?

No, your branded app will be available in addition to the mobile version of your website. Branded App by Wix is a fully native mobile app that can be downloaded from app stores. Members accessing your site from a mobile browser can still view the mobile version.

When I make changes to my Wix site, does my app automatically update?

Your app is linked to your site dashboard. That means any changes or edits you make on the dashboard are reflected in your branded app. This includes adding items to your online store, new bookings or services, or creating new blog posts. 

However, any content or design changes you make directly from the Editor won't affect your app's design.

How do I access the Branded App dashboard?

The Branded App dashboard is located in your Wix account. Click the Start Now button to start creating your app. Go to the Branded App dashboard now.

How do I publish my Branded App?

After you've designed your app in the Branded App dashboard, you'll follow the steps to open both an Apple and Google developer account. This process is done on Apple and Google's side and can take a few business days to be approved.

Once your account is approved, you'll finish registering your app from the Branded App dashboard and submit your app to Wix for approval. Once that's submitted, we'll submit it to the relevant app stores.

Can my app be viewed in multiple languages?

You can change the default language of your branded app. Your members can still choose their preferred language from their member profiles. Learn how to change your app's language in Step 2 of this article. 

Note: Branded App by Wix does not currently support multilingual.

Can I migrate my existing members from my member app to my branded app?

If you're using an existing Wix member app to communicate with your members (Spaces by Wix, Fit by Wix or Dine by Wix), there's no migration required.

Your members will get a notification in their app asking them to download your new branded app. Learn how to switch your preferred member app.

Can I only publish my app in one app store (e.g. only Apple's App Store and not Google Play?)

Currently you must register your app in both stores.

What is the difference between Branded App by Wix and Spaces by Wix?

The main difference between your branded app and Spaces by Wix is that a branded app has no Wix branding and is only for your business and community. Your members download your app directly from the App Store and Google Play rather than downloading a Wix app and engaging with your site from there.

What are the available languages for Branded App by Wix?

Branded App by Wix is available in the following languages:
Arabic, Chinese, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish and Ukrainian. 

Can my app members/I use my branded app offline?

No, Branded App by Wix requires an online connection. Currently it is not possible to use the app offline and then have the content sync once the device is online again.

Purchasing a Branded App plan

What is included in a Branded App plan?

Learn more about what's included in a Branded App plan. 

Does my Branded App plan include membership fees to Apple's App Store and Google Play?

No, the plan does not include the registration fees and you must pay those separately. Apple's App Store membership fees start at $99 USD a year, and Google Play is a $25 USD one-time fee.

What happens to my app if I cancel my Branded App subscription?

You can get a full refund within the first 30 days of purchasing a subscription.

After your app is live, if you decide to cancel your subscription Wix automatically removes your app from the app stores. If your members try to use the app they will be notified that the app is no longer available for use.

Can I assign my Branded App plan to a different site in my account?

Yes. After you purchase a Branded App plan, it is possible to assign it to another site in your account.

  1. Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account.
  2. Click the Show More icon next to your branded app plan.
  3. Click Assign to a Different Site.
  4. Select the checkbox next to the relevant site.
  5. Click Next. 
  6. Click Assign to confirm. 

Can I transfer my Branded App plan from one Wix account to another Wix account?

Yes. Since your branded app is connected to a Wix site, you can change ownership by transferring the premium site associated with your branded app to another Wix account. Learn how to transfer a premium site to another account. 

Submitting your Branded App for review

What happens after I submit my app?

  1. We will review your application to make sure it follows Apple and Google's compliance guidelines. If we see something that needs changing, we'll notify you within 7 business days.
  2. Once your app passes our internal review, we submit the app to Apple and Google on your behalf. Once Apple and Google approve the app, it will be released to app stores. The upload process can take up to 3 days.
    Note: Your branded app is subject to Apple and Google's approval. Wix has no control over whether it will be approved or rejected by Apple and Google.

How long does it take for Apple and Google to approve my app?

The approval process varies from platform to platform and Wix has no control over the timeline.
  • Learn more about Apple's approval process.
  • Learn more about Google's approval process.

What happens if I get emails from Apple and Google?

As part of the Branded App plan, Wix takes care of your app's submission to the stores as well as the app's maintenance and compliance with any new policies. During this process you may receive emails from Apple and Google. These emails require no action from you.

Learn more about the emails you receive from Apple and Google.

What if my app is not approved by Apple and/or Google?

If your application does not pass Apple or Google's review, Wix gets notified. We'll then inform you why your app has not been approved and ask you to make the necessary changes.

Once you've made the changes, you will have to resubmit your app to Wix for approval, and then again to Apple and Google. Learn how to resubmit your app.

How do app updates work once my app is live in the app stores?

Once your app is live, we make sure it stays current by updating it when necessary.

Canceling your Branded App plan

How do I cancel my Branded App plan?

  1. Go to Subscriptions in your Wix account.
  2. Scroll down to the site with the branded app and click the More Actions icon  next to Branded App.
  3. Click Cancel Branded App.
  4. Click Cancel Now in the pop-up to confirm.

When I cancel my Branded App plan, will it still appear in the app stores?

After your app is live, if you decide to cancel your subscription, Wix automatically removes your app from the app store listings. 

If you want to build another Branded App, purchase a Branded App plan and follow the steps to publish your app on the Google Play and App Store.

How will canceling my Branded App affect my members?

If your members try to use the app they will be notified that the app is no longer available for use.

How do I get a refund for my Branded App plan?

You can get a full refund within the first 30 days of purchasing a subscription. To get the refund, cancel your plan from Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Learn more about the Wix refund policy.

Do I need to do anything with my Apple Developer Account or Google Developer Account?

Your Apple Developer Account or Google Developer Account information will be saved in case you want to relist your Branded App at any stage. If you wish to relist your Branded App, you can re-purchase a Branded App plan to get it back in the app stores. 

What can I do if I canceled my Branded App by mistake?

If you change your mind about canceling your Branded App, or canceled it in error, you can contact customer care for support and they can help you relist it. 

Note: Branded Apps remain listed for 2-3 days after cancelation.

question: Is there a feature in the Studio Editor that analyzes a site and highlights areas that require adjustment for accessibility?
answer: Currently, we do not offer a feature that analyzes a site and highlights areas that require adjustment in order to make it accessible. However, you can apply certain settings that may help make your client's site more accessible, like adding alt text and [arranging your elements in the layers panel](https://support.wix.com/en/article/studio-editor-working-with-layers#reordering-layers).

question: How can I create multiple Facebook & Instagram Ads campaigns using Wix?
answer:
To create multiple Facebook & Instagram Ads campaigns using Wix, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Facebook & Instagram Ads](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Facebook%20Ads&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https:%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Fdashboard%2F%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D%2Fpaid-ads%3FreferralInfo%3Dkb-article) in your site's dashboard.
2. The campaigns page shows all your current campaign(s) in a list. Click **Create New Campaign** at the top right to make another campaign.
3. Customize the settings and ad content of your new ad campaign. [Learn more about creating campaign content](https://support.wix.com/en/article/facebook-instagram-ads-creating-a-campaign).
4. Set your new campaign's daily budget. The daily budget is taken from your total ad credits.
5. Click **Launch** to launch your new campaign.

Your new campaign appears in the campaigns page. The status label is **In Review** until the campaign content is approved by Meta.

articles.title: Facebook & Instagram Ads: Creating Multiple Campaigns
articles.html_content:
Create multiple campaigns for Facebook & Instagram Ads with Wix, each tailored to your diverse business objectives, and experiment with your ad content to determine what yields the highest conversion rate. Track all your campaigns from one place and make updates to the content and daily budget from your site's dashboard.
Running multiple campaigns allows you to:
  • Test different ad content simultaneously: Try different ad text and creatives to see what drives the best results for your business. Try ads with shorter videos, longer videos, or image and text only.
  • Promote a specific sale or service: Create one evergreen Facebook & Instagram Ads campaign to generate more site traffic overall, and use another campaign to promote a specific sale or offering happening that month.
  • Manage one subscription and budget for all campaigns: You don't have to worry about paying multiple subscriptions for each campaign. You pay one subscription and choose your budget. Then you can allocate your budget across all campaigns.
In this article, learn more about:
  • The campaigns page
  • Creating multiple Facebook & Instagram Ads with Wix campaigns
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

The campaigns page

When you go to Facebook & Instagram Ads in your site's dashboard, the first element you'll see is the main campaigns page. Your campaigns page gives you a quick breakdown of each campaign you've created. Every campaign has its own card with key performance indicators including impressions, total clicks, ad spend used, and daily spend.
Tip:
Hover over a campaign and click Go to Dashboard to see all the data for that campaign.
Labels next to each campaign title show you the status of that campaign: Live, Paused, In Review, Disapproved, or Ended. Any live campaigns appear at the top of the list in chronological order.
From the campaigns page you can also manage your subscription and budget as well as create a new campaign.

Creating multiple Facebook & Instagram Ads campaigns

You can create as many campaigns as you want from your site's dashboard. Keep track of your spend for each campaign as well as the campaign status. For every new campaign, choose a daily budget that is allocated from your total ad credits.

To create multiple campaigns:

  1. Go to Facebook & Instagram Ads in your site's dashboard.
  2. The campaigns page shows all your current campaign(s) in a list. Click Create New Campaign at the top right to make another campaign.
  3. Customize the settings and ad content of your new ad campaign. Learn more about creating campaign content.
  4. Set your new campaign's daily budget. The daily budget is taken from your total ad credits.
How your budget works with multiple campaigns:
You pay for one Facebook & Instagram Ads subscription regardless of how many campaigns you run. The subscription includes all your ad credits for your campaigns. When you choose a daily budget for a new campaign, it's taken from the total 'bucket' of ad credits available for all campaigns in your account. To get more ad credits, Click Manage ad credits & budget in the campaigns page and increase your subscription.
  1. Click Launch to launch your new campaign.
Your new campaign appears in the campaigns page. The status label is In Review until the campaign content is approved by Meta.

FAQs

Click a question below to learn more about creating multiple campaigns.

Is there a limit on the number of campaigns I can create?

No. You can create as many Facebook & Instagram Ads with Wix campaigns as you need to, but there is a minimum daily spend for each campaign.

How do I change the daily budget of my campaigns?

  1. From the main campaigns page, click Manage Budget & credits at the right.
  2. View the ad credits remaining in the current billing cycle. Click Adjust Daily Budget to change your daily spend on each campaign.
  3.  Enter a new daily budget for the campaign(s) you want to change. At the bottom you can see the total daily spend across all your campaigns.
    Note: If you don't have enough budget for the new daily amount, you can increase your monthly subscription.
  4. Click Save to update your daily budget. If you have also increased your subscription, you will go through the checkout process at this step.

What happens when I pause a campaign?

When you pause a campaign, the campaign stops running and does not spend ad credits. The campaign status also changes to 'Paused' on the Campaigns page.

How long should I keep multiple campaigns running if I am comparing them for performance?

You should give campaigns at least two weeks in order to see any potential patterns and identify what is working and where you can adjust. Start by checking in after seven days to see which campaign is driving more traffic. After that, if one is vastly underperforming, you can reassess. 

What happens when I end all my campaigns?

When all of your campaigns have ended, auto-renewal of your Facebook & Instagram Ads with Wix subscription will automatically turn off.

question: How can I ensure that my site's design looks great on all screen sizes using the Studio Editor?
answer:
To ensure your site's design looks great on all screen sizes using the Studio Editor, you can customize your designs per breakpoint. Breakpoints are screen width ranges that represent the possible screens and devices visitors use, such as tablets and mobiles. The Studio Editor uses a cascading concept, where changes made on larger breakpoints trickle down to smaller breakpoints, but changes on smaller breakpoints don't affect larger breakpoints.

Additionally, you can use the responsive AI tool to make your sections responsive on all screen sizes with just one click. This tool identifies groups of related elements and applies the ideal layout tool for each group, such as stack or grid.

For element resizing, you can edit the element's size in pixels and select a responsive behavior to ensure it looks great on every screen size. Every element comes with a default responsive behavior, like scaling proportionally, which controls how it gets resized on other screens. You can change an element's responsive behavior from the Inspector panel to better meet your needs.

To make an element's design match any screen, enable the **Scale properties** toggle in the Inspector. This ensures that the design looks ideal on every screen, automatically adjusting properties like borders.

For text, the Studio Editor automatically scales text in proportion to the screen size. You can set minimum and maximum values to ensure the text never gets too small or too big. For more precise control, select **Custom** to set the size range for each separate breakpoint.

Edit the element's size in pixels and select a responsive behavior to take care of the rest. What is px*?It's a unit of measure that lets you set sizing with a familiar measurement (pixels), while the actual measurement behind the scenes is responsive.Every element comes with a default responsive behavior (e.g. Scale proportionally), which controls the way it gets resized on other screens. This truly accelerates the design process as you don't have to go through each and every breakpoint to set sizing.From the Inspector panel, you can change an element's responsive behavior to one that better meets your needs. Make the element's design match any screenWhen you set an element to scale proportionally, you can ensure that its design looks ideal on every screen. Customize your designs per breakpoint

The Studio Editor lets you tailor sites per breakpoint, so they always look great. Breakpoints are screen width ranges, representing the possible screens and devices that visitors tend to use (e.g. tablet, mobile). 
The Studio Editor uses a cascading concept when it comes to designing across breakpoints. Changes you make on larger breakpoints trickle down to smaller breakpoints, but changes on smaller breakpoints don't affect larger breakpoints. 

Let AI make your sections responsive

Make your section responsive on all screen sizes in just one click, using the power of AI. The responsive AI tool identifies groups of related elements and applies the ideal layout tool for each group (e.g. stack, grid). 

Automatic resizing across breakpoints

As you're designing a site, you want to make sure the elements look great on every screen size. Edit the element's size in pixels and select a responsive behavior to take care of the rest. 

What is px*?

It's a unit of measure that lets you set sizing with a familiar measurement (pixels), while the actual measurement behind the scenes is responsive.
Every element comes with a default responsive behavior (e.g. Scale proportionally), which controls the way it gets resized on other screens. This truly accelerates the design process as you don't have to go through each and every breakpoint to set sizing.
From the Inspector panel, you can change an element's responsive behavior to one that better meets your needs. 

Make the element's design match any screen

When you set an element to scale proportionally, you can ensure that its design looks ideal on every screen. Enable the Scale properties toggle in the Inspector to make it happen automatically.
This is useful, for example, if your element has a defined border. The border might seem too thick and overbearing on small screens, or non-existent on large screens. With the toggle enabled, all you have to do is set the design you want on desktop.

Automatic and manual text scaling

In the Studio Editor, text is set to automatically scale in proportion to the screen size. You choose the font size you want on desktop, we take care of the rest. You can set minimum and maximum values to make sure the text never gets too small or too big for your design. 
If you need more precise control of the text scaling, select Custom instead. This lets you set the size range for each separate breakpoint.

question: How can I categorize my custom code on my website to comply with data privacy laws?
answer:
To categorize your custom code on your website, follow these steps:

1. Go to [Settings](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20Settings&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/manage-website) in your site's dashboard.
2. Scroll down to **Advanced** and click the **Custom Code** tab.
3. Click **\+ Add Custom Code** at the top right.
4. Add your [custom code](https://support.wix.com/en/article/embedding-custom-code-on-your-site#adding-custom-code-to-your-site).
5. Click the **Code Type** tab.
6. Select the category that best describes your code's purpose.
7. Click **Apply**.

Correct categorization helps your site comply with data privacy laws such as the [GDPR](https://support.wix.com/en/article/preparing-your-wix-site-for-the-gdpr) and the [LGPD](https://support.wix.com/en/article/preparing-your-wix-site-for-the-lgpd). These laws require that your visitors can decline the use of non-essential cookies while using your site.

articles.contents:
Categorizing Your Custom Code
Categorize your custom code embeds (cookies) so that browsers can recognize the purpose of your code. All code has a purpose, which may be classified as either Essential, Marketing, Analytic or Functional.  Correct categorization helps your site comply with data privacy laws such as the GDPR and the LGPD. These laws require that your visitors can decline the use of non-essential cookies while using your site.Custom codes are categorized as essential by default. This means that the code is loaded prior to visitor consent and cannot be disabled. If your custom code can be more accurately be described as either Marketing, Analytic or Functional code, it is your responsibility to classify it as such.How to decide how your code should be categorized:
Essential cookies: These cookies are integral to the use of your site. They enable basic functionality such as security, identity verification and network management. Marketing cookies: These cookies are used to track advertising effectiveness to provide a more relevant service and deliver better ads to suit visitor interests. Analytic cookies: These cookies help to understand how visitors interact with your website, discover errors and provide a better overall analytics. Functional cookies: These cookies collect data to remember choices visitors make to improve and give a more personalized experience.To categorize your custom code:
Go to Settings in your site's dashboard. Scroll down to Advanced and click the Custom Code tab. Click + Add Custom Code at the top right. Add your custom code.  Click the Code Type tab. Select the category that best describes your code's purpose.
Click Apply.
articles.title: Categorizing Your Custom Code
articles.html_content:
Categorize your custom code embeds (cookies) so that browsers can recognize the purpose of your code. All code has a purpose, which may be classified as either Essential, Marketing, Analytic or Functional.  Correct categorization helps your site comply with data privacy laws such as the GDPR and the LGPD. These laws require that your visitors can decline the use of non-essential cookies while using your site.
Custom codes are categorized as essential by default. This means that the code is loaded prior to visitor consent and cannot be disabled. If your custom code can be more accurately be described as either Marketing, Analytic or Functional code, it is your responsibility to classify it as such.
How to decide how your code should be categorized:
  • Essential cookies: These cookies are integral to the use of your site. They enable basic functionality such as security, identity verification and network management.
  • Marketing cookies: These cookies are used to track advertising effectiveness to provide a more relevant service and deliver better ads to suit visitor interests.
  • Analytic cookies: These cookies help to understand how visitors interact with your website, discover errors and provide a better overall analytics.
  • Functional cookies: These cookies collect data to remember choices visitors make to improve and give a more personalized experience.

To categorize your custom code:

  1. Go to Settings in your site's dashboard.
  2. Scroll down to Advanced and click the Custom Code tab.
  3. Click + Add Custom Code at the top right.
  4. Add your custom code. 
  5. Click the Code Type tab.
  6. Select the category that best describes your code's purpose.
  1. Click Apply.

articles.html_content:
When you set up your SEO Checklist, you'll be asked to add a location if your business serves customers in a physical location. This will help your site get found locally in search results. 
If the location of your business changes, you can update it in your SEO dashboard.
In this article, learn more about: 
  • Viewing your checklist's location
  • Updating your checklist's location

Viewing your SEO Checklist's location

The location in your SEO Checklist is the one that you entered when you initially set up your checklist.
You can check your location by clicking the Edit details icon  next to your keywords at the top of your checklist. Here, you can also update your location to match the location written on your site.

Updating your SEO Checklist's location

You can update your SEO Checklist's location if you need to change it. For example, if your business location changes and you update it in your site's content, you can update the location in your checklist to match it.

To update your location:

  1. Go to your SEO checklist in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click the Edit details icon  next to Keywords.
  3. (Optional) Select I serve customers from a physical address or within a local service area if you didn't select this when you created your checklist.
  4. Enter your location as it is in your site's content under Location.
  1. Click Save. 
Note:
If you don't have a local business, if your business operates internationally, or you don't want it to be associated with a specific location, you can delete the location in your SEO Checklist's settings. This will stop your checklist from prompting you to add a location. 
Tip:
Check out these 5 SEO tips for beginners in the Wix Blog.

articles.title: Email Marketing: Understanding Your Monthly Balance
articles.html_content:
Your email marketing balance shows the number of emails you can send to recipients each month. You can send an unlimited amount of email marketing campaigns as long as you remain within your email limit. You can send 200 emails a month for free, or upgrade your plan to send more emails.
In this article, learn more about:
  • Actions that impact your balance
  • Checking your monthly balance
  • Upgrading your email marketing balance
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
Note:
Email marketing plans are separate from Wix's Premium plans.  Premium plans enhance your site's capabilities, while an email marketing plan enables you to use advanced email features to boost sales.

Actions that impact your monthly balance

Your balance is impacted every time you send or schedule an email, including automated emails.

Actions that impact your monthly balance:

  • Email marketing campaigns (including sent, scheduled or resent)
  • Email sent using Wix Automations
  • Scheduling an email campaign: If you schedule a campaign to be sent to 50 contacts in one week, those 50 emails are automatically deducted from your quota.

Actions that do not impact your monthly balance:

  • Sending a test email: You can send yourself a test email or campaign and see how it looks to subscribers.
  • Transactional emails: Order confirmation, shipping confirmation, password reset, and other transactional emails do not impact your monthly balance.
  • Sharing a campaign that has already been published 
When a quota is reached:
  1. No new email marketing campaigns can be sent.
  2. Automations continue being sent and are not blocked.

Checking your monthly balance

You can check how many emails you've sent in the current month from your email marketing dashboard. You can also see the date your balance resets. If you've used up your limit for the month you can either wait until the balance resets or upgrade your plan.

To check your monthly balance:

  1. Go to Email Marketing in your site's dashboard.
  2. Under Monthly balance you can view your current balance as well as a progress bar that shows how close you are to the limit.

Upgrading your email marketing balance

To send more emails per month, upgrade your email marketing plan and choose the package that works for your business.
Want to compare plans before upgrading?
Compare the different email marketing plans to see which is right for your business.

To upgrade your email marketing balance:

  1. Go to Email Marketing in your site's dashboard.
  2. Under Monthly Balance click Upgrade to Send More.
  3. Select an email marketing plan and checkout.

FAQs

Click a question below to learn more about your email marketing monthly balance. 

When does my balance reset?

The date your balance and email quota resets is determined by your plan.
  • Free email marketing plans: The quota resets on the first day of each month at 00:01 UTC for all time zones.
  • Premium email marketing plans: The quota resets at the same date and time you purchased the plan. For example, if you upgraded your plan on January 5th at 8:15 UTC, your balance renews on February 5th at 8:15 UTC.

What happens if I try to send an email when my quota is reached?

If you try to send an email once your quota is reached, no new email marketing campaigns will be sent. However, automations will continue to be sent and are not stopped.

question: How do I create my first online program using ADI?
answer:
Prerequisites: Ensure that you have added Online Programs to your site as described in Step 1.

To create your first online program, follow these steps:

1. Go to [Online Programs](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Manage%20Online%20Programs&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/challenges/list) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **+ Create New** at the top right.
3. Pick a program template with pre-filled content or click **Start Fresh** to create a program from scratch.
4. Fill in your online program's basic information as well as its pacing, timing, and duration. [Learn more](https://support.wix.com/en/article/online-programs-creating-a-new-program) about how to create a program.
5. Click **Continue.**
6. Add content to your program such as sections and steps. [Learn More](https://support.wix.com/en/article/online-programs-adding-sections-and-steps-to-your-program)
7. When you're finished adding content, click **Publish** to publish your program and make it possible for participants to join.

**Tip:** You can also get to Online Programs in your dashboard by selecting the Online Programs element in the ADI Builder and clicking **Manage**.

articles.title: ADI: Adding and Setting Up Online Programs
articles.html_content:
Build online programs to inspire your members to achieve a particular goal. Create a scheduled program with a fixed start and end date, or set up a self-paced program for participants to complete at their own pace. Make your program public for anyone to join, private pending your approval, or create a secret program accessible only via invite link.

Step 1 | Add Online Programs to your site

When you add Online Programs to your ADI site it installs two separate pages: the main Programs list page as well as an individual Program Page for each one of your programs.

Show me how

  1. Click Add on the top bar inside ADI.
  2. Click Apps.
  3. Hover over Online Programs and click Add.
Note:
When you install Online Programs, Members Area and Pricing Plans are also installed if you do not have the apps on your site.

Step 2 | Create Your First Online Program

Head over to Online Programs in your site's dashboard to create your first program. We recommend creating an online program before customizing the page in the ADI Builder, so you can better visualize how the settings work with content.

Show me how

  1. Go to Online Programs in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click + Create New at the top right.
  3. Pick a program template with pre-filled content or click Start Fresh to create a program from scratch.
  4. Fill in your online program's basic information as well as its pacing, timing and duration. Learn more about how to create a program.
  5. Click Continue. 
  6. Add content to your program such as sections and steps. Learn More
  7. When you're finished adding content, click Publish to publish your program and make it possible for participants to join.
Tip:
You can also get to Online Programs in your dashboard by selecting the Online Programs element in the ADI Builder and clicking Manage.

Step 3 | Set Up Your Program List Page

The Program List page is where both site visitors and current participants can see a list of all your active programs. You can change what program details to display in the Program list settings.

Show me how

  1. Click the Pages drop-down in the top bar inside ADI.
  2. Click Programs. 
  3. Hover over the Program list in the ADI builder and click the Show more  icon.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Choose what details to display in your Program list by clicking the Show/hide   icon next to the element:
    Note: The changes affect all programs in your Program list.
    • Image: The thumbnail above the program name. 
    • Duration: How long the program runs for.
    • Participants: How many people are enrolled in the program.
    • Price: The price of the program.
  6. Edit the button text that encourages site visitors to join your program.

Note: To create a new program or update a program's content, click Manage Programs at the bottom.

Step 4 | Set Up Your Program Page

Every program gets its own page with information, steps, and a button to join. Depending on if a site visitor or an active program participant is looking at the page, you can change the settings to display the most relevant information for the viewer. 
Note:
The settings you choose for your Program Page affect every program.

Show me how

  1. Click the Pages drop-down in the top bar inside ADI.
  2. Click Program Page under Programs.
  3. Hover over the Programs Page element in the ADI builder and click the Show more  icon.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Choose what details to display in the Visitor view of your Program Page by clicking the Show/hide icon  next to each element. The Visitor view is how the Program Page looks to people who are not enrolled in the program.
    Note: Select or deselect a checkmark to see how the page looks in both views.
    • Date: The program's start date.
    • Image: The Program Page's central image.
    • Duration: How long the program is running for.
    • Steps: The number of steps in the program.
    • Participants: The number of participants in the program.
  6. Choose what details to display in the Participant view of your program page by clicking the Show/hide icon  next to each element. The Participant view is how the program page looks to people who are currently enrolled in the program.
    • Duration: How long the program is running for.
    • Steps: The number of steps in the program.
    • Participants: The number of participants in the program.

question: How can I add Session Recordings to my Wix site?
answer:
To add Session Recordings to your Wix site, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Analytics](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?title=Select%20a%20Site&buttonText=Analytics%20Highlights&actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fmanage.wix.com%2Fdashboard%2F%7B%7BmetaSiteId%7D%7D%2Fanalytics/highlights) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **Session Recordings** on the left.
3. Click **Get Session Recordings**. **Note:** If you already have the Twipla app installed from the Wix App Market, click **Enable Session Recordings**.
4. Click **Agree & Add** in the window.
5. Choose a data privacy mode:
   * [**Light Privacy**](https://www.twipla.com/en/support/all-about-features/privacy-center#c98820): Offers minimal visitor anonymity, displaying all visitor information and site data insights.
   * [**Medium Privacy**](https://www.twipla.com/en/support/all-about-features/privacy-center#c98822): Offers medium visitor anonymity, displaying all site data insights except for visitors' IP addresses.
   * [**GDPR Privacy**](https://www.twipla.com/en/support/all-about-features/privacy-center#c98823): Offers high visitor anonymity and reduced site data insights.
   * [**Maximum Privacy**](https://www.twipla.com/en/support/all-about-features/privacy-center#c98824): Offers the highest visitor anonymity and disables most site data insights.
6. Click **Choose and Continue**.
7. Click **Select** under the plan you would like to purchase:
   * **Pro Plus:** 10,000 new monthly session recordings.
   * **Pro:** 2,000 new monthly session recordings.
   * **Basic:** 500 new monthly session recordings.
   * **Free:** 10 new monthly session recordings. 
   
   **Tip:** Choosing this plan does not require payment, which means you can skip steps 8-10.
8. Select a billing cycle (yearly or monthly) and click **Continue to Checkout**.
9. Enter your payment details and click **Submit Purchase**.
10. Click **Let's Go**.

 Click Get Session Recordings.

Choose if to record all pages or record only specific pages:
        
Record All Pages: Capture sessions for every visitor navigating any page on your site. Record Only Specific Pages: Only visits to your defined pages within your site will be recorded.   Sessions to Record: Choose between recording All Sessions or Only Sessions With Activity. Only Record Sessions With a Minimum Duration: Define the minimum session length, so you can avoid recording short sessions. Click the toggle to enable it and enter the duration (in seconds) in the Recording Duration Limit field. Click Save Changes.Tip:Click Reset All Settings at the bottom to reset any changes you made.Customizing your privacy settingsCustomize your privacy settings to control how much visitor information your site collects and displays. Light Privacy: Offers minimal visitor anonymity, displaying all visitor information and site data insights. Learn more about the Session Recordings page. Manage your recordings: Manage your recordings in the Actions column. For example, mark a recording as unwatched or delete a recording. Analyze a recording: Select a recording to open the detail page to watch it, review its details (e.g. visitor type, device), and analyze the visitor's actions on your site. articles.title: Wix Analytics: Adding and Setting Up Session Recordings
articles.html_content:
Record and review real visitor sessions on your site using Session Recordings in Wix Analytics. By understanding exactly how visitors interact with your site, you can identify areas for improvement and enhance the user experience.
Focus on the use-cases that interest you the most by defining which sessions to record, filter, and analyze. For example, if you notice that visitors frequently abandon their carts on a specific page, you can review their session recordings to pinpoint the issue.
Important:
You must upgrade your site to add Session Recordings.

Adding Session Recordings to your site

Go to your site's dashboard to add Session Recordings. Choose a data privacy mode and a plan according to the number of sessions you want to record each month.

To add Session Recordings:

  1. Go to Analytics in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Session Recordings on the left.
  3. Click Get Session Recordings.
    Note:     If you already have the Twipla app installed from the Wix App Market, click Enable Session Recordings.
  4. Click Agree & Add in the window.
  5. Choose a data privacy mode:
    Note: You can always change this setting later.
    • Light Privacy: Offers minimal visitor anonymity, displaying all visitor information and site data insights.
    • Medium Privacy: Offers medium visitor anonymity, displaying all site data insights except for visitors' IP addresses.
    • GDPR Privacy: Offers high visitor anonymity and reduced site data insights.
    • Maximum Privacy: Offers the highest visitor anonymity and disables most site data insights.
  6. Click Choose and Continue.
  7. Click Select under the plan you would like to purchase:
    • Pro Plus: 10,000 new monthly session recordings.
    • Pro: 2,000 new monthly session recordings.
    • Basic: 500 new monthly session recordings.
    • Free: 10 new monthly session recordings.
      Tip: Choosing this plan does not require payment, which means you can skip steps 8-10.
  8. Select a billing cycle (yearly or monthly) and click Continue to Checkout.
  9. Enter your payment details and click Submit Purchase.
  10. Click Let's Go.

Configuring your recording settings

Define the conditions for which visitor sessions should be recorded. This way you only receive relevant recordings and collect the data you need.

To configure your settings:

  1. Go to Analytics in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Session Recordings on the left.
  3. Click the General Settings tab.
  4. Configure your settings using the following options:
    • Choose if to record all pages or record only specific pages:
      • Record All Pages: Capture sessions for every visitor navigating any page on your site.
      • Record Only Specific Pages: Only visits to your defined pages within your site will be recorded.
    • Sessions to Record: Choose between recording All Sessions or Only Sessions With Activity.
    • Only Record Sessions With a Minimum Duration: Define the minimum session length, so you can avoid recording short sessions. Click the toggle to enable it and enter the duration (in seconds) in the Recording Duration Limit field.
    • Obscure All Text: Enable the toggle to obscure all text elements in a recording to enhance privacy and data security.
  5. Click Save Changes.
Tip:
Click Reset All Settings at the bottom to reset any changes you made.

Customizing your privacy settings

Customize your privacy settings to control how much visitor information your site collects and displays. On this page you can adjust your data privacy mode, set country-specific preferences, and review legal documents.

To customize your privacy settings:

  1. Go to Analytics in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Session Recordings on the left.
  3. Click the Privacy Center tab at the top.
  4. Choose what to do:

Select a data privacy mode

Change your data privacy mode to collect the information you need from site visitors.
Note: Make sure you are familiar with your country or region's data privacy regulations to accurately tailor your privacy preferences.
  • Light Privacy: Offers minimal visitor anonymity, displaying all visitor information and site data insights.
  • Medium Privacy: Offers medium visitor anonymity, displaying all site data insights except for visitors' IP addresses.
  • GDPR Privacy: Offers high visitor anonymity and reduced site data insights.
  • Maximum Privacy: Offers the highest visitor anonymity and disables most site data insights.

Tip: Click the drop-down below each level to learn what it includes and what site visitor information is collected. The higher the level of privacy, the less information about your site visitors will be provided.

Change a country status

Customize your privacy preferences by country. Learn more about changing a country status.

Note: You must upgrade your Twipla plan to use this feature.

Review legal documents

Access Twipla's Terms of Use and Data Processing Agreement by clicking View File next to the relevant file.

Note: This is relevant if you are subject to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
Learn more about Twipla's legal documents.

Managing your session recordings

Managing your recordings helps you efficiently organize and utilize the session data collected from your site visitors. You can view and manage all your session recordings on this page, and then start analyzing each recording to collect insights.

To manage your session recordings:

  1. Go to Analytics in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Session Recordings on the left.
  3. Choose what to do:
    • View your recordings: See all your visitors' session recordings and information on each. Find the recordings you need by changing the date range, adding filters, switching the view, and more. Learn more about the Session Recordings page.
    • Manage your recordings: Manage your recordings in the Actions column. For example, mark a recording as unwatched or delete a recording.
    • Analyze a recording: Select a recording to open the detail page to watch it, review its details (e.g. visitor type, device), and analyze the visitor's actions on your site. This is where you can identify how to improve your site, based on scrolling, mouse clicks, and more.

FAQs

Click a question below to learn more about session recordings.

How can I see how many recordings I have left?

You can see how many monthly recordings you have left at the top right of the Session Recordings page. Once you reach your monthly limit, it will stop recording sessions.

How long are recordings saved for?

Recorded sessions are saved for up to 36 months.

I'm already using the Twipla app. Do I still need to purchase a plan?

Yes. Session Recordings is a separate app, so even if you are already using the Twipla app that you installed from the Wix App Market, you still need to select a plan to access the Session Recordings page.

Why is the number of recordings I have different than the number of sessions on my site?

This may be due to several reasons:
  • Site visitors may refuse to record their sessions due to privacy concerns, usage of private browsers, or refusal to consent to cookies.
  • You may have reached your limit of session recordings. To record more, upgrade your Twipla plan.
  • If you chose a time frame (e.g. the last 90 days) and installed Session Recordings sometime during this period, you only see recordings from that point onwards.

I'm having issues with Session Recordings.

To troubleshoot any issues you're having with Session Recordings, please contact Twipla's support at support@twipla.com or by clicking the blue button at the bottom right corner of the Session Recordings page.

question: How do I set up a referral program on my Wix site?
answer:
Prerequisites:

- You must have one of the following plans: Wix Editor (Business or higher plan) or Wix Studio (Plus or higher plan).
- You need at least one of these apps: Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, Wix Events, Wix Pricing Plans, or the new Wix Restaurants ordering app.

To set up a referral program on your Wix site, follow these steps:

### Step 1 | Create your referral program: Dashboard
1. [Go to Referral Program](https://www.wix.com/my-account/site-selector/?buttonText=Open%20Referral%20Program&title=Select%20a%20Site&autoSelectOnSingleSite=true&actionUrl=https://www.wix.com/dashboard/{{metaSiteId}}/referrals/) in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **Set Up Program**.
3. Provide basic info about your program in the **Program details** section:
   - **Program name:** Enter your referral program name. (Note: This is for internal use only and does not appear on your site.)
   - **Reward trigger:** Click the drop-down and choose the action that will trigger a reward for the referring customer:
     - **Store order placed**
     - **Ticket ordered**
     - **Session booked**
     - **Plan ordered**

### Step 2 | Set your program rewards: Dashboard
1. Scroll down to the **Referring customer reward** section and select an option from the drop-down:
   - **Coupon:** Customize your coupon by selecting the type, reward name, what it can be used for, and the discount.
   - **Loyalty points:** Enter the number of loyalty points in the **Points given** field.
   - **No reward:** Choose not to reward the referring customer.
2. Scroll down to the **Referred friend reward** section and choose how to reward a referred friend:
   - **Coupon:** Customize your coupon similarly to the referring customer reward.
   - **Loyalty points:** Enter the number of loyalty points in the **Points given** field.
   - **No reward:** Choose not to reward the referred friend.

### Step 3 | Decide whether to activate automated emails: Dashboard
1. Scroll down to the **Emails** section. If you chose to offer rewards, you'll see automated emails for each reward type.
2. Click the toggle next to the email notifications you want to enable or disable:
   - **Enabled:** Customers will automatically receive an email.
   - **Disabled:** Customers will not automatically receive an email.

### Step 4 | Review your referral program: Dashboard
Use the **Program preview** on the right to get an idea of how the program will look on your site. When you're happy with your program setup, click **Save**.

### Step 5 | View your new site pages
When you add a referral program to your site, 2 new site pages are automatically generated. Go to [your editor](https://manage.wix.com/account/site-selector/?actionUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wix.com%2Feditor%2F%7BmetaSiteId%7D%3FeditorSessionId%3D%7Besi%7D%26) to see and [customize the Referral Program pages](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-referral-program-customizing-your-referral-program-pages).

articles.html_content:
Add Wix Referral Program to your site to allow your members to refer friends to your business by sharing referral URLs. You have the option to reward both the customer doing the referring and the friend being referred.
To launch your referral program, you need to set it up, add the relevant pages and publish your site. Once launched, the program runs automatically with no need for you to manage any aspect manually, unless you'd like to make changes to the way it works.
To add a referral program, you must have:
  • One of the following plans:
    • Wix Editor: A Business or higher plan
    • Wix Studio: A Plus or higher plan
  • At least one of these apps: Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, Wix Events, Wix Pricing Plans or the new Wix Restaurants ordering app.

Step 1 | Create your referral program

Give your referral program a name, and confirm the action a referred friend needs to take to trigger a reward for the referring customer.

To create your referral program:

Dashboard
Wix app
  1. Go to Referral Program in your site's dashboard.
  2. Click Set Up Program.
  3. Provide basic info about your program in the Program details section:
    • Program name: Enter your referral program name.
      Note: Your program name is for internal use only and does not appear on your site.
    • Reward trigger: Click the drop-down and choose the action that will trigger a reward for the referring customer:
      • Store order placed: When the referred friend places a store order, the referring customer will be rewarded. 
      • Ticket ordered: When the referred friend purchases an event ticket, the referring customer will be rewarded.
      • Session booked: When the referred friend books a session, the referring customer will be rewarded.
      • Plan ordered: When the referred friend orders a pricing plan, the referring customer will be rewarded.
      • Restaurant order placed: When the referred friend places a restaurant order, the referring customer will be rewarded.

  2. Tap Manage  at the bottom.
  3. Tap Referral Program under Customers & Leads.
  4. Tap Create Program.
  5. Provide basic info about your program in the Program details section:
    • Program name: Enter your referral program name.
      Note: Your program name is for internal use only and does not appear on your site.
    • Reward trigger: Tap the drop-down and choose the action that will trigger a reward for the referring customer:
      • Store order placed: When the referred friend places a store order, the referring customer will be rewarded. 
      • Ticket ordered: When the referred friend purchases an event ticket, the referring customer will be rewarded.
      • Session booked: When the referred friend books a session, the referring customer will be rewarded.
      • Plan ordered: When the referred friend orders a pricing plan, the referring customer will be rewarded.
      • Restaurant order placed: When the referred friend places a restaurant order, the referring customer will be rewarded.
Note:
You might see your reward trigger is pre-selected and can't be changed. This happens if your site has only one app that the referral program can be based on (Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, Wix Events, Wix Pricing Plans, or the new Wix Restaurants online ordering app).

Step 2 | Set your program rewards

Choose if and how you’d like to reward those participating in your program.

A referring customer is rewarded when a referred friend signs up as a site member and takes the action on your site that is set as your reward trigger (e.g. places an order, books a session). A referred friend is rewarded when they click the referral URL they receive and sign in or sign up to your site. 
Notes:
  • Any reward coupons you issue are for single use (unique coupon codes that can only be used once by the recipient). 
  • You can only issue loyalty points as a reward if you've added a loyalty program to your site.

To set your program rewards:

Dashboard
Wix app
  1. Scroll down to the Referring customer reward section and select an option from the drop-down: 
    • Coupon: When the trigger you set in step 1 is actioned by a referred friend, your referring customer is rewarded with a coupon. Customize your coupon:
      1. Type of coupon: Select Discount (%), Discount ($) or Free shipping.
      2. Reward name: Enter the reward name that will appear on your site.
      3. Apply to: Choose what the coupon can be used for. 
      4. Discount: (Discount coupons only) Enter the percentage or monetary discount the coupon will offer.
      5. Include subscriptions: Allow the reward to apply to both one-time purchases and for every recurring purchase. 
    • Loyalty points: When the trigger you set in step 1 is actioned by a referred friend, your referring customer is rewarded with loyalty points. Enter the number of loyalty points in the Points given field.
    • No reward: Your referring customer is not rewarded when the trigger you set in step 1 is actioned by a referred friend.
  2. Scroll down to the Referred friend reward section and choose how to reward a referred friend:
    • Coupon: When a referred friend clicks a referral URL and signs in or signs up to your site, this referred friend is rewarded with a coupon. Customize your coupon:
      1. Type of coupon: Select Discount (%), Discount ($) or Free shipping.
      2. Reward name: Enter the reward name that will appear on your site.
      3. Apply to: Choose what the coupon can be used for. 
      4. Discount: (Discount coupons only) Enter the percentage or monetary discount the coupon will offer.
      5. Include subscriptions: Allow the reward to apply to both one-time purchases and for every recurring purchase.
    • Loyalty points: When a referred friend clicks a referral URL and signs in or signs up to your site, this referred friend is rewarded with loyalty points. Enter the number of loyalty points in the Points given field.
    • No reward: When a referred friend clicks a referral URL and signs in or signs up to your site, this referred friend is not rewarded.
  1. Scroll down to Referring customer reward and choose how to reward your customer: 
    • Coupon: When the trigger you set in step 1 is actioned by a referred friend, your referring customer is rewarded with a coupon. Customize your coupon:
      1. Reward Type: Select Discount (%), Discount ($) or Free shipping.
      2. Reward name: Enter the reward name that will appear on your site.
      3. Apply to: Choose what the coupon can be used for. 
      4. Discount: (Discount coupons only) Enter the percentage or monetary discount the coupon will offer.
    • Loyalty points: When the trigger you set in step 1 is actioned by a referred friend, your referring customer is rewarded with loyalty points. Enter the number of loyalty points in the Number of points given field.
    • No reward: Your referring customer is not rewarded when the trigger you set in step 1 is actioned by a referred friend.
  2. Scroll down to Referred friend reward and choose how to reward a referred friend:
    • Coupon: When a referred friend clicks a referral URL and signs in or signs up to your site, this referred friend is rewarded with a coupon. Customize your coupon:
      1. Reward Type: Select Discount (%), Discount ($) or Free shipping.
      2. Reward name: Enter the reward name that will appear on your site.
      3. Apply to: Choose what the coupon can be used for. 
      4. Discount: (Discount coupons only) Enter the percentage or monetary discount the coupon will offer.
    • Loyalty points: When a referred friend clicks a referral URL and signs in or signs up to your site, this referred friend is rewarded with loyalty points. Enter the number of loyalty points in the Number of points given field.
    • No reward: When a referred friend clicks a referral URL and signs in or signs up to your site, they are not rewarded.
Note:
The option to include subscriptions when choosing rewarding customers and friends is only available on desktop (in your site's dashboard).

Step 3 | Decide whether to activate automated emails

You can enable or disable two types of automated emails:
  1. Emails sent to all customers making a store, event, booking, pricing plan, or order purchase, sharing details of your referral program.
  1. Emails notifying customers of new referral rewards they've received.

To enable or disable email automations:

Dashboard
Wix app
  1. Scroll down to the Emails section. If you chose to offer rewards to referring customers or referred friends, you'll see automated emails for each reward type. 
  2. Click the toggle next to the email notifications you want to enable or disable: 
    • Enabled: Customers will automatically receive an email.
    • Disabled: Customers will not automatically receive an email.
Notes:
  • The automated emails that you see listed here will differ depending on the apps you've installed. Enabling an automation will mean this email is sent once per site member.
  • If you selected No reward for Referring customer reward in step 2, you will not be able to enable the Notify customers about their referral reward automation.
  • Click Edit next to any automation to review and edit the way it's set up within Wix Automations.

    • Disabled: Customers will not automatically receive an email.
Notes:
  • The automated emails that you see listed will differ based on the apps you've installed. Enabling an automation means this email is sent once per site member.
  • If you selected No reward for Referring customer reward in step 2, you will not be able to enable the Notify customers about their referral reward automation.

Step 4 | Review your referral program

After filling in the details of your new referral program, it's time to take one last look before launching it. 
Dashboard
Wix app
Use the Program preview on the right to get an idea of how the program will look on your site. When you're happy with your program setup, click Save.
Scroll up and down the page to review the details of your referral program before launching it. When you're happy with your program setup, tap Save at the top right.

Step 5 | View your new site pages

When you add a referral program to your site, two new site pages are automatically generated. Your "Refer Friends" page shares details of your referral program with site visitors; your "Referral Landing Page" is the page referred friends see when they click a referral link.
Go to your editor to see and customize the Referral Program pages. If you've set up your program from your site's dashboard, you can click Go to Editor at the top of the screen.
Notes:
  • These new pages won't be live and accessible to visitors until you publish your site.
  • If you haven't added Wix Loyalty Program to your site, a third page will also be added: My Rewards. Your My Rewards page is where site members keep track of their points and rewards.

question: How can I use my free 1-year domain voucher with Wix?
answer:
To use your free 1-year domain voucher with Wix, follow these steps:

1. [Go to Domains](https://manage.wix.com/account/domains) in your Wix account.
2. Click **Buy a Domain**.
3. Type the domain you'd like to claim, including the domain extensions (e.g. .com) and click **Search**.
4. Click **Get It** if the domain is available. 
   
   **Tip:** If your domain is not available, you can claim one of the recommended alternatives or try searching for a different domain.
5. Choose a registration period and click **Continue**. 
   
   **Note:** Make sure the domain voucher is applied in the summary section at this point.
6. Enter (or edit) your contact information and click **Continue**.
7. Select a privacy option: 
   
   * **Full privacy protection:** Your contact details won't appear in the WHOIS domain information records. The voucher does not cover the cost of Private Registration.
   * **Basic Protection:** Some personal information will be public, but your name, address, phone number, and email will be kept private. If someone wishes to contact you, they are redirected to a contact form that protects you from receiving spam. articles.title: Using Your Free 1 Year Domain Voucher
articles.html_content:
You receive the 1 year free domain voucher with the initial purchase of selected yearly or multi-year Premium or Studio site plans. This voucher enables you to register a domain for free for one year. You can renew the domain the following year for the regular price. 

In this article, learn more about:
  • Using your voucher
  • Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

Using your voucher

Your voucher must be redeemed within 2 months of purchasing your plan. You can check the expiration date of your voucher in the Premium Vouchers section of your account.
You will need to enter your payment information when claiming your voucher, but you won't be charged. This allows us to process your renewal after the first year to make sure your domain stays live.

To use your voucher:

  1. Go to Domains in your Wix account.
  2. Click Buy a Domain or Get a New Domain.
  3. Type the domain you'd like to claim, including the domain extensions (e.g. .com) and click Search.
  4. Click Get It if the domain is available.
    Tip: if your domain is not available, you can claim one of the recommended alternatives or try searching for a different domain. 
  5. Choose a registration period and click Continue.
    Note: Make sure the domain voucher is applied in the summary section at this point.
  1. Enter (or edit) your contact information and click Continue.
  2. Select a privacy option: 
    • Full privacy protection: Your contact details won't appear in the WHOIS domain information records. The voucher does not cover the cost of Private Registration.
    • Basic Protection: Some personal information will be public, but your name, address, phone number and email will be kept private. If someone wishes to contact you, they are redirected to a contact form that protects you from receiving spam. You can only change this option to full privacy protection when manually extending a domain subscription.
  3. Click Continue.
  4. Select your payment method.
    Note: You'll see the voucher discount applied before submitting your purchase.
  5. Click Submit Purchase.
  6. Assign the domain to your site.

FAQs

Click a question below to learn more about your domain voucher.

What domain extensions can I use my voucher for?

The voucher is valid for the following extensions: 

.art, .at, .be, .biz, .blog, .ca, .ch, .club, .co.at, .co.in, .co.uk, .coach, .com, .com.au, .com.br, .de (Germany only), .firm.in, .fit, .fitness, .fr, .fun, .gen.in, .in, .ind.in, .info, .live, .net, .net.in, .nl, .online, .or.at, .org, .org.in, .pictures, .rocks, .shop, .site, .space, .store, .studio, .training, .work, .xyz, .yoga

Can I apply this voucher to a domain I've already purchased?

No. The free domain voucher is limited to the purchase of new domains only. The free domain voucher cannot be applied retroactively to a domain purchased before you purchased your yearly plan. 

Can I use the voucher to renew a Wix domain?

No, you cannot use the voucher to renew a Wix domain. The free domain voucher is limited to the purchase of new domains only.

Can I apply this voucher to a domain I want to transfer to Wix?

Yes. You can also choose to redeem your voucher when transferring a domain to Wix. 

If you have a valid domain voucher, it is applied automatically when you select the registration extension period for the domain in your Wix account during the transfer process.

Does this voucher include privacy protection?

The free domain voucher does not include privacy protection. However, you can purchase this option for an additional fee.

I'm a collaborator on someone else's site and I need to purchase a domain. Can I apply a voucher?

Yes. Billing Managers can apply a domain voucher on behalf of the site owner. Learn more about domain voucher roles and permissions.
